name: Known From / Logo Bar (press & logo strip with marquee or slider)
status: Built — launched (tested internally, documented in Slite)

what.text: A configurable Shopify section ('Known from') that shows a row of press or partner logos, or round/rounded thumbnails with captions, under an optional heading. With more than 5 items it can scroll automatically as an endless marquee or work as a slider with arrows. With 5 or fewer items, or when the style is set to 'None', it renders as a static centered row. The ticket's landing-page field says PDP, and the section is named 'Global'. The final build (ed-cro-bekannt-aus / ed-logo-bar) is a general logo bar that can also be used for category bubbles.

why.text: Showing recognizable media or partner logos transfers the credibility of known brands to the shop (authority and social-proof heuristic). This lowers first-visit skepticism and perceived risk, which matters most for unknown brands or on product pages where the buyer is deciding. The moving marquee adds visual interest without taking up much space. The same layout also works as visual category navigation.

how.text: Create the section file in the theme (ed-cro-bekannt-aus.liquid, based on ed-logo-bar.liquid) and paste in the code. Add one block per logo or image. Each block has an image, an image style (full image or thumbnail), a thumbnail shape (circle or rounded), an optional caption, and an optional link. Then set the section options in the theme editor: heading, colors, spacing, layout width, and the style above 5 items. Marquee mode repeats the item set 12 times and animates it with a CSS keyframe translate. Slider mode loads Swiper 11 from the jsDelivr CDN (CSS and JS) and initializes it with loop, navigation arrows, optional autoplay, and breakpoints. Static mode is the fallback for 5 or fewer items.

items: Section background color (transparent falls back to the theme background)
Heading text, desktop/mobile heading size and bottom margin
Top and bottom spacing (desktop and mobile)
Style above 5 items: Scroll (marquee) / Slides (slider) / None
Per block: image, image style (image vs thumbnail), thumbnail shape (circle vs rounded), caption text, link URL
Open links in a new tab
Item width and gap (desktop and mobile)
Show dots between items, dot size, dot color
Marquee: animation duration (seconds), pause on hover
Slider: slides per view (desktop and mobile), arrow navigation, autoplay on/off, autoplay delay

dependencies.text: No metafields needed. Shopify Online Store 2.0 theme with sections and blocks. The slider mode relies on the external Swiper 11 library from the jsDelivr CDN, which adds a third-party request and could matter for page speed or CSP. The code relies on theme settings (settings.background, settings.text_color) as color fallbacks. Logo images must be uploaded per block. Documentation lives in Slite.

items: Bounce rate and scroll depth to the section
Click-through rate on linked logos or thumbnails (when used as navigation)
Conversion rate for new vs returning visitors
Page load / LCP impact from the Swiper CDN assets

name: CRO | Rich Text Section (Headline, Subheadline, Text & Button)
status: Built — delivered, documented (ticket still marked In Progress)

what.text: A standalone, reusable Shopify section called "CRO | Rich text" for brand story, USP or quote copy. It combines a headline, a subheadline, a body text block and a CTA button. Colors, fonts, alignment, sizes and the button are all editable. The layout can be stacked (centered, 'Showcase' style, e.g. a brand logo, small caps tagline and large quote) or side by side (headline and button on the left, body text on the right, 'Concept' style). The delivered code also includes an optional image/logo block, text transform, line-height, letter-spacing, mobile-specific overrides, max-width and padding.

why.text: Clear, well-structured brand and value copy builds trust and communicates the USP right where visitors land. Typographic hierarchy (big headline, then subheadline, then body) guides the eye and makes the message scannable. The CTA button after the story turns reading attention into a click. Because every style is editable, CRO teams can test message, tone and CTA wording without developer work.

how.text: Add the section file (ed-cro-rich-text.liquid) to the theme. It uses block types: image, subheading, heading, content and button. Style settings are output as CSS variables scoped to #shopify-section-{{ section.id }}. Color settings fall back to theme colors when transparent (rgba(0,0,0,0)). Custom fonts load via @font-face from the font_picker. The side-by-side layout is a CSS grid (3fr 4fr, 60px gap at 768px+, 120px gap and padding at 1180px+). The stacked layout is the default. Merchants add the section in the theme editor and add and order the blocks. Bold, italic and underline in text are handled via rich text (a highlighted-heading style is also in the CSS). Desktop and mobile visibility classes (cro_richtext-hide-desktop, cro_richtext-hide-mobile) are included. The developer states it works in any Shopify theme.

Headline: text, color, font family, alignment (left/center/right), font size, line height, letter spacing, text transform, spacing, optional max-width, mobile overrides

Button: label, link, background color, text color, shape (rectangular/rounded), alignment (left/center/right, separate for mobile)
Hide on desktop / hide on mobile

name: Sub-Collections (Category Bubble / Title Navigation Strip)
status: Built — launched (v1 tested internally and documented; v1.1 requests from the PL team still open)

what.text: A configurable Shopify section that shows a horizontal strip of category shortcuts (sub-collections). Each item has a title, a link and an image, icon or custom SVG. Two styles are available: 'Show bubbles' (round or square image above a label) and 'Show titles' (outlined, uppercase text boxes with no image). Background colour, text colour, font sizes, image sizes, gaps, alignment and positioning (static, or absolute so it overlays the hero or collection image) are all editable in the theme editor. On mobile the strip scrolls horizontally. With 4 or fewer items the strip is centred. The ticket asks for up to 20 categories.

why.text: Story-style category bubbles give shoppers a fast, visual, one-tap route into the catalogue. This cuts the clicks and decisions needed to reach relevant products, and it exposes the range of categories to people who would not open the main menu. Familiar, thumb-friendly mobile patterns (Instagram-style stories) lower friction and increase category-level engagement, which feeds PDP views and add-to-cart rate.

how.text: 1) Create the section file sections/sub-collections.liquid from the provided code. 2) In the theme editor, add the 'Sub-Collections' section to the template (e.g. under the header or hero). 3) Choose a Style (bubbles or titles), an Image style (circle or square), sizes, colours, gap, alignment and positioning. 4) Add one 'Collection' block per category with a Link and a Title, plus an Image or an SVG (the SVG overrides the image). Blocks without a link are not rendered. 5) For A/B tests, hide the section with the 'Display Section' checkbox and re-enable it for the variant with CSS: .shopify-section-story-icon-slider { display:block !important; }. A comment suggested using overflow-x:auto instead of scroll to avoid a needless scrollbar. The final code already uses auto.

items: Display Section (checkbox; can be force-shown in A/B tests via CSS)
Image size desktop (40–200px, default 80) and mobile (40–200px, default 65)
Text colour (also used for the border colour in the 'titles' style)
Font size desktop and mobile (8–50px, default 14)
Gap between items desktop and mobile (0–100px, default 10)
Positioning: Static / Absolute (overlay on the hero or collection image)
Block 'Collection': Link, Title, Icon image, SVG (HTML; overrides the image)

Requested for v1.1, not in the current code: badges (text, colours, borders), vertical offset when overlaying the hero, an optional desktop headline, more layout styles (e.g. square layouts, NaturesWay style), and highlighting the active category on collection pages with colour options

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps. The code assumes theme-specific elements: a #main wrapper, the CSS variables --menu-height and --border, and the ed-section class. Positioning and styling may need adapting per theme. Category images must be uploaded for each block. The current code has no explicit max_blocks, and Shopify's default block limit applies. The 20-category requirement is from the ticket, not from the schema. Tested in the Sectionify demo theme.

items: Bounce / exit rate on the page where the strip appears
Add-to-cart rate and conversion rate for sessions that click the strip
Mobile scroll depth within the strip (interaction rate)

name: Before vs. After Comparison Slider
status: Built — code delivered, tested by Christoph; product image/doc entry still pending

what.text: A standalone Shopify section ("Before vs. After") with an optional section headline and subheadline above a full-width image comparison slider. Two images are stacked and a draggable vertical handle reveals one or the other. Each image has its own overlay label (small subheading plus bold title) at the bottom corner: the 'before' label sits bottom-right, the 'after' label bottom-left. Reference: the Heyskin before/after slider and the Shopify theme 'Concept'. The screenshot shows it as a headphone color-variant comparison, so the slider also works for product variants, not only before/after results.

why.text: Letting the visitor drag the handle and compare two states themselves makes the product's effect or difference tangible and builds trust in the claimed result. The interaction also increases engagement and time on page. Visual proof of a transformation reduces perceived risk. Comparing variants or colors helps with choice and supports purchase confidence.

how.text: Create the section file ed-before-vs-after.liquid and paste the delivered code. The section is styled via CSS custom properties driven by section settings. Heading and subheading blocks carry their own typography settings. The comparison component stacks a 'before' and 'after' layer; the 'after' layer is clipped with clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0) and a handle button positioned at --compare-percent (default 50%) that is moved by drag (col-resize cursor). Overlay text boxes sit in the bottom corners. The source file is truncated, so the slider JavaScript and schema were not visible and need to be checked in the full file. Add the section via the theme editor on the homepage or any template.

2 images, each with its own overlay text: subheading and heading with font family, size (desktop/mobile) and color

name: Shop the Look (Shoppable Lifestyle Image with Hotspots + Product Carousel)
status: Built — tested, documented (Slite guide), ready for reuse

what.text: A custom Shopify section (file ed-lookbook.liquid, named 'Shop the Look') that shows a large lifestyle image with pulsing white hotspot dots. On desktop, hovering a dot opens a small product card (thumbnail, title, price) next to it. Beside the image is a heading area (subheading plus headline with a hand-drawn highlight underline) and a product carousel. Each carousel card shows a product image, a rating badge, the vendor, the title, the price and variant swatches, plus an Add-to-Cart button that appears on hover. On tablet and mobile the hover popup is hidden and the carousel shows compact product rows with a small ATC link.

why.text: Shoppable lifestyle imagery lets shoppers see products in context, which inspires them and makes it easy to buy the whole look. Hotspots invite exploration, and the pulsing dot draws the eye without cluttering the image. The product details and ATC button sit next to the scene, so the path from inspiration to cart is short. This lifts product discovery, cross-selling and AOV. The rating badge adds light social proof.

how.text: 1) In the theme code, create the section file ed-lookbook.liquid and paste the provided code (the ticket's step-by-step guide is also in Slite). 2) In the theme editor, add the 'Shop the look' section to the page. 3) Upload the lifestyle image as the 'Thumbnail'. 4) Add one 'Heading' block (subheading and headline, optional custom fonts, sizes, letter spacing, text style, gaps and margin). 5) Add one 'Item' block per product and pick the product. Place its hotspot with percentage coordinates (distance from top and from left), so no pixel fiddling is needed. 6) Set colors, layout (Container or Full) and desktop/mobile spacing. The layout is a CSS grid: image on the left (about 2/3), heading and carousel on the right (about 1/3).

items: Section spacing top / bottom / left / right (desktop)
Section spacing top / bottom / left / right (mobile; left/right apply to Full layout only)
Heading block: subheading, headline (with highlight underline), optional custom fonts, sizes (desktop/mobile), letter spacing, text style, gap between items, bottom margin
Item block (one per product): product selection, hotspot position as % from top and % from left

Ticket wishlist (acceptance criteria, not all confirmed in the code): hotspots optional, pulse animation configurable, selectable product elements (title, reviews, price, teaser, variants, ATC button)

Product data comes from standard Shopify products (images, vendor, price, color variants as swatches). The rating badge probably needs a reviews app or metafield, but the source does not say which. The code file is cut off at the end, so the details of the final markup are unverified.

name: Collection Page Spotlight (in-grid banner, video, product and reviews tiles)
status: Built — delivered and tested; theme-specific install docs still being refined

what.text: A 'Spotlight' tile that sits inside the collection product grid at an editable position. It breaks up the grid with a highlighted content tile. The ticket describes four variants: (1) a category banner with headline, sub-headline, optional button and link, (2) a benefits/info banner with text over an image, (3) a highlighted product tile with an optional full-width add-to-cart button, and (4) a reviews tile with a rating summary and a testimonial card. The final code ships as four blocks of the collection products section: Spotlight, Spotlight video, Spotlight product and Spotlight reviews. Video was added beyond the original ticket. Each block has separate desktop and mobile visibility and a grid position.

why.text: Native-looking tiles inside the product grid interrupt scrolling without pulling the shopper off the page. A banner can communicate a category benefit or lead time, and a highlighted bestseller tile gets extra attention. A reviews tile puts social proof right where shoppers compare products, which lowers purchase anxiety. Repeating the tile on every page of results keeps the message visible during long browsing sessions.

how.text: Add the block definitions (spotlight, spotlight_video, spotlight_product, spotlight_reviews) to the 'blocks' array of the schema in the theme's collection products section. Then create the snippet ed-collection-spotlight.liquid and render it inside the product loop whenever the loop index matches a block's 'position' setting. If 'repeat_position' is on, the tile repeats on every page. Merchants then add and configure the blocks in the theme customizer. CSS custom properties are scoped per block ID and set height, padding, border radius, text colour and background overlay. The 'Show at Desktop only' and 'Show at Mobile only' checkboxes hide the tile via media queries at the 1000px breakpoint. 'Full-width at Mobile' makes the tile span both grid columns. The dev notes say the install steps differ by theme: you must first find the correct collection template and section, and a developer is needed. The code supplied in the ticket is truncated, so the rendering loop and the product and reviews snippet markup are not visible.

why.text: Detailed specs answer the technical objections of considered purchases (e.g. electronics) directly on the PDP, so shoppers don't have to leave the page or search elsewhere. The accordion keeps the page scannable and avoids a wall of text. The 'Included in the Box' panel makes the scope of delivery concrete and tangible, which reduces uncertainty about what is actually received and reinforces perceived value.

name: Product Comparison Table (Compare Function)
status: Reference only — ticket closed as duplicate of 'CRO | Global | Konkurrenzvergleich'; references kept in that ticket

what.text: A comparison section that places 2–3 selected products side by side. Each column shows the product image, name with variant, price and a 'View' button. Below them is a table of spec rows (e.g. Driver, Weight, Dimensions, Battery, Ear Pads, Voice Assistant). Unsupported features are marked with an X. In the Impact 'Sound' style, the table is capped at about 5 rows with a 'View all' toggle. In the Concept style, a left column carries an eyebrow ('Compare'), a headline ('Which wireless headphones are made for you?'), a short intro and a 'Learn more' button. The Impact style uses a centered headline, intro and 'Shop Headphones' button above the table.

why.text: Shoppers who are unsure which model fits often leave to compare elsewhere. Putting the comparison on-site cuts the effort of weighing options and lowers choice anxiety. Aligned spec rows make differences and price steps easy to see, which guides people to the right model, or to a higher-priced one when the extra value is visible. Marking missing features with an X makes the trade-offs obvious. The framing question ('Which … is made for you?') adds a light personalization cue.

how.text: Build a theme section with blocks, one block per product (product picker). Spec rows are either defined as row labels in the section with values read from product metafields, or entered manually per block. Render the product image, title (including variant), price and a 'View' button linking to the PDP. Show the first ~5 rows and hide the rest behind a 'View all' toggle (JS expand/collapse). Render an empty or false value as an X icon. Provide a heading area (eyebrow, headline, text, CTA button) with two layouts: left-aligned beside the table (Concept) or centered above it (Impact). Both reference themes already ship a version of this, so their code can be adapted.

name: Testimonials Section (3 Styles: Quote Slider, Card Carousel, Card Grid)
status: Built — tested internally (3 testers), KVA approved, launched

what.text: A reusable Shopify section for showing customer testimonials on any page. It ships as three separate sections, each with its own logic: (1) 'Testimonials': a centered, large-quote slider with a star rating, author name and dots/arrows. (2) 'Testimonials two': a horizontally scrolling card carousel with a headline, prev/next arrows, a product/review image, name with 'Verified Buyer', stars, review text and a linked product row. (3) 'Testimonials three': a card layout of image, name, stars, text and product link, which stacks on mobile. The original ticket also asks for a headline, sub-headline, CTA button, an optional badge ('300,000 customers love Doonails') and video-thumbnail testimonials with a play icon (up to 15). Those video/badge items are not visible in any final screenshot.

why.text: Real customer voices are one of the strongest social-proof signals. Star ratings and 'Verified Buyer' labels add credibility, which lowers purchase risk. Names, photos and real quotes make the proof concrete and relatable. Showing the purchased product beside each review links the proof to a product and gives a quick path to it. A badge with a large customer count (e.g. '300,000 customers') adds bandwagon proof, and video testimonials add authenticity.

how.text: Create the section files in the theme (Impact base). Style 1 is a Flickity carousel with fade, wrap-around and adaptive height, plus a shared snippet 'ed-flickity-control' for dots and optional prev/next arrows. Each testimonial is a block with rating (1–5), text and author. Stars are rendered by looping filled and empty 'rating-star' icons up to 5. A decorative quote mark is drawn with a CSS mask, and the mobile layout shrinks the quote mark and stars. The background colour is injected via a section-scoped style. Styles 2 and 3 follow the Sleek-style card design (image, name + Verified Buyer, stars, text, product row) and were built as separate sections ('Testimonials two' and 'Testimonials three'); their code is not in the file provided. After internal testing, mobile fixes were made: tighter spacing, wider cards so the next card peeks, a larger gap between title and cards, stars that follow the rating, and a stack of a single card.

name: CRO | Image with Text
status: Built — launched (Concept-style variant delivered; Impact-style slider split into a separate ticket 'CRO | Multi-image with slides')

what.text: A reusable, fully configurable two-column 'image with text' Shopify section. A thumbnail image sits on one side. The other side holds a content panel built from blocks: icon, subheading, heading, body text and button. On desktop the layout is side by side; on mobile it stacks. It can be placed on any page via the theme editor. It matches the 'Concept' theme reference: large rounded image on the left, light content card on the right with an icon, a bold heading and a paragraph.

why.text: Pairing a strong visual with a short, scannable block of copy communicates a brand story, product benefit or USP faster than text alone. The icon plus bold heading gives a quick visual hierarchy, and a clear button gives the user a next step. Because every typography, spacing and colour setting is editable, the section can be restyled per test without developer work, so A/B variants of messaging and layout are cheap to ship.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-image-with-text.liquid, paste the supplied code, and add it to the theme. Colours, spacing, widths and fonts are exposed as CSS variables driven by section and block settings. Blocks available: Thumbnail (image), Icon, Subheading, Heading, Content (text) and Button. Add the section in the theme editor, then add and reorder blocks. Set section width (Container/Full), max-width, corner radius, text alignment, content position (top/center/bottom), text and background colours, and the content-panel background. Spacing is set per side, with separate mobile values. Each text block has its own font, size, line height, letter spacing, spacing, transform and colour. Desktop switches to a row layout at 1000px and above. The content panel width is controlled by a percentage setting, and the thumbnail can have a custom height per breakpoint.

items: Text alignment (left/center/right), with separate mobile alignment
Content position vertical: Top / Center / Bottom
Text colour, section background and content background (transparent falls back to the theme colours)
Content panel width as a percentage of the section
Thumbnail block: image, image position (row/column direction), border radius, custom height per mobile/tablet/desktop
Icon block: image alignment, custom max-width, spacing top/bottom (mobile too)
Subheading, Heading and Content blocks: custom font family, size, line height, letter spacing, text transform, colour, spacing and custom max-width with alignment (mobile sizes too)
Button block: text, link, button text colour, button background colour, text transform
Original spec also requested bold toggle, round-to-square button style, background image/opacity and section height (Auto/Full/75%). These are only partly evidenced in the delivered code.

dependencies.text: Needs a Shopify OS 2.0 theme with section blocks and theme colour settings (settings.heading_color, settings.text_color, settings.background) plus existing .button--primary and .button--secondary classes. Built and tested on a Focal-based theme. The code uses theme global styles. Images and icons are uploaded per section. The Impact-style slider with thumbnails is NOT part of this element; it lives in the separate 'CRO | Multi-image with slides' section. The supplied code was truncated at the image border-radius rule, and the corner radius bug was reported fixed in a later code update.

name: FAQ Accordion Section with Support Intro Block (Variant 1)
status: Built — delivered, documented (Variant 1 = Impact-style layout; tabbed category variant split into a separate ticket)

what.text: A reusable Shopify section 'CRO | FAQ Section' with a two-column card. The left column is an optional intro block (max 1) with a heading, a subline, a row of 4 support-team avatars with a green 'online' dot, and a support availability line (e.g. 'Available Mon–Fri 8am–8:30pm. Average answer time: 24h'). The right column is a grey rounded box holding an accordion of FAQ blocks. Each block is one question with a round chevron toggle and a rich-text answer. On mobile the columns stack and the availability/avatar block moves below the accordion.

why.text: Answering common objections (shipping, returns, account, gift wrapping) right where the buyer hesitates lowers perceived risk and reduces support load. The human avatars, the 'online' dot and the stated response time make support feel approachable and reliable, which builds trust. The accordion keeps the page compact while the answers stay one click away.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-faq-section.liquid and paste in the supplied code (CSS, markup, vanilla JS, schema). The section has two block types: 'intro' (max 1: heading, heading size, content, 4 avatar images, active-status color, footer title, footer content) and 'faq' (question, rich-text answer, open-by-default checkbox). Colors and radii are exposed as CSS variables set from the section settings. The accordion is a custom <ed-collapsible> structure with a button toggle, aria-controls/aria-expanded, and Web Animations API open/close (500ms). A 'multiple open at once' checkbox controls the single-open behavior. Add the section in the theme editor, add one Intro block and as many FAQ blocks as needed. The code was built against the Impact theme.

name: PDP Up-/Cross-Selling (Add-on Product Slider/Stack)
status: Built — code delivered (Shopify theme block); setup guide still being simplified for non-developers

what.text: A compact up-/cross-sell module on the product page, placed directly under the Add-to-Cart area. It shows a merchant-curated list of related products (e.g. 'Buy it with', 'Pairs well with', 'You may also like'). Each row has a small product image, the product name (plus variant title if any), the price (with a struck-through compare-at price if one exists) and a compact '+ Add' button that adds that product to the cart without leaving the PDP. Three layouts are in the code: a 'Slides' carousel with prev/next arrows, a collapsible 'Stack' accordion, and a 'Normal' always-open list.

why.text: Shoppers who have already decided to buy are at their most receptive to a low-friction add-on. Showing a relevant, inexpensive complementary product right next to the main CTA, with a one-click add and no page change, raises AOV through impulse and complementarity ('goes well with'). The compact format avoids distracting from the main purchase, while a visible price keeps the decision easy.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet snippets/ed-cro-cross-selling.liquid and paste the delivered code. 2) Add a new block definition ('CRO | Up/Cross-Selling') to the product section schema (e.g. main-product.liquid). 3) Render the block in the product section/form so it appears under the buy buttons. 4) Create a product metafield (namespace/key standard.cro_up_cross_selling, type: list of products). 5) Add the block in the Theme Editor and configure heading, ATC text and layout. 6) Assign the add-on products to each product via the metafield. The Slides layout lazy-loads Swiper from a CDN; the Stack layout uses a custom collapsible with an open/closed toggle. The add button reuses the theme's product form and loader-button and inherits the primary button colors.

items: ATC button text (rich text, e.g. '+ Add')
Layout: Stack / Slides (the code also supports 'Normal')
Spacing top/bottom for desktop (>=1000px) and mobile (px)

Ticket wish list (not all visible in the final UI): heading font/color/bold/alignment, number of products, product spacing, hover zoom or alternate image, button shape (round to square), button color and alignment, links, optional 'Added' state, background color

dependencies.text: Product metafield 'CRO | Up/Cross-Selling' (namespace.key standard.cro_up_cross_selling, type list of products) must exist and be filled per product. Needs a theme with a product form using is='product-form' and is='loader-button' custom elements (Focal-like) and CSS variables --primary-button-background and --primary-button-text-color. Edits to the product section's schema and render logic are required (theme code editing). Swiper v11 is loaded from the jsDelivr CDN for the Slides layout. Reference themes in the ticket: Impact, Concept, Local.

name: Cart Up-/Cross-Selling Carousel
status: Built — launched (Focal theme; other themes need code adaptation)

what.text: A recommendation block inside the cart drawer and cart page that suggests complementary products (e.g. 'Passt perfekt dazu' / 'Perfect match') below the cart line items. Items can be shown as a horizontal slider or stacked vertically. Each item has an image, title and an Add button. Optional teaser text, price (with compare-at price and savings) and star rating can be shown. Products with variants open a variant-selection popup (swatches and an add-to-cart button) before being added. Headline, sub-headline, text color and background color are configurable.

why.text: Cart is a high-intent moment, so complementary add-ons are accepted more easily and raise AOV. Items are low-friction, one-click adds that don't interrupt checkout. The sub-headline ('8 out of 10 customers also buy') adds a social-proof/bandwagon cue. Optional ratings and savings text reinforce trust and perceived value. Product-specific recommendations via metafield add relevance.

how.text: Built for the Focal theme. (1) Add a 'Cart Upsell' group to settings_schema.json with: show/hide checkbox, display select (horizontal slider / vertical), headline, sub-headline, product_list (limit 5), text color, background color, and checkboxes for teaser, price and rating. (2) Create snippet cart-upsell.liquid: it collects products from the product metafield custom.cart_upsell (product list) of every cart item, de-duplicates them, and excludes products already in the cart. If no metafield products exist, it falls back to the global product list in theme settings. It renders each one via upsell-product-temp, and renders a variant popup per product. (3) Create upsell-popup-temp.liquid: a bottom-sheet popup with image, title, price, option swatches (color swatches vs. text buttons, sold-out variants dimmed) and an add-to-cart button. (4) Create upsell-product-temp.liquid: the item row with image, title link, optional teaser (teaser-text snippet), optional rating (product-rating snippet, i.e. a placeholder for a review app) and optional price block with compare-at price and 'You save X'. A slick slider with arrows handles the horizontal mode. Slider/AJAX add-to-cart JS is not in the file and was shown in a Loom video. Ratings and teaser text depend on existing theme snippets. To show it during an A/B test while hidden in settings, use the CSS override `.cart-upsell{display:block !important;}`. Design styles from the references (Impact 'Sound', Concept 'Harmony', doonails, true-nature) need only CSS tweaks.

items: Sub-headline text (default '8 von 10 Kunden kaufen zusätzlich')
Show ratings/reviews (default off; star colors adjustable)

dependencies.text: Product metafield custom.cart_upsell (type: list of products) for per-product recommendations. Falls back to a theme-settings product list. Built for the Focal theme (cart drawer; slick slider; teaser-text and product-rating snippets; color-swatch-style snippet and color_swatch_config setting). The rating snippet is a placeholder for a review app (e.g. reviews.io). Requires dev work (no-code install not possible). Ticket notes KVA (cost estimate) approval: yes. Not portable to other themes without code changes. Cart JS (add-to-cart, slider init, popup toggling) is not included in the provided file (I).

name: Cart Hide "Remove" Button Toggle
status: Built — delivered, documentation pending

what.text: A theme-settings checkbox ("Hide remove button") in the Cart settings group that hides the "Remove" (Entfernen) text link on every line item in both the cart drawer (mini-cart) and the main cart page. It is off by default, so the link only disappears when merchants enable it. The ticket is labelled "Section", but the code is a global theme setting with Liquid conditionals, so it is better classified as a Feature.

why.text: Removing the easy exit from the cart reduces accidental or impulsive item deletions and keeps the cart value intact. The shopper's attention stays on the checkout CTA. Customers can still change quantity, so the path to removal is less prominent but not blocked. The effect is likely small and could frustrate users or hurt trust if removal is too hard, so it should be A/B tested. This reasoning is inferred, not stated in the ticket.

how.text: 1) In settings_schema.json, under the "Cart" group, add a checkbox setting with id cart_hide_remove_button, label "Hide remove button", default false. 2) In mini-cart.liquid, wrap the anchor with class line-item__remove-button in {% unless settings.cart_hide_remove_button %}...{% endunless %}. 3) In main-cart.liquid, wrap both the mobile (hidden-tablet-and-up) and desktop (hidden-phone) remove links in the same unless condition. The link keeps its url_to_remove and the translation key cart.general.remove.

items: Hide remove button (checkbox, default off) in Theme settings > Cart

dependencies.text: No metafields (ticket says MF/N). It assumes a theme with settings_schema.json, a "Cart" settings group, mini-cart.liquid and main-cart.liquid, and the .line-item__remove-button markup (Prestige-style theme, inferred from class names). No app is required. Because the setting is global, an A/B test needs a theme-level split or a test tool, since a theme setting alone cannot target a user segment.

name: Cart Shipping Progress Bar with Free Gift Milestones
status: Built — launched (Focal theme; documented in Slite)

what.text: A progress bar for the cart drawer and cart page that shows how much more the customer must spend to reach milestones: free shipping, a free gift, and a second free gift or automatic discount. Each milestone has its own icon marker on the bar. A dynamic message ('Only $X left until free shipping') updates as the cart value changes. When a threshold is reached, the customer can add a free gift from a gift-product block (optionally a slider of several gifts). The original brief asked for up to 5 goals, but the shipped build covers free shipping plus 2 gift tiers.

why.text: The goal-gradient effect: people accelerate as they approach a visible goal. A bar that shows remaining spend turns the free-shipping or gift threshold into a concrete target and encourages adding items to the cart, which lifts AOV. Several milestones keep motivation going after the first goal is reached. Gift icons add a reward and reciprocity element, and 'free' framing reduces perceived cost. Showing the bar in the cart means the nudge arrives at a high-intent moment.

how.text: Built for the Focal theme (code was not written for other themes, so other themes need adjustments). 1) Add a 'Shipping Progress Bar' settings group to settings_schema.json under cart settings: text color, active bar color, rest-of-bar color, rounded/square border, shipping icon (HTML), and a 'show free shipping minimum' checkbox. 2) Add a 'Cart Free Gift' settings group: display toggle, enable free item, headline, threshold, product_list of gift products, auto-add, gift icon, before/after messages with an [amount] placeholder, text and background colors, and the same fields for a 'Second Free Gift' with its own threshold, icon, messages, products and auto-add. 3) In the cart drawer, replace the content before the mini-cart form with Liquid that calculates thresholds (multi-currency via 'EUR:50,USD:60'), excludes non-shippable items, and renders a <free-shipping-bar> whose --progress CSS variable is cart total / max threshold. Icons are placed at left:% positions per threshold, and the message switches by the current stage. 4) Create the snippet free-gift-cart.liquid, which lists gift products (image, title, compare-at price, 'free for you', add button). It hides gifts already in the cart and shows the second-tier gifts only after the first gift is in the cart. The installation walkthrough was shared as a video, not as written steps. Discount logic: the second gift needs a matching automatic discount code created in Shopify.

name: Cart "Good Choice" Reassurance Banner

what.text: A slim, full-width banner at the top of the cart drawer, directly under the drawer header. It shows a check-mark icon and a short reassurance message, e.g. "Good choice! Your order will be in your hands within 1-2 business days." Background color, text color, icon, icon size, message text and font sizes (desktop and mobile) are all editable in the theme editor. It is built as a block with a limit of 1 inside the mini-cart (cart drawer) section.

why.text: Right after add-to-cart, buyers often feel post-decision doubt. Positive reinforcement ("good choice") validates the decision, and the delivery promise removes uncertainty about shipping time. A soft green background with a check mark signals success and safety. Placing it at the top of the cart keeps it visible at the moment of commitment and can reduce cart abandonment. The message text can also be swapped for brand or ingredient value messaging, as the second screenshot's example copy suggests.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet `ed-cart-good-choice.liquid`. It renders a flex container with an icon (inline SVG takes priority over an uploaded image), plus a richtext content area. CSS variables for text color, background, icon size and font sizes are set via a style tag scoped to the section ID. A `no-icon` class makes the text full width when no icon is set. On mobile (<1000px), the icon takes about 16% of the width and the text about 74%. 2) In `mini-cart.liquid`, add a `good_choice` block to the schema (limit 1) with the settings listed below. 3) In `mini-cart.liquid`, find `drawer__header` and directly below it loop over `section.blocks`, rendering the snippet for blocks of type `good_choice`. The merchant then adds the block to the Cart drawer in the theme editor and fills in the color, icon and text.

name: Payment Icons Bar (PDP & Cart)
status: Built — launched (shared PDP/Cart section; reorder option deferred to v1.1)

what.text: A configurable row of payment-method icons (PayPal, Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Klarna, Apple Pay, Sofort, etc.) placed near the add-to-cart button on the PDP and in the cart. Merchants choose which icons appear and whether they render in grayscale or full color. Optional extras (from the code) are a background color, rounded or square corners, and a 'pay in installments' line with a Klarna or PayPal logo and custom text. The original ticket also asked for an 'We accept' heading, which is visible in the PDP screenshot.

why.text: Showing familiar payment logos at the decision point reassures buyers that their preferred, trusted payment method is accepted. This lowers perceived payment risk and checkout anxiety. Logos of known brands such as PayPal, Klarna and Visa act as trust signals. The installment line also lowers the perceived price barrier by showing that paying in installments is possible.

how.text: Build one shared Shopify section (not separate PDP and Cart copies) that renders the icons with Shopify's payment_type_svg_tag. Each icon gets a checkbox. A 'payment_style' select (grayscale/colorful) applies a CSS filter: grayscale(1) or none to the SVGs. The delivered code uses a snippet 'ed-payment-bar.liquid' (flex row, space-between, wrap) and a snippet 'ed-klarna-custom-payment.liquid' for the installment line. Settings are stored in config/settings_schema.json, and the wrapper div is rendered where the bar should appear, for example in the cart. Wrap it in a toggle ('Display Section') so it can be shown or hidden for A/B tests. The wrapper is also given a CSS class so it can be force-shown during a test. Limit to about 6 active icons for layout reasons. The final solution is one global settings block that controls both PDP and Cart, as agreed in the comments.

name: PDP Store Benefits (Icon + Text USP Section with Normal / Tabbed-Slider Layouts)
status: Built — delivered and tested (Jan–Apr 2025); documented

what.text: A configurable Shopify section for the product page that shows up to 4 store benefits (e.g. free shipping from €35, 100-day returns, free spare-parts service, pay within 30 days via Klarna). Each benefit has an icon (SVG or uploaded image/logo) and optional text. It has two styles. 'Normal' shows a grid of icon + text items, which can be laid out vertically or horizontally with a configurable number per row on desktop and mobile. 'Slider' shows a row of icon tabs; clicking an icon switches the headline and longer text below it, and the selected icon can swap to an 'active' icon version.

why.text: Placed near the buy buttons, it answers last-minute purchase objections (shipping cost, returns, payment terms, warranty) at the point of decision. This lowers perceived risk and reinforces the value of buying from this store. Short icon + text pairs are scannable. The tabbed slider variant packs more reassurance into little space through progressive disclosure. Logo/image support also allows it to double as a trust-badge or payment-logo strip.

how.text: Create a store-benefits snippet (CSS + Liquid + small JS for tab switching) and render it from the product section/template with the benefit settings passed in. In the 'normal' style it renders a CSS grid with a configurable column count (desktop/mobile) and per-item flex layout (icon + text). In the 'slider' style it renders a header row of icons with a 4px underline on the active item, and a content area where only the active benefit's text is visible. A click handler toggles the 'active' class. Colors, font size, icon size, padding, gap and border radius are exposed as settings, and an SVG field overrides the image field. Later the benefits were refactored into theme BLOCKS (one block per benefit with its own settings and an 'Enable benefit' toggle) to keep the settings panel manageable. Editor note: icons are clickable in the editor to preview each tab.

name: Exciting Content Elements (Animated Counter Stats Section)
status: Built — launched (client feedback applied; documentation and product image still pending)

what.text: A reusable full-width Shopify section that shows a headline, a subheadline and 2–4 stat boxes side by side. Each box has a large number (e.g. "22", "99+", "88"), a short uppercase category label (e.g. HEADPHONE, BLUETOOTH, SPEAKER) and a short description. Thin dividers separate the boxes. On desktop an optional hand-drawn sparkle/star icon is placed over the top-left of the grid and animates in (line-drawing effect). Variant 1 of two; Variant 2 is a separate ticket.

why.text: Large, scannable numbers quickly communicate scale, range or proof (selection size, number of offers, years, customers). Concrete figures are more credible than vague claims. A counter that animates as the section scrolls into view draws attention and makes the facts easier to remember. The hand-drawn icon adds a friendly, distinctive touch that breaks up the page and keeps visitors scrolling.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-exciting-content-elements.liquid, paste in the provided code and add it via the theme editor (Global / any template). Blocks: Heading Title (with optional highlighted word and underline SVG), Heading Content (subheadline rich text), and repeatable Content Element blocks (number, label, description). CSS custom properties drive the settings. Layout is a CSS grid: 1 column on mobile, and on screens of 1000px or wider N columns (default 3) with vertical border lines between items. The count-up animation uses the native IntersectionObserver (no third-party libraries). The JS is wrapped in an IIFE so the section can be added several times on one page without conflicts. The draw icon is an absolutely positioned inline SVG with stroke-dashoffset animation. It is hidden below 1000px.

what.text: A PDP block titled "Product Short Videos" showing a row of small circular video thumbnails, similar to social media stories. The first thumbnail has a colored gradient ring (orange to purple) marking it as the active or unwatched item. The others have no ring. The thumbnails show short product-in-use clips, such as hands handling a bag, a close-up detail, and a person carrying the product. It can sit inside the buy box or be a larger standalone section. why.text: Short clips show size, material, and real-life use faster than static photos, which reduces uncertainty before purchase. The story-style circles are familiar from Instagram and TikTok, so they invite a tap. The gradient ring on the first item signals unseen content and creates curiosity. Videos of people using the product also work as lightweight social proof.

how.text: Build it as a PDP block or section that renders a horizontal row of circular thumbnails, one per product video. Source the videos from product-level metafields or media. Tapping a thumbnail presumably opens the clip in a modal or story-style player (not shown in the ticket). Give the first or active item a gradient ring. Offer two placements: compact inside the buy box, or a larger standalone section. Make the icon size a theme setting (for example a CSS variable driven by a range slider).

name: Collection Card Color Swatches (CRO | Artikel Farben)
status: Built — launched (delivered 2025-04-22; documentation reviewed in May 2025)

what.text: Variant color swatches shown under the product image on each product card in collection and listing grids. Each swatch is a small thumbnail of the variant's featured image, with a colored background as a fallback. The first variant is selected by default, and a tooltip with the variant name appears on hover. Clicking a swatch swaps the card's primary image to that variant's image. Swatches can be round or square, in small, medium or large sizes. They only render for products with more than one variant. The ticket asked for the swatches to lead to the variant, but the delivered code swaps the card image and does not change the link.

why.text: Shoppers can see color options right in the grid and preview them without opening the PDP. This reduces clicks and friction, helps shoppers find the color they like faster, and makes the range feel bigger. Showing more choices on the card also lets shoppers self-select, which increases the relevance of the click to the PDP. A thumbnail of the real product in each color is more informative than an abstract color dot.

how.text: Three steps, built and tested on the Focal theme (the reference was the Eclipse theme), with a setup guide for other themes. 1) In the product-item snippet, inside the product-item__info div, add Liquid that renders a list of swatch buttons, one per variant. It is wrapped in a check for more than one variant and the theme setting being on. The markup includes the CSS for the swatch sizes, shapes, hover ring, selected ring and tooltip. Each swatch's inner span uses the variant's featured image as its background and stores a large image URL in data-background. 2) In main-collection.liquid, add a script that sets up click handlers: on click it marks the swatch as selected and swaps the src and srcset of .product-item__primary-image to the swatch's image. It re-initializes on DOMContentLoaded, on shopify:section:load in design mode, on the collection:updated event, and via a MutationObserver for AJAX-loaded products (filters, pagination). 3) In settings_schema.json, add a 'CRO | Product Colors' header with three settings: a show checkbox, a Round/Square select and a Small/Medium/Large select. Maintenance happens through variants and their variant images in the Shopify admin.

items: Show CRO Product Colors (checkbox, default on)

dependencies.text: Products need multiple variants, each with an assigned variant featured image. The ticket flags a metafield as needed, but the delivered code uses none, only variants and variant images. Written for the Focal theme: it relies on the product-item snippet and the classes .product-item__info and .product-item__primary-image, and the product-item.product-item element, so other themes need class adjustments. The swatches work only on collection and listing pages. A PDP color selector that links to separate products (as in Eclipse) is a different, metafield-based solution and is out of scope.

name: Countdown Timer Section (Global)
status: Built — launched (section coded by Rana, documented in Slite; a few acceptance-criteria items are not visible in the delivered code)

what.text: A configurable countdown timer section (ed-countdown-timer.liquid) that counts down to a set end date and shows days, hours, minutes and seconds. It has an optional sub-headline, a headline and an outline CTA button. Two layouts are available: Minimalist (horizontal: text on the left, timer on the right) and Vertical (centered, with a large timer under the text). The background can be a color, an image or a video, with an optional color overlay. The original brief also asked for use in the announcement bar, the BuyBox, the Cart Drawer and under the hero image or price, so it would work as both a section and a block.

why.text: A visible deadline creates urgency and loss aversion. Shoppers who see time running out for a promotion (for example 'Last chance – 20% off sale items') are more likely to decide now instead of postponing the purchase. A live ticking timer makes the deadline concrete. A matching CTA next to it gives a direct next step. Because the timer can be switched off, the same element also works as a plain text-based scarcity message.

how.text: 1) Create the section file ed-countdown-timer.liquid in the theme and paste the provided code. 2) Add the section to the desired template through the theme editor. 3) Choose the layout style (Minimalist = horizontal, Vertical). 4) Add a 'Countdown header' block with sub-headline, headline (rich text), button text and URL, and optionally 'open in new tab'. 5) Add a 'Countdown timer' block with the end date and the labels for days, hours, minutes and seconds. 6) Set the background color, text color, overlay color and opacity, and optionally a background image or video. 7) Optionally enable 'customize settings' to override font sizes, weights, gaps and button height separately for desktop and mobile. JavaScript in the section runs the live countdown and loads resources. Documentation exists in Slite and a support video was recorded.

name: Announcement Bar (Benefits, Reviews.io, Countdown, Dismissible Promo Bar)
status: Built — launched (tested internally, documented)

what.text: A custom, theme-portable Shopify section placed at the top of the page. It combines up to three stacked layers. (1) A main bar with benefit messages (icon + text, optional small CTA button) or a live Reviews.io rating block (average score, review count and the Reviews.io logo). (2) An optional countdown timer bar with text before and after the timer. (3) An optional additional promo bar with a link that visitors can dismiss with an X. The bar can be sticky and can be restricted to specific page types. The reference screenshot shows a green gradient bar with '4.68 / 5 positive Bewertungen' and the Reviews.io logo, then two benefits ('Free shipping from €49' and '100-day money-back guarantee'), then a purple promo bar ('Secure our sets at a special price – also perfect as a gift') with a close X.

why.text: The first screen the visitor sees carries the key trust and value signals: free-shipping threshold, risk-free guarantee and a live review score. This reduces purchase anxiety and perceived risk right away and keeps those messages visible while scrolling when the bar is sticky. A countdown or promo message adds urgency and highlights offers. Because the extra bar can be dismissed, it avoids annoying returning visitors, and the message stays out of sight for 7 days after dismissal.

how.text: Create a snippet 'announcement-reviewsio.liquid', which fetches the average rating and review count from the public Reviews.io timeline API using the store key from the block settings. Create a section file 'announcement-bar.liquid' with blocks of type 'message' (icon SVG, text, link, optional button) and 'reviews-io-widget'. The section also contains a countdown timer (show_timer: text before/after, link, colours) and an additional bar (text, link, colours, close icon). Visibility and sticky behaviour are resolved in Liquid via template.name (all / home / product / collection). Sticky behaviour is set per device: sticky, sticky_desktop or sticky_mobile. Position uses 'position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 5' with a breakpoint at 741px, and CSS variables expose the sticky state to the theme (--enable-sticky-announcement-bar). Layout: with two messages they sit 50/50 and the Reviews.io block is full-width and centred, ordered first on mobile. With a single block the content is centred at 100%. The dismiss click hides the additional bar and stores a timestamp in localStorage; the bar stays hidden for 7 days. Built from scratch because the old announcement code was scattered across the theme. Estimated effort was 8–12 hours (KVA).

name: Optimized Price Communication (Old Price → New Price → Savings)
status: Built — launched (code delivered by Jani, fixed and extended by Rana; internal testing in March 2025)

what.text: A price display for product cards (collection) and the product page (PDP). It shows the crossed-out old price first, then the new sale price, then a savings label (e.g. 'Du sparst €3,00' or 'You save 20%'). Font size and font color for the old price, the sale price and the regular price are configurable, as are the savings text and the savings format (absolute amount or percentage). Rana's final version adds a savings-label style (Classic/Bold), label size, label color and label background.

why.text: Showing the higher reference price first anchors the buyer on the old value. The sale price then reads as a gain, and the explicit savings label (amount or %) makes the deal concrete. Configurable colors and sizes let you make the sale price and savings stand out, for example red for the sale price and green for savings, which strengthens the perceived discount. The ticket does not state the reasoning, so this is inferred.

how.text: 1) Create or adapt the snippets product-item-price.liquid (collection cards) and product-price.liquid (PDP). Both render the sale price, compare-at price and savings label from the selected or first available variant. For variant ranges they use the cheapest variant with a 'from' price. 2) Reverse the visual order with CSS: the compare price gets `order: -1` inside the flex price list, so it appears before the sale price. 3) Add a 'Prices style' group to config/settings_schema.json with a discount_mode select (percentage/saving), range sliders (8–100px) and color pickers for price, compare price and sale price, plus a savings_label_text field. 4) Output the settings as inline CSS (font-size, color, gap 8px, margin/padding reset) scoped to .product-item and .product. 5) Render the snippets in product-item.liquid and product-info.liquid where the price should appear. 6) In the final version, add the savings style (Classic/Bold), label size, color and background settings. Note that the original code had bugs and CSS conflicts (some settings had no effect), which Rana fixed.

name: Highlighted Search Bar with Predictive Search Drawer
status: Built — launched (tested by Christoph and Chris, KVA approved; documentation partly incomplete)

what.text: A standalone Shopify section called "Search function" that makes on-site search more prominent. Variant 1 leaves the search as a plain header icon (magnifier next to the burger menu, as on HNDS). Variant 2 shows a visible search bar under the header, with a grey background band, a coloured rounded border, a placeholder (e.g. "Wonach suchst Du?") and a magnifier icon on the right (as on dermalogica.de). The bar can optionally be sticky. Tapping it opens a custom right-hand predictive search drawer. The drawer has a title, input, live results for products, collections, pages and articles in tabs, and a "View all results" button that goes to /search?q=.

why.text: A visible search field lowers the effort needed to find a product. Shoppers who know what they want (high-intent) get a direct route to it instead of hunting for a small icon. A sticky bar keeps this path available during scrolling. Live product suggestions with image and price shorten the path to the PDP and cut dead-end browsing. The placeholder phrased as a question ("What are you looking for?") invites interaction.

how.text: 1) Create a dedicated section ("Suchfunktion") with a "Highlight" setting: not highlighted (icon only) or highlighted (full-width bar). 2) When highlighted, expose settings for background colour, border colour, placeholder text and a sticky toggle. 3) Because the theme's built-in search drawer is spread across several files and is not portable, build a self-contained snippet (psy-search.liquid) with its own markup, CSS and JS. The snippet includes a fixed full-screen overlay, a right-aligned drawer (max 500px, full width on mobile), a header with close button, an input with a submit icon, hidden tabs (products/collections/pages/articles) and a results area. 4) The JS debounces input (300ms) and calls /search/suggest.json with resources[type]=product,collection,page,article, limit 5 and unavailable products hidden. It renders results (2-column product grid on mobile), aborts stale requests, shows empty/loading/error strings, and formats money with the theme's currency format. Enter, the magnifier or the "View all results" button redirects to /search?q=. 5) Test in the dedicated "Search functionality" theme.

name: Product Teaser Texts (Metafield-driven subtitle under product title)
status: Built — launched (tested internally; documented in Slite; product image added to the product catalog)

what.text: A short, product-specific teaser line shown directly below the product title. It appears on the PDP and in every product card or product list on the home page and collection pages. Content comes from a product metafield called 'Teaser-Texte' (rich text, so single words can be bolded). Font size (desktop and mobile) and text colour are set globally in the theme settings, and display can be switched on or off separately for home, collection and product pages. On product-list cards the teaser is a link to the product page.

why.text: The teaser puts a single benefit, USP or emotional hook right next to the product name, where attention is highest. This helps shoppers decide before they open the PDP and reinforces the value proposition on the PDP. Bolding single words lets key terms stand out when the text is skimmed. Because each product has its own text, the copy stays relevant instead of generic.

how.text: 1) Create a product metafield 'Teaser-Texte' (rich text) in the Shopify admin. Its definition namespace must match the lookup used in the code (product.metafields.standard['teaser-texte']). 2) Create the snippet teaser-text.liquid. It decides from the template (index / collection / product) and the theme settings whether to show the text. It outputs the metafield with metafield_tag, as a div on the PDP and as a link to product.url in lists. It also injects CSS using the colour and font-size settings, with a media query at 1000px for desktop. 3) Add a 'Teaser texte' group to config/settings_schema.json with: desktop font size range, mobile font size range, colour picker, and three checkboxes (home, collection, PDP). 4) Render the snippet under the product title in product-item.liquid with product_page: false, and in product-info.liquid with product_page: true. 5) Merchants write the text in Admin > Products > [product] > Metafields section > 'Teaser-Texte'.

name: Collection Page Price Hide Toggle (CRO | Prices)
status: Built — tested and approved (Feb–Mar 2025), documented

what.text: A theme-level on/off switch that hides all price information on collection pages and on featured-collection blocks. With it off, prices show as normal (Variant #2). With it on, product cards show only image, title and optional badge/teaser, with no price (Variant #1). It is set up as a checkbox in the theme settings and not as a standalone section, although the ticket calls it a Section named 'CRO | Prices'. In the editor it sits under Collection → Collection page → Theme Settings → 'Price Hide Button'.

why.text: Without a price on the grid, shoppers can't screen products out on price alone, so they click through to the PDP. There, the benefits, reviews and trust elements get a chance to justify the price before it is judged. This raises PDP views and works well for high-consideration or premium products. It also works as a clean A/B test: price visible vs. hidden on the listing. The effect can go either way, because some shoppers dislike hidden prices, so it should be tested rather than assumed.

how.text: 1) In config/settings_schema.json add a 'Collections' group with a checkbox `show_price_on_collections` (default false; label: 'The activation hides all price information on featured collections and collection pages'). 2) In snippets/product-item.liquid, after the closing </product-item> tag, add `{% if settings.show_price_on_collections == true %}<style>.shopify-section--featured-collections .product-item-meta__price-list-container, .shopify-section--main-collection .product-item-meta__price-list-container {display:none;}</style>{% endif %}`. 3) Merchants turn the checkbox on or off in the theme customizer. The 'show' variable name is misleading, because true means prices are hidden. For an A/B test, run the two states as separate theme/variant versions or via the test tool. The ticket says non-devs cannot install it, so a developer has to do it.

items: Hide prices on collection pages and featured collections (checkbox `show_price_on_collections`, default off, true = prices hidden)

The code appears to target a Maestrooo-style theme such as Prestige or Impact (inference). The core price hiding needs no metafield. The optional teaser needs the product metafield 'Product Teaser' to be filled in. The teaser and badge settings were added because of the 'Spotlight' feature (per a dev comment) and are not needed for price hiding. Developer installation is required. The price is hidden only via CSS (display:none), so it is still present in the page source.

name: PDP Video Play Button (Gallery Overlay with Fullscreen Video Popup)
status: Built — launched (QS passed, documentation written; instructions being made theme-agnostic)

what.text: A small round or square thumbnail with a play icon is overlaid on the product gallery images. It uses the product's featured video (or a custom thumbnail). On click, the video opens in a fullscreen black popup with native controls and autoplay. The popup closes via the X button, a click on the backdrop, or the Escape key, and the product page is visible again. The button can sit in any of the four corners, appear on the first image only or on all images, and be a circle or a square. It is rebuilt from the Focal theme's native video play button and is configured in the theme editor under the product section's Media settings as 'Video Play Button'.

why.text: Product video answers questions that static images can't: real size, how it looks when worn, texture, and movement. That reduces uncertainty and return risk. A small preview thumbnail in the corner of the gallery draws attention without interrupting the shopping flow, and it is opt-in, so there is no autoplay annoyance. The popup shows the video large and distraction-free, and shoppers return straight to the product and the buy box. Seeing the item in use also acts as informal social proof and builds trust.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet video-play-button.liquid. It reads the product metafield standard.featured_video (video source URL) and an optional featured_video_thumbnail, falling back to the video's preview image. It renders a <video-play-button> custom element with a thumbnail, an overlay and a CSS play triangle. 2) Create the snippet video-play-button-popup.liquid, containing a fullscreen popup container, a close button, a lightweight JS class (VideoPlayButton extends HTMLElement) and CSS. The class creates the <video> element on open, removes it on close, closes on Escape or backdrop click, and locks page scroll via a class on <html>. The CSS positions the button according to the section settings; it is 54px on mobile and 100px at 1024px and wider. 3) Add three select settings to the product section schema (main-product.liquid): position (top_left/top_right/bottom_left/bottom_right, default top_right), fixing (first/all, default all) and format (circle/square, default circle). 4) Inside the media image wrapper (.product__media-image-wrapper), render the video-play-button snippet if the featured_video metafield exists; if fixing is 'first', render it only when forloop.index == 1. 5) In main-product.liquid, render the popup snippet once if the metafield exists. Because the button renders inside the main product section, it cannot be a standalone section. Theme file names and structure may differ, so the instructions must be made theme-independent. The ticket also notes that pasting schema lines at the very end of the JSON causes a syntax error, so the placement must be explained clearly.

items: Position: top left / top right / bottom left / bottom right (default: top right)
Fixing the video: show on first product image only / show on all product images (default: all)
Optional per-product thumbnail via metafield featured_video_thumbnail (otherwise the video preview image is used)
Autoplay and controls are set as attributes on the custom element (both true by default)

dependencies.text: Product metafield standard.featured_video (Shopify's native video metafield; the button only renders if it is filled). Optional metafield standard.featured_video_thumbnail. Shopify theme based on Focal (the Focal main-product section and the .product__media-image-wrapper element); other themes need adapted file names and insertion points. Must be installed by a developer (code in 2 snippets plus 3 edits in main-product.liquid), so no-code installation by non-devs isn't possible yet. No app required; the custom lightweight JS replaces the dependency on the theme's ed-custom.js.

name: PDP Image Info Buttons (Info Bar Overlay with Tooltip)
status: Built — launched (v1.0 delivered and tested; v1.1 ideas collected)

what.text: A slim info bar placed on each product gallery image, either overlaid at the bottom of the image or underneath it. It shows a short benefit or USP headline (e.g. 'High-quality 925 sterling silver', 'With important cofactors', 'Includes free Mjuck insert worth up to €79'). An (i) icon at the right edge reveals a longer explanatory text in a tooltip bubble on hover. The text is maintained per product and per image. If no title is maintained for an image, the whole bar is hidden. The tooltip appears only if a detail text exists.

why.text: Short USPs sit directly on the product image, where attention is highest, so key benefits are seen without scrolling to the description. The optional (i) tooltip gives details on demand, which keeps the image clean while answering objections (material, ingredients, bonus value) at the moment of consideration. This supports perceived value and reduces uncertainty. Custom colors let the bar match the brand and stay unobtrusive.

how.text: Original build is a theme-code integration: (1) Create the snippet info-buttons.liquid. It takes the image loop index and reads title and text from a product metafield list (later converted to a metaobject so merchants only enter text instead of editing JSON). It renders the bar only if the title is not blank, and the (i) icon and tooltip only if the text is not blank. CSS positions the bar absolutely at the bottom center of the media item. The tooltip is a white bubble with an arrow that fades in on icon hover. (2) Add a 'Info buttons' settings block to the product section schema, with colors, width and position. (3) Render the snippet inside each product media item in product-media.liquid, passing forloop.index. The 'under image' option sets the bar bottom to 0 and adds bottom padding to the media item. Instructions must be theme-independent, since not every theme has main-product.liquid, and written so non-experts can follow them.

items: Info bar background color (default #ffffff; clearing the hex gives a transparent bar)
Info button background / fill color (default transparent; the schema label is mislabeled as a duplicate 'Info bar text color')
Info bar width, 20–100% (default 80%), to make it as wide as or narrower than the image
Info bar position: Inside image / Under image
Per-product content (metaobject or metafield): title and tooltip text per image; empty title hides the bar
Style variations (requested by the PL team; the code shows only color variations)
v1.1 ideas: adjustable bar height, icon size, text alignment (left / centered)

dependencies.text: Needs a product metafield (standard.info_buttons) with a list of title/text entries, later replaced by a metaobject for easier editing. Requires editing theme files: new snippet info-buttons.liquid, schema in the main product section, and a render call in the product-media snippet inside the media item loop. Built and tested on a Dawn-like theme (sectionfy.io). The CSS selector .product__media-item may need adjusting for other themes. The metafield definition must exist before content can be edited, and Shopify can take time to reflect metafield changes. Non-devs cannot install it without the instructions.

name: PDP Product Thumbnails Gallery (Theme-Agnostic Slider)
status: Built — launched (source code + setup guide delivered; documented)

what.text: A standalone, theme-agnostic product media section. A main image slider is paired with a clickable thumbnail strip, placed left of or below the main image on desktop. On mobile the thumbnails can be shown below or swapped for pagination dots. The section also supports video slides with a round video thumbnail button (play icon) that opens a fullscreen video popup, optional video autoplay and looping, and automatic selection of the active slide when a product variant is chosen. The original request was to recreate the Focal theme's thumbnail function 1:1 as its own section so it can be used in other themes.

why.text: Thumbnails show shoppers up front how many images exist and what they show (angles, details, in-use shots, infographics, video). That lowers the effort of exploring the product, supports purchase confidence, and increases media engagement. Syncing the slider to the selected variant shows the exact colour or version the shopper picked, which reduces uncertainty and returns. The video bubble draws attention to rich content.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet ed-product-media.liquid and paste in the delivered CSS and Liquid. 2) The section uses two Flickity carousels: carousel-nav (thumbnails) and carousel-main (large images), loops over product.media, and renders image, video, or 3D-model badges. 3) Layout is controlled by CSS classes: ed-thumbnails-left, ed-thumbnails-right, ed-thumbnails-bottom, and ed-thumbnails-bottom-mobile. 4) On mobile without thumbnails, pagination dots are shown (a long active dot, short inactive ones) plus small arrows. 5) Desktop prev/next uses half-width clickable zones with custom arrow cursors. 6) The video bubble is a circular thumbnail at the top right of the image that opens a fullscreen popup with a close button. 7) Variant sync: custom JavaScript reads the variant ID from the URL. If the variant has a featured image that exists in the slider, that slide is set as active. This works because every theme updates the URL with the variant ID. 8) Setup guide and source ZIP were provided to developers.

items: Desktop thumbnails position (Left / Bottom; code also supports Right)
Optional transparent gradient arrows on the thumbnail strip

dependencies.text: Flickity carousel library. Theme-specific icon snippets (e.g. render 'icon' for video/3D badges) and the theme's media setup. The variant-to-slide sync depends on the variant ID being written to the URL. Product media must be in product.media. The existing CSS references hnds.de arrow assets, which should be replaced per store. Reference screenshots come from Solago (hnds.de) and the Focal theme. Rana also built a product video play button in a separate ticket.

name: Configurable PDP Buy Box (fully block-based, with variant, subscription, payment and price-per-portion options)
status: Backlog — spec / requirements list (no build confirmed)

what.text: A fully modular PDP buy box in which every element is a theme block, including product title, price, variants, quantity, CTA, payment icons, USPs and legal notes. The box and the area behind it can be styled (box color, background color, background shadow). The top and bottom blocks sit flush with the box edges, with no extra spacing. The box bundles these features: (1) variant selectors with style options (square, rounded, image swatches), highlighted selected state, a 'Bestseller' badge and discount badges; (2) configurable quantity buttons; (3) a subscription display with tabs for one-time purchase vs. subscription, each with its own benefits; (4) styling for legal notes and base prices (font size, color, placed below or beside the price); (5) payment icons with custom uploads and ordering; (6) an installment-payment display (Klarna popup or own term and interest rate); (7) a 'price per portion' indicator. The screenshots show the following reference UI: rating + title + price + 'Only €0.19 per shower' bubble, short description, benefit bullets, stock bar, dark CTA with a sub-line, payment icon row and shipping info cards. They also show icon-based trust bullets with a Klarna line and a USP icon grid.

why.text: The buy box is where the purchase decision is made, so clarity and trust here have the biggest effect on conversion. Highlighted selected variants and a 'Bestseller' badge give social proof and reduce choice paralysis. Discount badges tied to the strike-through price make the saving visible. Price per portion, and installment amounts or Klarna, reframe a high sticker price as a small daily or per-use cost (price anchoring, pain-of-paying reduction). A subscription tab with its own benefits clarifies the value of recurring purchase and can raise LTV. Payment icons, guarantee bullets and shipping USPs reduce perceived risk right next to the CTA. Block-level control lets the team A/B test each lever quickly.

how.text: 1) Rebuild the buy box as a Shopify section in which every element is a block (title, rating, price, description, USP list, variant picker, quantity, subscription tabs, CTA, payment icons, legal/base price, price per portion, stock bar, info cards). 2) Add global color settings (box color, outer background color, background shadow). Each block also gets its own color setting, which overrides the global value. 3) Remove top and bottom padding on the first and last blocks so they sit flush with the box edge. 4) Variants: a style selector (square / rounded / image), selected-state color and highlight, an optional centered or left-aligned layout and optional full-width layout. The Bestseller badge has configurable text, color and target variant. Discount badges are pulled automatically from the strike-through price and have configurable colors. The default selected variant is set via a metafield. Optionally, separately listed products that are really variants can be linked as variants on the PDP. 5) Quantity buttons are definable in the editor. Whether the logic should be custom or use a Bundles app is still to be decided. 6) Subscriptions: tabs for one-time purchase and subscription, each with separate benefits. Compatibility with Recharge and Shopify subscription apps must be checked. 7) Legal notes and base price: font size and color settings, placed below or to the right of the price. 8) Payment icons: a visual style option (reference zoelu.com), fix the Klarna Pay Later icon, support custom icon uploads, add Swift as a default icon, and add custom Prepayment and Pay-on-invoice icons. Icon order should be configurable. How to maintain the order so that cart and PDP stay consistent is an open question (a shared global setting or snippet is suggested, inferred). 9) Installments: store a term and an interest rate to calculate the installment. Offer an easy Klarna integration so the Klarna popup is available. Adapt the section to the vegardians.de bestseller-bundle example. 10) Price per portion: the number of portions comes from a global editor setting or a product metafield. The layout follows the referenced Figma wireframes (TrueNature, Berserker) or the screenshots.
