name: PDP Delivery Time & Stock Status Communication
status: Built — launched (delivered in the test theme; install instructions were being reworked to be theme-independent)

what.text: A configurable product-page block that shows a colored status dot and a short availability or delivery message directly above the Add to Cart button. It covers four states: In stock (for example 'Auf Lager - in 1-2 Werktagen bei Dir'), Low stock ('Nur noch [count] übrig'), Overselling/Preorder ('Bald wieder auf Lager' or 'Ab dem [next_incoming_date] wieder auf Lager'), and Sold out ('Bald wieder für dich verfügbar'). The message updates live when the shopper switches variants. Every state has its own editable text, text color and background color, all maintained in one place in the theme editor.

why.text: Delivery certainty is one of the biggest sources of purchase anxiety. A green dot with a clear promise such as 'in stock, in your hands in 1-2 working days' lowers perceived risk right at the decision point. A red or amber low-stock message adds honest scarcity and urgency. Preorder and incoming-date messaging keeps out-of-stock shoppers on the page and sets expectations instead of losing them. Placing the message next to the CTA means it is seen at the moment of commitment.

how.text: Add an 'inventory' block schema (limit 1) to the product section's blocks. Create an inventory.liquid snippet that checks the selected variant's availability, inventory_policy, inventory_quantity, incoming and next_incoming_date to pick one of the four states. The snippet renders the text with a colored 10px dot (a ::before pseudo-element) and replaces the [count] and [next_incoming_date] placeholders. Render the snippet from product-form.liquid via a `when 'inventory'` case. Also output a JSON map of per-variant HTML. Add a small <product-inventory> custom element to theme.js that listens to the form's 'variant:changed' event and swaps in the matching HTML. Merchants then edit texts and colors in the theme editor. The PL team also asked for a pulsing dot animation (like Bestelectronic), an option to hide the dot, and per-part coloring (for example only 'Auf Lager' in green). The code supplied covers per-state colors, but the pulse animation and hide-dot toggle are not visible in the delivered code.

items: In stock: label text, label color, text after label, text color, background color
Low stock: low inventory threshold (range 0-100, 0 = always show in stock), text with [count] placeholder, color, background color
Overselling/Preorder: text, incoming-stock text with [next_incoming_date] placeholder, color, background color
Sold out: text, color, background color
Requested but not confirmed in the delivered code: pulsing dot animation, option to hide the dot, link of the text to a product metafield

dependencies.text: Needs a theme with a main-product / product-form structure that supports blocks, plus the ability to edit theme.js and add a snippet. The code was written for a specific theme (Dawn-like, with a variant:changed event). Inventory tracking must be enabled in Shopify. The Preorder and incoming-date states depend on the variant's inventory_policy 'continue' (sell when out of stock) and on Shopify's incoming inventory and next_incoming_date data from transfers or purchase orders. The Shopify Admin handles this data, with no separate app mentioned. Install instructions had to be rewritten to be theme-independent for non-developers. Some customer-facing German default texts are hard-coded.

Support tickets or contacts about delivery time

name: Cart Reservation Label (Static Notice / Countdown Timer)
status: Built — launched (Focal theme; per-theme adaptation needed for other themes)

what.text: A configurable label shown in the cart drawer and cart page with two modes. Mode 1 (static scarcity) shows a fixed notice such as "Your items are not reserved in the cart" next to a small icon. Mode 2 (dynamic scarcity) shows a countdown message such as "Your cart is reserved for (time) minutes" with a live mm:ss timer. The timer duration is set in minutes (the ticket cites 1–120). When the timer expires, the countdown label is hidden and the static label is shown again.

why.text: The static notice implies that stock is not held, which creates loss aversion and nudges shoppers to check out sooner. The countdown adds a time-bound deadline to finish the purchase, which triggers urgency and reduces cart abandonment and dithering. Placing it right in the cart puts the pressure at the decision point. Overly aggressive or fake timers can erode trust, so the duration should be realistic.

how.text: Add a Liquid snippet (cart-reservation) that renders two label blocks, a static one and a timer one. The timer text contains the placeholder "(time)", which is replaced with a span that JavaScript updates. Settings live in theme settings (settings_schema.json): icon (HTML/SVG), static text (richtext), timer text, minutes, text colour, font size, alignment, background colour and border style. Inject the minutes value as a JS variable in theme.liquid. In theme.js, reservationTimer() runs a 1-second interval against a start/end timestamp stored in localStorage and updates the .time element. checkCart() resets the end time when a product is added while the cart is empty (no #mini-cart-form). Hook reservationTimer() into the cart drawer re-render (CartDrawer._rerenderCart) and checkCart() into the add-to-cart handler (ProductForm._onSubmit) in the Focal theme. Render the snippet in the cart with {% render "cart-reservation" %}. Other themes (e.g. Impulse) need their own hook points because each theme's cart differs.

items: Reservation icon (pasted SVG/HTML; icon colour is only changeable by editing the SVG, with a colour picker planned for v1.1)
Static label text (rich text), e.g. "Deine Artikel werden im Warenkorb nicht reserviert"
Timer label text with (time) placeholder, e.g. "Dein Warenkorb ist für (time) Minuten reserviert"

dependencies.text: No metafields. The ticket flags it as not installable by non-devs. It needs theme file edits: a new snippet, a script variable in theme.liquid, JS in theme.js, theme-settings schema entries, and hooks in the cart drawer and add-to-cart code. Built on the Focal theme; other themes (e.g. Impulse) need custom hook placement. Relies on browser localStorage for the timer state. Behaviour note: in the timer-label field the static text is shown when no timer is wanted or after expiry. Per the comments, the first (static) field applies when no timer is desired. In the code, the timer text field must be non-empty for the countdown to render.

name: Cart Payment Icons & Installment/Invoice Payment Bar
status: Built — launched (documented, product image in catalog)

what.text: A payment bar placed directly under the checkout button in the cart (cart page and cart drawer). It shows a row of selectable payment-method icons (PayPal, Mastercard, Visa, Amex, Klarna, Apple Pay, Sofort, etc.). Below the row is an installment/invoice message line, e.g. 'Bequem auf Raten zahlen' ('Pay comfortably in installments') with a Klarna or PayPal logo. The ticket asks for it to be built as its own section. The delivered build uses theme settings and snippets rather than a section-editor block.

why.text: Payment icons next to the checkout button reassure shoppers that their preferred, familiar payment method is accepted, which lowers payment anxiety at the decision point. The 'pay in installments / on invoice' message lowers the perceived price barrier and the risk of paying upfront. This is especially useful for higher-priced carts. Grayscale styling keeps the bar unobtrusive, while a colorful style raises brand recognition.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet ed-payment-bar.liquid. It renders payment_type_svg_tag icons for each enabled checkbox and applies a grayscale or colorful filter. 2) Create the snippet ed-klarna-custom-payment.liquid. It shows the Klarna or PayPal logo plus a configurable text line, with a font size and color setting. 3) Add the 'Styling of payment bar' schema to config/settings_schema.json. 4) Render both snippets in a wrapper div (.ed-payment-bar-cart) under the checkout button in the cart template and drawer. The installment line only renders if 'Show rate payment on cart page' is enabled. Cart settings were deliberately separated from the PDP settings, so the PDP bar is controlled in the product section. The dynamic installment amount shown in the second reference ('Pay over 3 interest-free payments of 19.97 €') comes from the Klarna On-Site Messaging app and cannot be hard-coded.

name: Cart Shipping Cost Communication (Subtotal / Shipping / Total)
status: Built — launched (approved by 3 testers; v1.1 coupling idea open)

what.text: A cart footer price breakdown for the cart drawer and cart page with three rows: Subtotal, Shipping and Total. The shipping row shows the shipping fee, or a highlighted 'Free' label (custom text, colour and bold) once the free-shipping threshold is reached. Optionally the shipping row shows a country dropdown (e.g. 'Shipping costs: Germany ▾') with live shipping rates taken from the Shopify shipping zones. If the dropdown is switched off, one global shipping fee is shown.

why.text: Showing shipping costs early and transparently removes the surprise-cost shock that causes cart abandonment. A green, bold 'Free' label turns free shipping into a visible reward. A per-country shipping estimate gives international buyers certainty before checkout, which builds trust and reduces risk.

how.text: Add the settings to settings_schema.json (calculation on/off, free-shipping threshold, delivery fee, live-calculation checkbox, footer labels, free-text colour). Create the snippet totals-cart.liquid, which computes the shipping price (0 if cart total >= threshold) and renders the Subtotal, Shipping and Total rows. Render it in mini-cart.liquid before the checkout button, and on the cart page. For the optional country dropdown, add a mini-shipping-estimator custom element in theme.js. It calls Shopify's /cart/prepare_shipping_rates.json and /cart/async_shipping_rates.json with country and zip, stores the choice in cookies, and uses the country-with-province-zip snippet for default zip codes. The free-shipping threshold must also match Shopify Settings > Shipping. The code is based on a theme with a 'mini-cart' and a 'themeVariables' object.

name: Collection Model View Toggle (Product vs. Model Images)
status: Built — launched (code documented, support video available)

what.text: A toggle in the collection page's meta bar (next to the product count and sort-by) that switches all product-card images between the product-only shot and the on-model shot. It comes in three layouts: (1) a checkbox-style switch labelled e.g. 'Tragebilder' (worn images), (2) two text buttons 'Model | Product' with an underline on the active one, (3) a 'classic' layout with a title ('Opinion:') and two icons (a shirt for product-only, a person for model) with optional hover tooltips. The position in the meta bar can be left, center or right. It was implemented as a block inside the main-collection section, with a limit of 1 per section.

why.text: Shoppers in apparel and accessories want to see how an item looks when worn (fit, drape, scale) as well as the clean product shot for detail. Letting them choose their preferred view on the listing page reduces the need to open each PDP, speeds up browsing and comparison, and increases confidence and relevance. This gives the shopper control and improves product-card engagement and click-through. The toggle also stays visible without taking up product space, because it lives in the existing meta bar.

how.text: 1) In main-collection.liquid, replace the 'product-facet__meta-bar anchor' markup with the provided version, which renders the 'ed-model-view' snippet in the left, center or right slot depending on the setting. 2) Add a new schema block 'model_view' (limit 1) with settings for position, layout (checkbox/button/classic), the labels and the tooltip texts. 3) At the end of the section's top <style> tag, add the Liquid loop that reads the model_view block settings into variables (active_model_view, model_type, position, labels, tooltips). 4) Create the snippet ed-model-view.liquid containing the CSS, the markup for the three layouts and the JS. The JS toggles the class 'ed-ModelView-active' on the product list. The CSS then hides the first card image and shows the second one (and swaps them back on hover), so the theme must output the model image as the second image of each product card. In the theme editor, add the 'Model view' block to the collection page and set its options. Non-developers cannot install it, but once it is installed the block can be configured in the editor.

items: Classic layout: Tooltip text for product view and for model view

Ticket spec (original ask, not seen in the code): visibility on/off, design variation, background color, text color, icon and toggle colors (active/inactive). The delivered code only exposes the settings listed above; the toggle colors are hard-coded (#e6e6e6 inactive, black knob when active).

dependencies.text: Needs a Shopify theme whose collection section is main-collection.liquid, with the classes 'product-facet__meta-bar', 'product-list.product-facet__product-list' and 'product-item__image-wrapper' (Prestige-style theme markup). Each product must have a model image as its second image (the first being the product shot, or the reverse depending on the store's setup), because the toggle only swaps image order via CSS. No metafields or apps are required (ticket field: MF/N). The snippet uses fixed element IDs (ed-model-view-button-open/close), so it supports one instance per page. The JS runs on DOMContentLoaded and the Shopify design-mode section load event; it does not re-bind after AJAX filtering or pagination, so this should be tested.

name: PDP Social Proof Banner (Avatar Stack + Rating Pill)
status: Built — launched (documentation/instructions being made theme-agnostic)

what.text: A configurable social proof banner for the product page, placed in the buy box (e.g. below the buy buttons). It has two modes. (1) 'Social banner': a stack of up to 5 round avatar images, a bold influencer/customer name with an optional blue Instagram-style verified checkmark, and a rich-text line such as 'and 63,000 others are thrilled with us'. (2) 'Rating banner': a full-width pill with rich text in which the placeholder '(rating)' is replaced by five yellow/currentColor stars, e.g. '18,386+ customers rated us 5 stars'. Background colour, text colour, corner style (rounded or square) and top/bottom margin are editable.

why.text: Showing real faces, a recognisable name and a large aggregate number triggers herd behaviour and the bandwagon effect ('others like me already bought'). The verified checkmark borrows social-media credibility and authority. A star rating with a review count is a fast, universally understood trust shortcut. Placing it right by the add-to-cart/buy buttons addresses last-second doubt at the decision point.

how.text: Build it as a product-page block in the theme's main product section (limit 1). Block schema: a 'Type' select (social / rating), colour pickers for background and text, a margin range slider (0–60px), a corner style select (rounded 10px / square 0), five image_picker fields, a text field for the name, a checkbox for the checkmark, a richtext field for the message, a checkbox for bold text, and a richtext field for the rating text (using the '(rating)' token). Render it through a snippet (social-proof-banner.liquid) called from the block loop of the product form. The snippet outputs overlapping 24px circular avatars (-4px overlap, white ring) with the name, the inline SVG checkmark (#4C8AE7) and the text on one flex row. In rating mode the '(rating)' token is replaced with five inline SVG stars via JS. Note: the Liquid in the ticket is theme-specific (it assumes product-form.liquid and main-product.liquid), so instructions must be adapted per theme.

name: Product Badges (Tag-driven image labels)
status: Built — launched (tested internally, documented)

what.text: Small text badges (e.g. "BESTSELLER") overlaid on a corner of the product image. They appear on collection product cards and on the product page media, and are also reused in search and featured collections. Badge text comes from product tags in the format "__label:Bestseller". Theme settings control position (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) and corner radius in px. Badge colors are configured per badge name through a metaobject. The same snippet also shows automatic "Sold out" and discount (% or amount) badges.

why.text: A badge such as "Bestseller" gives social proof and a quick decision cue right where the shopper is looking at the product image. This reduces choice overload in grids and steers attention to winners, promotions and new items. Consistent, color-coded badges let shoppers scan a list quickly and support click-through to the PDP.

how.text: 1) Add a "Product Badges" group to settings_schema.json with two custom label color pairs, a position select (top_left/top_right/bottom_left/bottom_right) and a corner-radius range (0–100px). 2) Create the snippet product-labels.liquid. It loops over product.tags, picks tags containing "__label", and takes the text after the colon. It then looks up the metaobject "product_badge" for an entry whose badge_name equals that text and applies its color and background_color inline. If no entry matches, it falls back to the theme-setting colors (label--custom / label--custom2 for "__label2"). It also outputs a sold-out badge and a discount badge. The snippet's CSS positions .product-item__label-list absolutely inside the image wrapper according to the position setting and applies the border-radius. 3) Render {% render 'product-labels', product: product, reduced_content: reduced_content %} inside .product-item__image-wrapper in product-item.liquid. 4) Render {% render 'product-labels', product: product, reduced_content: false %} inside .product__media-image-wrapper in product-media.liquid. Workflow for merchants: create a metaobject entry (badge name, text color, background color), then add the product tag "__label:<same name>". The two are linked automatically by name matching.

items: Custom label 1 text color and background color (theme settings)
Custom label 2 text color and background color (for __label2 tags)
Position: top left / top right / bottom left / bottom right
Metaobject "product_badge": badge_name, color, background_color (individual per-badge colors)
Discount badge display (percentage or amount) via existing theme settings (show_discount, discount_mode)

dependencies.text: Product tags in the format "__label:Name" ("__label2:Name" for the second style). A Shopify metaobject definition "product_badge" with the fields badge_name, color and background_color (needed for individual colors). A theme with .product-item__image-wrapper and .product__media-image-wrapper containers (code is based on a Maestrooo-style theme), plus theme translation keys for sold out and discount. Needs edits to settings_schema.json, product-item.liquid and product-media.liquid. Metaobjects cannot yet be created via Git or theme files, so they are set up manually in the admin (API creation is planned for a later phase).

what.text: A fully configurable product card for the collection (category) page grid. Each card has a product image with an optional slideshow (arrows), a corner icon badge, a colored benefit/icon bar under the image, an uppercase title, a subline, star rating with review count, a price, and optional text badges such as 'Bestseller' or 'Neu'. The ticket originally asked for a standalone 'Produktkacheln' section. why.text: Cards show the key purchase info (pack size, duration, price per unit, rating, status badges) before the click. This lowers the effort of comparing products and makes the card more persuasive. Star ratings and 'Bestseller'/'Neu' tags add social proof and quick-scan cues. The benefit bar and icon badges communicate value at a glance. A quick-ATC button on the card shortens the path to purchase, and the base price makes different pack sizes easy to compare.

how.text: Build the card as a snippet that extends the theme's product-item snippet. It reuses the existing product-image slideshow Jani already built. Render it inside the main-collection section, with all options exposed in that section's settings so the theme's filter/sort keeps working. Drive the badges from product tags (colors set in the editor, position set to left/right and top/bottom). Drive the text badges (up to 3), benefit badges and icon badges from product-level data (metafields or a dynamic source). Pull the base price from the Shopify backend. Integrate the reviews.io rating widget with a star color setting. The quick ATC is either a small bubble on the image (position, color, icon configurable) or a full-width button under the price. Open point from the comments: whether it adds the first variant or opens a variant picker for multi-variant products, as in the Focal theme. what.text: A full-width pill-shaped badge under each product card on collection pages (below title, price and ratings). It shows a short attribute or benefit such as 'dry skin' with an icon, or 'oily skin' with an icon. The content comes from a product metafield, so each product can show a different badge. Colors, corner radius and alignment are set globally in theme settings.

why.text: Shoppers scanning a grid can't open every product. A visible 'who it's for' or 'use case' label (skin type, evening routine) lets them self-qualify in seconds. This cuts decision effort and the number of PDP visits needed to compare, and sends the right shoppers to the right product. The icon adds quick visual recognition, and the soft pill style adds emphasis without competing with price or the CTA.

how.text: 1) In snippet product-item.liquid, paste the badge block at the end of the product-item__info div. It renders only if the 'show_cro_type_badges' setting is on and the metafield is not blank. It outputs a wrapper div containing a flex span styled from the theme settings. 2) In settings_schema.json, add a 'CRO | Type Badges' group at the end of the 'Collections' settings: checkbox, SVG color, text color, background, border-radius range 0-100px (step 4, default 100), and alignment select (Left/Center/Right). 3) Create a multi-line text product metafield 'CRO | Type Badges' with namespace and key standard.cro_type_badges. It accepts HTML, SVG or plain text, and an tag for an image icon. Put the icon and text together in one metafield, so no extra metafield per icon is needed.

name: Product Title Badges (Badges Above Product Title)
status: Built — delivered for feedback (June 2025); later marked as duplicate/done

what.text: A section that shows up to 3 pill-shaped badges directly above the product title, on both the product detail page and the product cards in collection grids. Badge text comes from per-product metafields. Each badge can have its own color scheme and an optional icon. Empty metafields hide the badge, and if all are empty the whole badge row is hidden. Screenshots show examples such as 'Top rated', 'Limited', 'Best match' (PDP/collection) and 'Pflegt und stärkt die Nägel' (a benefit pill with an icon on the live Health Routine PDP).

why.text: Short labels next to the product name give the buyer a fast read on the product's key claim before they read anything else. Labels like 'Top rated' work as social proof, 'Limited' adds mild scarcity/urgency, and benefit pills ('Nourishes and strengthens nails') communicate value. Placing them at the title level makes them visible in both grid scanning and PDP evaluation. Color-coded schemes (neutral/success/warning) let the label's tone match its meaning.

how.text: Build two implementations, because the theme handles the PDP and the collection card differently. (1) PDP: a custom section 'CRO | Title Badges' added to the product template above the title. Each of the 3 badge blocks has a color scheme dropdown, an icon image picker, and a dynamic-source badge text bound to a product metafield (Title badge 01/02/03). (2) Collection: a 'CRO | Product Title Badges' group in Theme settings > Collections, with per-badge color scheme and icon, plus global style settings. Both read the same three product metafields, so the same text appears in both places. Render a badge only if its metafield is non-empty, and render nothing if all are empty. Use pill styling with uniform padding and gaps, wrapping onto a second line on small screens. Optionally add a light fade-in, make sure badges don't overlap images, and keep text screen-reader readable.

name: Competitor / Product Comparison Table Section
status: Static section built (code delivered); dynamic compare-list version built but moved to Backlog as too complex

what.text: A configurable Shopify section called 'CRO | Konkurrenzvergleich' (comparison table). It shows a heading, subheadline, text and CTA button, plus a side-by-side table. Up to 4 products (or 'us vs. others' columns) are compared, each with an image, name, price and 'View' button. Below them sit feature rows (e.g. Driver, Weight, Battery, or 'Ritual guide included: Yes / No'). One column can be highlighted as the 'active' column, e.g. 'WE' vs 'OTHERS'. A dynamic variant (the 'CRO | Dynamic Compare' section) builds the table from products visitors add via a '+ Add to Compare' button, stored in browser localStorage.

why.text: Comparison tables cut decision effort and show the differences between options in one view. Highlighting 'our' column with ticks against competitors' 'No' makes the unique selling points concrete and reduces the doubt that stops purchases. For product ranges, a side-by-side comparison guides undecided visitors to the right variant, which reduces choice paralysis and can raise AOV by steering toward higher-priced options. Reference cases: IMPACT theme 'Sound' preview and the live example on thatspiritualshop.de.

how.text: Static version: add the section to any template. Select products (product pickers) or type the column values by hand. Add one 'row' block per feature, with a label and a value per column. Choose the highlighted column and adjust fonts, sizes, colours and borders. Dynamic version: a '+ Add to Compare' button on collection product cards saves product data (including metafields for specs) to localStorage. The button then changes to a link to the Compare page. A dedicated Compare page renders the saved products. Liquid (server-side) and JS (client-side) are synced with a workaround. Feedback: choosing products only through the section, e.g. with a dropdown, would be less confusing, but this was not built.

name: Price Breakdown (Fair Pricing Transparency)
status: Done — treated as equivalent to the existing 'CRO | Global | Kostentransparenz' (cost transparency) section; reference only

what.text: A section that shows shoppers how the product price is made up. A headline and short intro sit above 4 percentage segments (e.g. 42% / 24% / 18% / 16%, or 45% / 25% / 20% / 10%). Each segment has a short label such as production, development, marketing, service or profit. The segments are shown either as a grayscale segmented bar with the active item highlighted (dotcomcanvas) or as circular photos above the percentages (hundpur). A short explanatory text or brand promise sits below, and an optional trust badge or award can be shown beside it. The ticket also suggests making the points clickable so each one can reveal more content.

why.text: Price objections often come from not seeing what the money pays for. Showing where each euro goes frames the price as fair and justified, and justifies a premium for quality. This reduces perceived risk and price resistance, and builds trust through openness. Pairing the numbers with a quality promise or award adds authority. Interactive points let curious shoppers dig deeper without cluttering the page.

how.text: Build it as a theme section with a heading, subheading and 3–5 repeatable blocks. Each block holds a percentage, a label, an optional image or icon and an optional description. Style A: a horizontal segmented bar whose segment widths match the percentages, with the active item underlined or in a darker shade and its description shown below. Style B: round images above the percentages and labels, followed by a promise text and badge image in a card. For the clickable option, each block acts as a tab or accordion trigger that swaps the descriptive text below or opens a popup. Place it on the PDP below the product info or description, and make it reusable site-wide. The ticket notes this equals the existing Cost Transparency section, so reuse that build.

name: Collection Product Card Image Slider (CP Product Slider)
status: Built — launched (documented; infinite-swipe idea logged for v1.1)

what.text: A swipeable image carousel inside each product card of a product grid (primarily collection pages). Shoppers can browse 1 to 5 product images per card (e.g. front, back, detail, on-model) without opening the PDP. Navigation uses dots (bottom left or bottom right) and/or arrows with a configurable colour. Mobile and desktop can be switched on or off and styled separately. Dots sit below or beside the image rather than over it. The slider also applies to every grid that uses the product card: home, collection, product page recommendations and search results.

why.text: On a listing page, one static image forces a click to the PDP to see more. Letting shoppers see more angles in place lowers the effort needed to judge a product, which reduces uncertainty and speeds up decisions. It also increases engagement with the product card, which signals interest. Showing back, detail and on-model shots in the grid works like a quick-look and supports fashion/apparel where fit and look matter. Dots show that more images exist (progressive disclosure). Keeping dots off the image avoids visibility problems on busy or colored backgrounds.

how.text: 1) Add a 'CP product slider' group to config/settings_schema.json with the settings listed below. 2) Create the snippet cp-product-slider.liquid. It loops over product.images (limit = image count setting) and outputs lazy-loaded images with responsive widths and a 0.8 aspect ratio inside a Flickity container. The snippet also holds the CSS: dot and arrow styling, and mobile (<1000px) vs desktop (>=1000px) media queries that hide the original static image and show the slider. 3) Add a cpProductSlider() function to assets/custom.js that initialises Flickity only when a card has more than one image (config: adaptiveHeight, dragThreshold 10, contain, pageDots, prevNextButtons). 4) Render the snippet inside .product-item__image-wrapper in product-item.liquid. 5) Load Flickity CSS and JS in theme.liquid head (the ticket uses the unpkg CDN). Pagespeed must not suffer: images are lazy-loaded and the slider only initialises when there are 2 or more images. Because the code touches theme files, non-developers cannot install it.

name: Collection Page Infinite Scroll (Toggle vs. Pagination)
status: Built — launched (tested and documented; product image added to catalog)

what.text: A collection-page feature that automatically loads the next batch of products as the shopper nears the bottom of the product grid, with a loading spinner and no manual pagination. It is controlled by a checkbox in the collection section settings. When enabled, products load automatically and the pagination is hidden. When disabled, the standard pagination is shown and nothing loads automatically.

why.text: Infinite scroll removes the friction of clicking through numbered pages, so browsing feels continuous. Shoppers see more products in one session and are less likely to drop off at a page break. This can raise product views and add-to-cart rate on large collections. The toggle lets the team A/B test infinite scroll against classic pagination, since infinite scroll can hurt footer access and make it harder to return to a position in the list.

how.text: Implemented as custom code, because no existing theme had it. 1) Add a checkbox setting 'Enable Infinite Scroll' (id enable_infinite_scroll, default false) to the main-collection section schema. 2) When the setting is on, inject CSS that hides the page-pagination element (opacity 0, pointer-events none). 3) After {% endpaginate %}, render an <infinite-scroll></infinite-scroll> custom element when the setting is on. 4) In theme.js, define an InfiniteScroll custom element. It uses an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 100px, threshold 0.1) on the pagination element. When it comes into view, it fetches the rel='next' URL and parses the HTML. It appends the new .product-item nodes into '#facet-main .product-list__inner' and refreshes the pagination markup. It stops observing when there is no next link, and shows or hides a spinner during loading. 5) In custom.css, add the spinner styles and force .product-item[reveal] to opacity 1 so the appended items are visible. The selectors are theme-specific and must be adapted to other themes.

items: Enable Infinite Scroll (checkbox in the collection section, default off)
On = automatic loading of further products, pagination hidden
Off = no automatic loading, standard pagination shown

dependencies.text: No metafield needed. Needs a theme with a main-collection section that uses {% paginate %} and a page-pagination element with a rel='next' link. Needs the theme.js custom-element base class (CustomHTMLElement) and the selectors #facet-main .product-list__inner .product-item. Needs access to edit theme.js, custom.css and the section schema, so it cannot be installed by non-developers. The theme is a Focal-style theme (inferred from CustomHTMLElement and page-pagination). The source is a Sectionfy test theme. Estimated effort was about 5 hours. The ticket calls it a 'Section', but the implementation edits the existing collection section.

items: Page load/performance (LCP, INP) with more items loaded
Conversion rate and revenue per session (A/B vs. pagination)

name: Cart Drawer Sticky Elements & Scroll Settings (Sticky Checkout Button, Progress Bar, Payment Icons)
status: Built — launched (reduced scope: only checkout button, progress bar and payment icons can be sticky)

what.text: Settings in the cart drawer (mini-cart) section that keep key cart elements pinned while the rest of the cart scrolls. The checkout button can be sticky at the top or bottom of the drawer. The free-shipping/reward progress bar can stick to the top. The payment icons and store benefits bar can stick to the bottom. The whole cart drawer scrolls when its content does not fit on one screen. The sticky checkout button uses the inverse of a PDP sticky ATC: a cloned button is shown only while the original in-flow button is out of view, and it hides as soon as the original becomes visible.

why.text: Cart drawers with upsells, recommendations and notes push the checkout CTA below the fold, so shoppers have to scroll to find the next step. A persistent checkout CTA keeps the primary action always visible and reduces friction and drop-off. A sticky progress bar keeps the free-shipping or reward goal in view, which strengthens goal-gradient motivation and AOV. Sticky payment icons and store benefits give constant trust reassurance at the moment of purchase decision.

how.text: Built as theme-level code in the cart drawer section, not a pure no-code block. 1) Add schema settings to mini-cart.liquid: enable_sticky_button (checkbox, default on), sticky_button_position (top/bottom, default bottom), enable_sticky_progressbar (checkbox, default off), enable_sticky_paymenticons (checkbox, default off). 2) Add a conditional <style> block: the progress bar uses CSS position: sticky at top: 0 with a white background and negative gutter margins. The drawer is made scrollable (overflow-y: auto) and the footer transform is removed. The checkout button and payment icons are cloned and use position: fixed, because they sit inside the cart footer and CSS sticky breaks once the parent scrolls out of view. Add top padding to the drawer when the button is sticky at the top. When both the button and payment icons are sticky at the bottom, offset the button by the payment-icon height via a CSS variable. 3) Add a JS scroll listener on #mini-cart that clones #checkout-button-wrapper and #payment-icons-and-store-benefits once, then shows or hides each clone depending on whether the original is in the viewport. 4) In theme.js, after the cart drawer innerHTML is re-rendered, call checkCheckoutButtonVisibility() after about 800ms so the sticky state is rebuilt after cart updates.

name: PDP Product Tabs (Tabs on Desktop, Accordion on Mobile)
status: Built — delivered, documented (Slite doc); product image still requested for docs

what.text: A theme-agnostic Shopify section, "CRO | Product Tabs", that shows product information in a horizontal tab bar on desktop (uppercase labels, animated underline on the active tab, thin divider line, first tab open by default). On mobile the same blocks turn into a collapsible accordion. Each block is one tab and can be a Description (pulls product.description), a free Content block (rich text or a linked Page), a Custom Liquid/HTML block, or an FAQ block (up to 12 question/answer pairs, each with an 'open by default' toggle). Tables can be placed inside tab content via the HTML field. It replicates the tab function of the Focal theme but works in any theme.

why.text: Product pages carry a lot of secondary information (description, shipping, materials, size tables, FAQs). Tabs and accordions keep the page short and scannable while leaving the details one click away. This lowers cognitive load and scrolling, answers purchase objections (FAQs, size tables, care and shipping info) near the buy box and supports trust and risk reduction. Opening the first tab by default guarantees core information is visible without interaction, and collapsing on mobile avoids long page scrolls.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-product-tabs.liquid and paste in the provided code (CSS, Liquid and a small vanilla-JS tab controller, with no Focal code dependencies). In the theme editor, add the section to the product template and add blocks (Description, FAQ, Content, Custom Liquid), reordering them as needed. Each block's title becomes the tab label on desktop and the accordion header on mobile. Desktop tabs are driven by JS: click switches the active class, animates content height and slides the underline indicator; the first tab is initialised as active. Mobile uses custom <ed-collapsible> accordion markup (a button with aria-expanded plus a collapsible content div). The JS re-initialises on Shopify section load events so it works in the theme editor. Per-product content is intended via metafields or page assignments (e.g. Liquid/Content blocks that reference product metafields or Pages).

items: Custom max-width toggle plus max-width slider (preview shows 930px)
Section spacing desktop: top, bottom, left, right (px)
Section spacing mobile: top, bottom, left, right (px)
Blocks: Description, FAQ, Content, Custom Liquid (add, remove, reorder; number of tabs is flexible, ~4 recommended)
Per block: title, optional linked Page, rich-text content, 'expanded by default' (mobile)
FAQ block: up to 12 question/answer pairs, each with an open-by-default toggle

dependencies.text: Works with any Shopify theme, but the code assumes a few Focal-style theme conventions: the translation key 'product.general.description', the global theme settings settings.heading_color, settings.text_color and settings.background, the CSS variable --container-gutter and the .heading--small class. It needs checking or adapting on non-Focal themes. Per-product maintainability (the PL team's wish for self-created metafields) needs custom product metafields or page assignments referenced in blocks. The ticket requested separate line colour, icons per tab, a dedicated table builder and FAQ assignment, but these are not in the delivered code and settings screenshot: divider colour is hard-coded (#dfdfdf), there are no icon settings and tables are only styled through the HTML field.

name: Application Steps (Tabbed Image Steps with Progress Bar)
status: Built — launched (QA confirmed working, docs written)

what.text: A theme-editor section that shows a product's usage or application as a row of numbered step images (e.g. 01–04) with a progress bar underneath. Clicking a step image makes it active, advances the progress bar, and swaps the heading and description text below. Each step is a block with an image, a heading and rich text. Rebuilt from the Piwi skincare PDP, where it explains how to use the oil (Cleansing, Effect, Care, Additional care).

why.text: Showing how to use a product step by step lowers perceived effort and uncertainty, especially for products with a routine such as skincare. Numbered visuals chunk the information into small steps. The progress bar gives a sense of progress and a clear sequence. Seeing the product in use builds confidence and shows the product's value before purchase, which reduces hesitation and post-purchase misuse and returns.

how.text: Add the section file (ed-cro-application-steps.liquid) to the theme and place it on the product page template, or any page, through the theme editor. Add one block per step and upload an image (same format, ideally a white or neutral background so the fade works). Enter a heading and short text for each step. The first step is active by default. A small custom JS tab script toggles the active image, shows the matching text and sets progress to (index+1)/total. It is scoped per section, so the section can be duplicated on one page, and it re-initialises on shopify:section:load in the editor. A CSS gradient fades each image into the section background, and the step number sits over the faded area. Non-developers can set it up through the theme editor with the setup guide.

name: Auto-Apply Manual Discount Codes (Customer-Tag Based)
status: Backlog — scoping; reference implementation reportedly exists for client BIG (Focal theme)

what.text: Manually created Shopify discount codes are redeemed automatically, so the shopper does not have to type them in. The code can be applied either to all visitors (flat) or only to customers with specific customer tags. A related requirement is to display the active automatic discount codes to the shopper. The ticket links to an earlier implementation, but the links were not accessible, so the details are unconfirmed.

why.text: Removing manual code entry cuts checkout friction and stops shoppers leaving to hunt for coupons. Tag-based targeting makes the offer feel exclusive (VIP, newsletter or B2B segments), which raises perceived value. Showing the active discount builds reassurance that the shopper is getting the best price.

how.text: Per the comments, the approach is to link the feature to a metaobject that holds the manual discount code or discount link, and to load it before checkout. The ticket says it currently only works via customer tags. A likely build: a metaobject stores the code and the customer tag(s) it applies to. Liquid checks `customer.tags` (or applies to everyone if no tag is set). The code is then applied via Shopify's discount URL (`/discount/CODE`) or a cart/checkout redirect before checkout. A small banner or cart note shows the applied code. Comments warn that this may be hard to port outside the Focal theme because other themes are structured differently, and that it may not be a section at all, just a function connected to a metaobject.

name: Spacing Section (Spacer)
status: Built — tested, documented

what.text: A standalone Shopify section that adds an empty vertical band between two other sections. Its top and bottom padding and its background colour are set in the theme editor, with separate desktop and mobile spacing. It can be added to any template, so it works as a layout tool in A/B tests without a developer touching the theme.

why.text: Whitespace groups related content, separates unrelated blocks and sets the reading rhythm of the page. This reduces cognitive load and makes a CTA or a social-proof block easier to notice. Because spacing and colour can be changed per breakpoint without code, the agency can test layout variants quickly. This is an indirect lever with a small effect. It mainly supports other elements rather than driving conversion on its own.

how.text: 1) Create the section file `ed-spacing-section.liquid` in the theme and paste in the provided code. 2) In the theme editor, add 'Spacing Section' to any template between two sections. 3) Set the background colour and the top and bottom spacing for desktop and mobile. The CSS targets `#shopify-section-{{ section.id }}`. It applies the desktop padding from 1000px up and the mobile padding below 1000px. A transparent colour value falls back to the theme's global colour settings.

items: Background colour (default transparent, which falls back to the theme background; screenshot shows #6F719B)
Text colour (in the code only, not visible in the screenshot; default transparent, which falls back to the theme text colour)
Custom CSS field (visible in the editor panel)

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps are needed. The theme must expose the global colour settings `settings.background`, `settings.heading_color` and `settings.text_color`, which the section uses as fallbacks. It also needs standard section support (`presets`) so it can be added through the editor. The theme is assumed to wrap each section in `#shopify-section-{{ section.id }}`, as Shopify does by default. Non-devs can add the section once the file exists.

name: Testimonial Videos Slider
status: Built — launched (documented, added to product catalog)

what.text: A standalone, theme-editor-configurable Shopify section that shows a horizontally scrollable slider of vertical customer testimonial videos. On desktop, a left column holds the headline, sub-headline and text CTA link with an arrow. To its right sit the video cards, each with a custom thumbnail and a translucent play-button overlay. A round badge such as '300,000+ customers love [Brand]' overlaps the top-left or top-right corner of the video area. The editor supports up to 15 video blocks.

why.text: Short, authentic UGC videos from real customers are strong social proof. They show the product in real hands and real settings, which lowers perceived risk for new visitors. The large-number badge adds a bandwagon cue ('300,000+ customers love us') right next to the proof. A thumbnail with a play button invites a low-effort click. The optional CTA below the headline channels the trust into the next step.

how.text: Build a custom Shopify section (Liquid, schema, CSS, JS) with global section settings and a repeatable 'Video' block. Each block has a direct video URL (an MP4 uploaded to Shopify Files, not YouTube/Vimeo) and an image_picker thumbnail used as the video poster. Videos render as native <video> tags with the poster. An SVG play button overlays each video and hides while the video plays. Native controls show only during playback. Clicking a video toggles play/pause. The slider uses Slick Carousel with variableWidth, no arrows or dots, and infinite off. Slick and jQuery must be loaded in theme.liquid. Slide widths are fixed (about 224px on mobile, 284px on desktop). From 1000px up, the header becomes a fixed-width (295px) left column beside the slider. Add a small script so only one video plays at a time and the others pause. Re-initialise the slider on the shopify:section:load event. Editors should click Save in the theme editor to re-initialise the slider.

items: Border style: rounded or square corners
Video blocks (up to 15): video URL + thumbnail image

dependencies.text: jQuery and Slick Carousel (CDN) must be added to theme.liquid. The section does not include them. Videos must be uploaded to Shopify Files or another direct MP4 source, because YouTube links will not work. Thumbnails are chosen via image_picker. If the same Shopify file is reused across slides, editing it changes every slide that references it. No product metafields are needed (the ticket marks the metafield question as 'MF/N'). A container class and theme CSS variables for fonts are assumed. Whether non-developers can set it up is still to be clarified.

name: Collection Quick Add to Cart with Size Picker (Fashion)
status: Built — launched (tested internally, documented, source code handed over; theme-editor configurability planned for v1.1)

what.text: A quick add-to-cart feature for collection product cards. Each card shows a small cart/bag icon over the product image. Clicking it opens a size-picker overlay on the image, showing the variant options (e.g. XS, S, M, L) as white tiles with a close (X) button. Clicking a size adds that variant to the cart immediately (quantity 1) and opens the mini cart. Single-variant products add directly on the first click. Sold-out variants are marked as sold out and, when clicked, trigger the back-in-stock (BIS) flow instead of adding to cart, as on the PDP.

why.text: It removes the click-through to the PDP for shoppers who already know what they want (e.g. returning fashion customers who know their size), so the path from browsing to cart is shorter. Choosing a size is the only decision required, so friction is minimal. Sold-out sizes shown up front set expectations and capture demand via BIS. The mini cart opening gives instant confirmation and encourages further browsing and a higher items-per-order count.

how.text: 1) Add a checkbox setting 'Enable quick add to cart (custom)' (id product_add_to_cart_custom) to settings_schema.json. The theme's existing 'Enable quick add to cart' toggle is separate and activates the theme's default quick add. 2) Add the JS to custom.js: a delegated click handler on .product-item-atc (opens the picker if it has the open_sizes class, otherwise adds the first variant directly); a swatch click handler that finds the matching variant from the data-variants JSON, updates sold-out states, then POSTs to /cart/add.js with quantity 1 and dispatches the theme's cart:updated and cart:refresh events (openMiniCart: true); sold-out swatches trigger .BIS_trigger; a close handler removes the .active class from .card-size-picker. 3) In product-item.liquid, inside product-item__image-wrapper, render the 'card-size-picker' snippet when the setting is on. 4) Create the snippets card-size-picker, variant-picker-custom (builds swatch containers per option from product.options_with_values and outputs product.variants as JSON in data-variants), icon-product-block-cart, icon-size-picker-close and icon-mail. 5) Style the overlay (a bar at the bottom of the card image with white size tiles and an X on the right). Built on the Focal-based theme; porting to other themes requires adjustments.

items: Enable quick add to cart (custom): on/off checkbox, default on (theme setting)
Enable quick add to cart: the theme's native quick add toggle, kept separate
Design variations selectable in the section (per the Pegador reference); not yet configurable in v1, planned for v1.1
Size tile size and styling: CSS only for now, planned to become configurable in v1.1

dependencies.text: Shopify theme with a product-item.liquid card and a custom.js file. The code uses the Focal theme's cart events (cart:updated, cart:refresh) and window.themeVariables.routes. Needs a back-in-stock app that provides a .BIS_trigger element. Pegador used a BIS app that is not installed in the demo store, so sold-out behavior there is only approximated. No metafields required. A Non-Dev installation is not possible (the ticket says so). The source code is delivered as a TXT file and documented in Slite.

name: PDP Model & Fit Info Bar (Passform)
status: Built — launched (tested internally, KVA approved)

what.text: A slim info bar attached to the product image gallery on the PDP. It shows a fit statement fed by a product metafield, for example "Our model is 1.70 m tall and wears size S". The bar can sit as an overlay at the bottom of the image or directly below it. It has an optional leading icon (ruler/tag, image or SVG) and supports bold text via rich text. The ticket was filed as a "Section"; the delivered code is a theme block with a snippet, added to the product section.

why.text: Size uncertainty is the main barrier to buying clothing online and a leading cause of returns. Showing the model's height and the size they wear gives shoppers a concrete reference point right where they judge the product, so they can estimate their own fit. This lowers perceived risk, speeds up size selection and should reduce size-related returns. Placing it directly at the image keeps it in the shopper's line of sight and avoids a trip to a size chart.

how.text: 1) Create a product metafield "CRO | PDP | Passform" (namespace and key standard.cro_pdp_passform, single line text) and fill it per product, e.g. "Unser Model ist 1,70 m groß und trägt Größe S". 2) Create snippets/cro_pdp_passform.liquid. It renders only if the metafield has a value, outputs the icon plus the text, and applies the block settings as inline CSS. 3) Register a block of type cro_pdp_passform (limit 1) in the product section schema with the settings below. 4) Render the snippet inside the section's block loop (case/when or if/elsif), placed near the media gallery wrapper. 5) In the theme editor, add the block, set the style and position, then QA on desktop and mobile. The Overlay mode uses position:absolute at the bottom of the image. The optional "Hide image whitespaces" setting makes the gallery full-width on mobile. The screenshots show a later app-style variant ("CRO | Fit") with a rich-text content field and a "Hide if metafield is not available" toggle. The code file in the ticket does not contain those two features.

items: Icon as image (image picker, 18x18 px recommended)
Icon as SVG (HTML field; overrides the image icon; default ruler-style SVG)
Hide at Desktop (show on mobile only)
Fit position: Overlay on image / Below image (default Below image)
Space left-right / inner padding (0–30 px, default 16)
Text alignment: Left / Center / Right (default Center)
Border bottom on/off and border color (default #E0E6E9)
Gap left-right / outer margin (0–30 px, default 0)
Seen in screenshots: rich-text content field and "Hide if the metafield is not available" toggle

dependencies.text: Product metafield standard.cro_pdp_passform (single line text) must exist and be filled per product. It needs an OS 2.0 theme whose product section supports blocks and a snippet render. The CSS selectors for the full-width mobile option (.product__media-list .product__media-item) are Dawn-like and may need adapting to other themes. The theme should be duplicated before editing. The metafield key shown in the screenshot (standard.cro_pdp_fit) differs from the code file (standard.cro_pdp_passform), so check the key naming per install.

name: Multiple Product Videos (Story-Style Video Popups)
status: Built — launched (static theme-editor version; metafield/metaobject version tracked in a separate ticket)

what.text: A Shopify PDP section showing a heading (e.g. "Die Verwendung" / "How to use") above a horizontal row of round (or square) video thumbnails with captions, in the style of Instagram stories. Each thumbnail can show a play icon. Clicking one opens a modal popup that plays that item's video, with a title and a description. Content is entered per item in the theme customizer.

why.text: Short, tap-to-watch videos show how the product is used, styled or applied without forcing a long page read. This reduces uncertainty and helps shoppers picture owning the product, so they are more likely to add to cart. The familiar story-style UI invites curiosity and engagement, and keeping the video in a popup leaves the buy box and scroll position untouched. Multiple short clips let shoppers pick the use case that matters to them.

how.text: Create a new section file in the theme (the instructions file names it ed-multiple-product-videos.liquid) and paste the code. Add the section to the Product template in the theme customizer and place it under the buy box or product info. Set the heading, sub-headline, colors and font sizes. Add one "Item" block per video with a thumbnail image, video, caption/title and popup description. The ticket's own settings: background color, font color, font size, headline, sub-headline, and per-video thumbnail, video, title and popup description. Later additions: uppercase heading toggle, display on/off toggle with an A/B-test CSS override, separate desktop and mobile spacing and font sizes, alignment, and video controls (controls, autoplay, muted, loop, width, rounded corners). The JS must pause the video when the popup is closed. Test on desktop and mobile. Videos are static per section and cannot differ per product; unique videos per product need the separate metaobject/metafield version.

name: PDP Quantity Buttons & Tiered Pricing
status: Backlog — scope under discussion (not built)

what.text: A PDP section that shows pack sizes or quantities as clickable buttons or cards (e.g. '1x', '2 x 300g', '6 x 400g'). Exactly one option is active at a time. Each option can carry a discount badge (e.g. '10%') and a 'Bestseller' pill, both with custom colors. Three layouts are available: Text only, Text + Badge, and Visual (product image, quantity info, discount badge). The active option is highlighted with a border, background or shadow. In the reference screenshots, badges sit on the top edge or top-right corner of a button, and the Bestseller pill sits above its button.

why.text: Showing bundle sizes up front turns quantity into a visible choice instead of a hidden field. Discount badges (5% / 10% / 15% / 20%) create a tiered-pricing anchor that rewards buying more, which raises units per order and AOV. The 'Bestseller' pill is social proof and a default nudge toward the preferred pack. A single highlighted selection reduces decision effort. In the Visual layout, stacked product images show the larger pack, which makes the extra value tangible.

how.text: Build it as a Shopify section with a repeatable block per option. Each block holds display text, Shopify quantity, optional discount badge text and color, optional Bestseller label and color, and an optional image (Visual layout only). A layout dropdown switches between Text only, Text + Badge and Visual. Badge positions are fixed per layout. Mobile stacks the options vertically or uses a horizontal scroll, depending on layout. There are two implementation routes. (1) Full custom selector: the chosen quantity is passed to the cart, which needs new discount logic so tier discounts apply and the correct number of items is added. The dev estimate is about 8–10 h plus 2–3 h per theme. (2) Style the theme's existing variant selector, where each variant is named like a quantity: about 2–3 h per theme, but it only changes the variant, not the cart quantity. The dev suggested starting with this for the Focal theme.

items: Layout type dropdown: Text only / Text + Badge / Visual
Per option: Shopify quantity (number passed to the cart)
Per option: product image (Visual layout only)
Mobile behavior: stacked or scroll, depending on layout

dependencies.text: Tiered discounts need a new discount logic (e.g. quantity-based automatic discounts or a Shopify Function) so the cart gets the right quantity at the right price. For combination or bundle products, the selection may need to target a defined parent product block. The sections are shared across themes (Sectionfy), so the cart and variant integration needs per-theme adjustment (est. 2–3 h each). The variant-styling route needs variants named after quantities and an existing theme variant selector. The reference themes appear to use variants and not a true quantity field.

name: PDP Bulletpoints (USP List with Custom Icons)
status: Built — launched (client-approved; docs written)

what.text: A block in the PDP buy box (main-product) that shows a short list of key benefits or USPs above the fold, near the title, variants and add-to-cart button. Each bullet can use a standard disc, circle or number marker, or a custom icon (SVG or uploaded image, e.g. a green check). The list can be shown plain or inside a box with background, border and rounded corners. Bullet text comes from a product metafield, and individual words can be bold in the examples shown (e.g. 'with **probiotics**').

why.text: Shoppers scan rather than read. Short, scannable benefit bullets close to the price and CTA communicate the core value proposition quickly and cut the effort of reading the description. Check icons act as small reassurances (included extras, free shipping, no damage), which lowers perceived risk. Bolding key terms guides the eye to the strongest selling points. Product-specific bullets keep the message relevant.

how.text:
1) In main-product.liquid, add the schema block 'cro_bulletpoints' (limit 1) with settings for spacing, border, colors, list style, SVG/image icon and font sizes. 2) Create the snippet ed-cro-bulletpoints.liquid, which loops over the metafield list values and renders a
    with optional icon spans and

    text, using CSS variables for colors. 3) In product-form.liquid, add a `when 'cro_bulletpoints'` case that renders the snippet. 4) Create the product metafield definition 'CRO | PDP | Bulletpoints' with key standard.cro_pdp_bulletpoints (Single line text, list of values). 5) In the theme editor, add the block to the product template, position it below the variant picker, and fill the metafield per product. Note: the snippet falls back to theme colors when color settings are left transparent. Known code issues: the media query is written `max-with` (typo, so the mobile font size never applies) and the setting key `icon_margin_rigght` is misspelled.

name: Cart Promo Banner (Quantity Upsell)
status: Built — launched (Focal theme; tested by Chris, KVA approved)

what.text: A configurable promo banner shown under each cart line item in the cart drawer (originally also meant for the cart page). Example copy: "Order 2 and get an extra 10% off!". The banner only appears while the line item quantity is below a configurable threshold. Per comments, clicking it raises the quantity to the threshold and automatically applies a discount code, as in the Hundpur reference. The banner's text, icon, colors, corner style and alignment are all editable.

why.text: It puts a quantity-based incentive right where the buyer is reviewing the item, which encourages multi-unit purchases and raises AOV and units per order. The clear benefit (10% off) works as a discount anchor, and a single click to claim it removes friction. Because it disappears once the threshold is reached, it is not shown to customers who have already qualified.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet cart-promo-banner.liquid. It outputs a div with data-qty and data-line attributes, the icon and the rich text, plus CSS driven by theme settings (flex layout, 13px bold text, 5px padding, optional 4px radius, centered or left alignment, hover background). 2) In the cart drawer section (mini-cart.liquid), render the snippet inside the line item loop only when `line_item.quantity < settings.cart_promo_quantity`. 3) Add a 'Cart Promo Banner' group to settings_schema.json with these settings: quantity, richtext text, html icon, text color, background color, hover background color, border style and text align. 4) Create a quantity-based automatic or code discount in Shopify admin (for example 2+ units gets 10% off). 5) Add JS so that clicking the banner updates the line quantity to the threshold and applies the discount code. This JS is not in the code file and was shown only in a video. The build is Focal-specific, so cart code must be adapted for other themes.

items: Quantity threshold (banner shows while line quantity is below it; default 2)
Text (rich text; default 'Bestelle 2 und erhalte 10% Rabatt extra!')

Requires a Shopify quantity-based discount (automatic or code) set up in admin, since the discount logic lives in Shopify discounts and not in the banner. The cart-drawer click-to-add and apply-discount JS is not in the supplied code, only referenced in comments and a video. The build targets the Focal theme, so other themes need adapted cart code. Settings live in global theme settings rather than a section, and the team asked for a separate 'Cart – Promo Banner' settings entry. A comment also says the banner was once not showing in the cart (resolved via Loom video).

name: PDP Sticky Add-to-Cart Bar
status: Built — launched (theme-specific integration still required)

what.text: A sticky add-to-cart bar on the product page. It shows the product image, title, price (with compare-at price and a 'You save X' badge) and variant selectors (color swatches or dropdowns), plus an Add to Cart button. It stays hidden until the buy box's own ATC button has scrolled out of view. On mobile it is fixed to the bottom of the screen. On desktop (1000px and wider) it sits directly below the header.

why.text: Keeps the primary call to action in reach during long product pages, so shoppers don't have to scroll back up to buy. Showing price, savings and variant choice in the bar keeps the key purchase information in view and cuts friction on mobile. Showing it only after the main button leaves the viewport avoids a redundant duplicate CTA.

how.text: 1) Add a 'Sticky Add to Cart' header and four checkboxes to the schema of the product section (main-product.liquid): enable, show title, show price, show variant selectors. 2) Inside the section, render the 'sticky-atc-button' snippet when the setting is on and the product is available. 3) Create the snippet sticky-atc-button.liquid with the markup, CSS and JS. The bar is hidden via CSS transform. An IntersectionObserver on the buy-box ATC button toggles the .active class once that button is out of view. The JS uses the product variants JSON to resolve the selected option combination, updates price, image and button state, and submits via AJAX to the cart. Header height is measured to position the bar on desktop. The variant:changed event handling must be adapted to each theme's variant-change logic. Written independently of the Focal theme, since the original Elbdev code was Focal-specific and not portable.

items: Enable/disable sticky add to cart on the PDP
Code constants to adapt: header selector, payment container ID, 'You save' label text, and the color swatch config setting

dependencies.text: Needs a product section (main-product.liquid or equivalent) in which to add the schema settings and the render call. The snippet assumes a product form with ID 'product-form-{section.id}-{product.id}', a header element selector, and theme translation keys product.form.add_to_cart and product.form.sold_out. It optionally uses the theme settings color_swatch_config, currency_code_enabled and icon_stroke_width, plus a 'color-swatch-style' snippet. Variant-change event hooks must be adapted per theme. The JS shown in the source is truncated, so the AJAX add-to-cart and variant URL sync logic could not be verified. The first developer struggled with AJAX add-to-cart and variant ID/URL switching. name: Cart Store Benefits (Icon + Text USP Strip with Optional Slider)
status: Built — launched (tested by 3 reviewers, KVA approved)

what.text: A configurable Store Benefits section for the cart (cart page or mini-cart) that shows up to 4 USPs, each with an icon or logo image/SVG and text (for example free shipping from €35, 100-day returns, free spare-parts service, pay on invoice in 30 days with Klarna). It has two display styles. 'Normal' shows a static grid of benefits. 'Slider' shows a row of tappable icons, and tapping one reveals that benefit's headline and longer description underneath. The active icon can be swapped for a second 'active' icon or SVG. Text can be omitted entirely, so the section also works as a logo strip such as payment or brand logos. Benefits can be placed under the checkout button and made sticky or scrolling together with it.

why.text: The cart is the last point of doubt before checkout. Showing risk reducers (free shipping threshold, long return window, pay-later option) right next to the checkout button tackles the typical objections of shipping cost, fear of being stuck with the purchase and payment friction at the moment of decision. Icons make the USPs quick to scan. The slider lets you add more detail without pushing the checkout button down the page.

how.text: Built as a theme-settings-driven snippet 'store-benefits' (Liquid, CSS and a small JS click handler) plus a render call placed where the block should appear (cart template or mini-cart). Settings are exposed in Theme settings > Store Benefits. 'Normal' style renders a CSS grid of benefit items (icon + text). 'Slider' style renders a header row of icons with an underlined active state, and a content area that shows the headline and description of the active benefit. A click handler toggles the 'active' class. Per-benefit icon can be an uploaded image or pasted SVG (SVG overrides the image), with an optional separate active icon. The code is delivered as install instructions: step 1 creates the snippet, step 2 adds the render call. The ticket notes that the instructions must be made theme-independent (not every theme has main-product.liquid) and clear for non-experts. For sticky or scrolling behaviour, the benefits sit under the checkout button and scroll with it. This is handled via the separate 'CRO | Cart | Sticky and Scrolling Settings' element.

Theme settings schema entries (settings_schema.json) for all store-benefit settings, e.g. enable_store_benefits, store_benefits_style, benefit_svg_N, benefit_png_N, benefit_texte_N. The code uses the legacy img_url filter and lazyload classes, so the theme must support lazysizes or it falls back to plain images. name: Highlight Guarantees (Guarantee Card with Social-Proof Footer Bar)
status: Built — delivered; docs revised for non-developer install (Oct 2025)

what.text: A product-page block that renders a card directly under the buy buttons. It has an optional team or founder image (top, left or right), a bold guarantee headline (e.g. '365-day money-back guarantee!'), a short supporting quote or text, and a colored footer bar. The footer bar has a social-proof figure on the left (e.g. '300,000 happy customers') and an underlined link on the right (e.g. 'View reviews').

why.text: Placed right next to the add-to-cart button, the guarantee removes purchase risk at the moment of decision. A real human photo and a founder quote make the promise feel personal and credible. The customer count and review link add social proof and let hesitant buyers verify the claim. Combining risk reversal and social proof in one compact card boosts trust without pushing the buy box down much.

how.text: Build it as a theme block (type 'cro_highlight_guarantees', limit 1) in the product section schema. Steps: (0) duplicate the theme; (1) paste the block JSON into the 'blocks' list in the schema of sections/main-product.liquid (or the theme equivalent); (2) create the snippet cro_highlight_guarantees.liquid with the CSS and markup (thumbnail, main with heading and content, footer with text and link); (3) add a 'case block.type' loop to snippets/product-form.liquid that renders the snippet. Then add the 'CRO | Highlight GTD' block in the theme editor below Buy buttons. With image position left or right, the layout switches to a side-by-side flex layout and the footer stacks vertically. With position top, the image sits above the text and the footer shows text and link side by side.

Heading (inline rich text) and heading size 14–26px (default 20)
Footer: text size, text color (default #ffffff), background color (default #8782B9), left text, link text, link URL, open in new tab

dependencies.text: Needs a theme with a product section that supports blocks (e.g. main-product.liquid) and a product form snippet where blocks are rendered, plus edit access to the theme code. No app or metafields required. The block is limited to one per section. Uses a theme-level settings.text_color fallback, which may need adapting on themes without it. The original ticket asked for a standalone section with desktop/mobile images, alt text, font controls and a hide toggle, but the delivered build is a PDP block with the settings listed above. name: Cart Stock Availability Meter
status: Built — cart/cart drawer only; PDP version split into a separate ticket

what.text: A compact stock-availability bar shown under each cart line item (cart drawer and cart page). It shows the remaining stock of the variant as text (e.g. "Noch 8 auf Lager") plus a progress bar whose fill is the share of remaining stock relative to an 'original quantity'. Two layouts exist: Default (a pill with text on the left and a thin bar on the right) and Classic (a boxed card with the title 'Verfügbarkeit', the subtitle 'Nur solange der Vorrat reicht!' and a bar with the text 'Nur noch X% verfügbar' inside it). It only renders for variants with Shopify-tracked inventory and stock > 0.

why.text: Scarcity and loss aversion: a visibly shrinking bar and a concrete 'only X left' message make the buyer feel the product could sell out. This nudges them to complete checkout instead of postponing. Showing it at the cart stage reinforces the decision just before purchase. The visual bar is processed faster than text alone.

how.text: 1) Create the snippet `ed_cro_stock_availability`. It reads `variant.inventory_quantity` and the variant metafield `standard.cro_original_quantity` (falls back to 100 if empty), computes percent = stock*100/original (capped at 100), and renders the Default or Classic markup. It only renders if stock > 0 and `inventory_management == 'shopify'`. 2) Paste a settings block into `config/settings_schema.json` (checkbox, colors, layout select, text fields). 3) Create the variant metafield 'CRO | Original Quantity' (integer, min 0). 4) Add `{% render 'ed_cro_stock_availability', line_item: line_item %}`, wrapped in `settings.show_cro_stock_availability`, inside the line-item loop of the cart drawer and cart page files. 5) Customize in the Theme Editor and test on desktop and mobile. On mobile the Default layout wraps, so the bar sits full-width below the text. Numbers from 1,000 to 9,999 are formatted with a comma separator.

items: Default layout: text before stock (default "Noch") and text after stock (default "auf Lager"), as inline richtext so bold/italic/underline are possible
Classic layout: title, subtitle, text before and after the percentage (inline richtext)
Per variant: 'CRO | Original Quantity' metafield defines the reference quantity (100% bar length)

dependencies.text: Variant metafield `standard.cro_original_quantity` (Integer). Variant inventory tracked by Shopify (`inventory_management == 'shopify'`). Edit access to the code (new snippet, `config/settings_schema.json`, and the cart/cart-drawer line-item loop). Settings are global theme settings, not a section, because the snippet runs inside the cart loop where section settings are not available. The original ticket asked for a standalone section with separate font size, bold and underline settings, but the build uses theme settings and richtext. Not built for the PDP: variant switching would need extra JS and a separate layout, so a new ticket was agreed.

name: PDP Highlighted Discount Code Block (Copy-to-Clipboard)
status: Built — launched (simple clipboard version; auto-apply version planned as a separate ticket)

what.text: A card in the product-info area that highlights a discount code. It shows a headline such as "-20% with the code", a copy-to-clipboard button labelled with the code (e.g. ESN), and a short body text (e.g. an additional quantity discount and a hint to redeem the code in the cart). It also shows the calculated discounted price in an accent color next to the struck-through original price, and an optional "Learn more" link.

why.text: Showing the price after the code turns an abstract coupon into a concrete saving. The strikethrough original price adds price anchoring and a visible reference point. One-click copy removes the friction of remembering or typing the code, which reduces coupon-hunting drop-off. Putting the offer on the PDP, before add-to-cart, raises perceived value at the decision point. The quantity-discount hint nudges a larger basket (AOV).

how.text: Build it as a theme block inside the main product section so it can be positioned freely among the other product-info blocks. Three steps: (1) add the block schema (type highlight_discount) to the blocks of the product section schema; (2) create the snippet highlight-discount.liquid, which renders the card, the CSS, and a small JS clipboard handler; (3) add a `{% when 'highlight_discount' %}` case to the product form's block-type switch that renders the snippet. The discounted price is calculated in Liquid as the selected_or_first_available_variant price minus the configured discount percentage. The block renders only if a discount code is entered. The user clicks the button, the code is copied with navigator.clipboard, and a tooltip ("Code copied!") shows for 3 seconds. The shopper then pastes the code in the cart or checkout voucher field. For a product-specific code, link the discount code field to a product metafield, so the block appears only on products that have a value. Note that the code is not applied automatically.

items: Device display: desktop only / mobile only / both
Discount code (text; blank = block hidden; can be bound to a product metafield for product-specific codes)
Body text (richtext, e.g. quantity discount or redeem hint)
Learn more link text (blank = link hidden)

dependencies.text: Shopify theme with a product section that supports blocks (main-product.liquid and product-form.liquid in the reference theme; file names vary by theme). The discount code must already exist in Shopify admin. Optional product metafield for product-specific codes. The percentage entered must match the real discount in Shopify, since the displayed price is only calculated, not read from the discount. Code is not applied automatically; an auto-apply variant would need cart/drawer integration and was split into a separate ticket. Positioning (above/below/next to the product) is handled by block order in the theme editor. The original ticket also requested options not in the delivered code: scheduling, customer-segment targeting, collection targeting, multilingual input, and a separate quantity-discount toggle. Installation docs were still being clarified for non-expert users.
