name: Social Proof | Social Media Gallery (UGC Slider/Stack with Shoppable Cart Icon)
status: Built — launched (tested internally by Kian: yes)

what.text: A standalone Shopify section that shows a community/UGC gallery of customer photos with Instagram handles. It has a headline (with optional highlighted/underlined word) and a subheadline. Two layouts are available: a horizontal Slider (arrows, scrollbar, optional pagination dots, caption bar with @handle under each image) and a Stack grid (multiple images per row). In the Stack layout, images that have linked products show a small cart icon with the product count at the bottom-left. Clicking it opens a modal listing the linked products (image, name, vendor, price, default variant, 'Show product' button to the PDP). Nothing is added to the cart directly. Instagram handles are displayed as text and, per the request, the link can be non-clickable so shoppers are not sent away from the store.

why.text: Real customer photos act as social proof: a large community number ('1.4 million community') and real people using the product reduce uncertainty and build belonging. Handles under images add authenticity. The shoppable cart icon turns inspiration into discovery by letting shoppers see which products are worn in a photo and jump straight to the PDP, shortening the path from inspiration to purchase. Keeping the handles non-clickable avoids leaking traffic to Instagram.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-social-gallery.liquid and two snippets (ed-cro-social-gallery-slider and ed-cro-social-gallery-stack). The section has 'heading' and 'content' blocks (font, color, size, alignment, max width, spacing for desktop/mobile, optional highlighted word with SVG underline). A 'layout_style' select (stack/slider) renders only the relevant snippet, so only the slider or stack JS loads, which improves page speed. Each image block holds the image, Instagram handle, and linked products. Configure the layout, items per row (desktop/mobile), gap, corner radius, caption and arrow colors, scrollbar, pagination and modal options in the theme customizer. Colors default to transparent (rgba(0,0,0,0)) to fall back to global theme settings.

name: PDP Product Gallery Slider with Video
status: Built — delivered (code + setup doc); feedback on install instructions in Oct 2025

what.text: A custom PDP media gallery built as a Swiper slider. Product images and videos sit side by side as horizontal slides: 2 per view on desktop (>=1024px) and 1 per view on mobile. Navigation is an arrow on desktop, swipe on mobile, and thin dash/bar pagination below the slides. Videos are embedded in the slider and take the same space as the images. Native product videos get custom play/pause and fullscreen buttons at the bottom right. External (YouTube/Vimeo) videos show a poster with a play button. 3D models are supported. An optional round 'featured video' thumbnail with a play icon sits at the top right of the gallery and opens a fullscreen video popup (driven by the 'Featured video' and 'Featured video thumbnail' product metafields). The popup is hidden if the metafields are empty.

why.text: Showing several product images next to each other, including a video, lets shoppers see the product from more angles and in motion without extra clicks. This reduces uncertainty about fit, fabric and look, which is especially useful for apparel like jackets, and it lowers the return/doubt barrier before add-to-cart. A video thumbnail that stands out in the corner draws attention to rich content that many shoppers would otherwise miss. Pagination bars and arrows signal that there is more to explore and encourage interaction. Layout consistency between image and video slides avoids jarring jumps.

how.text: 1) Duplicate the theme first. 2) Create the snippet 'ed-product-image-with-video.liquid' and paste the provided code (CSS, Liquid loop over product.media, Swiper init, custom video-control JS). 3) In theme.liquid, add the Swiper 11 CSS and JS from the jsDelivr CDN in the head. 4) In main-product.liquid, comment out the existing media HTML and add {%- render 'ed-product-image-with-video', product: product, section: section -%}. 5) Add product videos/images in the product media in Shopify admin; the slide order follows the media order (drag and drop). 6) Optionally, fill the 'Featured video' (file) and 'Featured video thumbnail' (image) product metafields to show the round popup trigger. The build works with any theme because it uses its own code. Autoplay can be disabled via a theme customizer option (per the developer). Note: the code as shown sets native video to autoplay + loop with no native controls, while the acceptance criteria asked for no autoplay, so check this when configuring. The developer's comment says the option exists.

items: Slides per view: 1 on mobile, 2 on desktop (>=1024px)
Slide order: drag and drop of product media in Shopify admin
Video autoplay on/off (theme customizer option, per developer comment; external video uses the section setting 'enable_video_autoplay')
Video looping (section setting for external videos)
Featured video metafield (file): the video for the popup
Featured video thumbnail metafield (image): round thumbnail with play icon at the top right
Pagination style: dash bullets (a scrollbar option is commented out in code)

dependencies.text: Swiper 11 (CSS + JS via CDN, added to theme.liquid), the snippet ed-product-image-with-video.liquid, and an edit of the theme's main-product.liquid (file name varies by theme). Product metafields 'standard.featured_video' and 'standard.featured_video_thumbnail'. name: Shop-the-Look Hotspots in PDP Gallery Image
status: Built — delivered (documentation and product image requested)

what.text: A cross-sell module placed inside the PDP image gallery. One gallery slide shows a model image with up to 5 round white hotspot dots over the clothing and accessories. On hover (desktop) or tap (mobile), a black preview card opens next to the dot. It shows the product thumbnail, name (truncated), a short description, and the price (sale price if discounted). The whole card links to that product's page. Nothing is added to the cart automatically. The slide is inserted at a configurable position (1–4) in the product media swiper.

why.text: Shoppers see the outfit on a model and can discover matching items in context, without leaving the image or searching. This is a shop-the-look pattern that raises AOV and items per order by turning inspiration into low-friction cross-sell. The preview shows price and name up front, so the click-through is informed. Linking to the product page (not auto add-to-cart) keeps the user in control and avoids pushy behaviour. The last hotspot's card is open by default, which acts as a visual cue that the dots are interactive.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add a schema block 'CRO | Crosssale in Image' (type cro_crosssale_items, limit 1) with settings: slide position (range 1–4), an image picker, and up to 5 items. Each item has a product picker plus top % and left % position fields. 2) Create the snippet ed_cro_cross_sale_in_product_image.liquid. It renders the image in a swiper-slide wrapper with absolutely positioned hotspot dots (white 14px dot with a translucent halo that darkens on hover). Each dot has a black card (50px thumbnail, title truncated to 18 characters, description truncated to 48 characters, price, compare-at handling) linking to item_product.url. Inline JS toggles a 'visible' class on mouseenter of a dot. It shows only one card at a time and resets to the last item when the mouse leaves the image. On mobile the card is offset below the dot. 3) Create the snippet ed-product-image-with-video.liquid. It loops product.media in a Swiper gallery and, before each media item, renders the cross-sale snippet if the block's crosssale_position equals the media index and an image is set. Each cross-sale product's coordinates are entered manually as percentages in the theme editor. The setup was recorded in a walkthrough video.

items: Hotspot styling, info-box position (top/bottom/left/right) and offset, and hotspot title/description overrides were requested in the acceptance criteria. The delivered code only has CSS-fixed styling, the product's own title/description, and automatic placement (right on desktop, below on mobile)

dependencies.text: Shopify theme with a main-product section and a Swiper-based product gallery (custom ed-product-image-with-video snippet, theme-specific classes). Cross-sale products are chosen via product settings and positioned with percentage coordinates per item. Tied to a specific theme (dopesnow/Sectionfy). The ticket comments describe the configuration as complex, with a unique value per cross-sale product. The product image is needed for documentation.

name: PDP Anchor-Link Navigation for Product Details (Expanded Content, Scroll-to-Section)
status: Reference only — spec from a single ticket line with a live example URL; build status unknown

what.text: A navigation on the product page that links to anchor points for the product detail sections (e.g. description, features, materials, size guide). Nothing is collapsed into an accordion or tab. All content stays fully visible on the page, and clicking a nav item scrolls the page down to the matching section. The ticket gives a live example on the dopesnow.com product page for the Blizzard Full-Zip Snowboard Jacket (men's, black).

why.text: Content that is already open removes the click-and-reveal effort that accordions add, so shoppers see the product information (specs, benefits, sizing) without having to hunt for it. The anchor nav gives a quick overview of what is on the page and lets shoppers jump straight to what matters to them, such as fit or material. This reduces friction and uncertainty on long PDPs, and fully visible text also helps content discoverability and SEO. This reasoning is my inference; the ticket does not state it.

how.text: Add a nav row (links or tabs) near the product info or the start of the details area. Each link points to an element id on a content section (href='#section-id'). All detail sections are rendered open, with no accordion or tab collapse. Use smooth scrolling (CSS scroll-behavior: smooth or a small JS handler) and a scroll-margin-top or offset so the target is not hidden under a sticky header. Optionally make the nav sticky and highlight the active section while scrolling. The ticket only states the behavior (no collapsing, scroll to anchor); the implementation details are inferred.

name: Multi-Level Mega Menu with Image Thumbnails (Desktop + Mobile Drawer)
status: Design reference provided — build status not stated

what.text: A header navigation mega menu that supports deep category trees (4 or 5 levels). On desktop, a left rail lists top-level categories (some with a '+' expander, plus 'Brandneu', 'Sale', 'Renewed' and a bold 'Show all for men >' link). Next to it, columns show subcategories with round product thumbnails, and some entries have a '+' to drill down further. On mobile, it is a full-height drawer with a close (X) button. It lists the main categories as rounded cards with a thumbnail and a bold label, an 'All lights →' link, secondary links (Sustainability, About us, FAQ, Contact) as arrow rows, and a language selector at the bottom.

why.text: Visual thumbnails and clear hierarchy let shoppers recognise categories faster than with text-only lists. That lowers cognitive load and shortens the path to the right collection. Surfacing promo categories (New, Sale, Renewed) in the top rail draws attention to high-intent and discounted ranges. The deep tree keeps large catalogues browsable without crowding the page. On mobile, big tap targets, thumbnails and a clean list reduce mis-taps and bounce.

how.text: Build a custom header/navigation section in the theme that reads a Shopify menu (Online Store > Navigation) with up to 4–5 nested levels. Shopify's native menus allow at most 3 levels, so deeper levels need a workaround, e.g. a metaobject/metafield-driven menu structure or an app. Per link, add an image (collection image or a metafield/metaobject thumbnail). Desktop: a left column for level 1; on hover or click, render level 2 in a multi-column grid with round thumbnails; show a '+' on items that have children and expand level 3+ via a flyout or accordion. Add a 'View all' link for each top-level item. Mobile: a drawer with an X close button, level-1 items as image cards, tap-to-drill-down for deeper levels, secondary links and a language/market selector in the footer of the drawer. Design reference is in Figma (Lumiere Design | A/B Testing); Dopesnow.de is the live reference.

name: Cost Transparency (Price Breakdown) Section
status: Built — QA passed, documented

what.text: A configurable Shopify section called 'CRO | Kostentransparenz' that explains how the price is made up. A headline and sub-headline sit above a row of round or rounded-square images. Each image carries a bold percentage and a label, e.g. '45% Development & Production', '25% Staff', '20% Sales', '10% Profit'. Below that is a text block with its own headline, copy and an optional image or badge. The final build has two blocks, left and right. The left block is the cost breakdown. The right block reuses the same image row and adds a size/serving chart with up to 5 rows (icon, title, package images, amount). If only one block is active it stretches to 100% width. why.text: Customers often object to a high price. Showing what the money pays for (ingredients, people, sales, profit) makes the price feel fair and justified. A closing 'promise' text and a badge or award add credibility. The effect should be strongest on premium-priced products.

why.text: Social proof placed right next to the purchase decision lets shoppers see real customer voices without scrolling to the review section lower on the page. Hand-picking the best reviews per product (with a short headline and a star rating) lets the team highlight the objections and benefits that matter most. This reduces perceived risk at the moment of the add-to-cart decision. A swipeable carousel keeps the block compact so it does not push the CTA down the page.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add a new block schema 'CRO | Review Spotlight' (type cro_review_spotlight, limit 1) with the settings below. 2) Create the snippet/section cro_review_spotlight.liquid. It reads the product metafield standard.cro_pdp_review_spotlight, loops over 1..10, and renders a slide only when the title_N field is not blank. Each slide shows filled stars (rating_N) plus empty stars (5 minus rating) using the theme's 'rating-star' icon, then the title and content. Slides are wrapped in the theme's <flickity-carousel> with a config built from the block settings (adaptiveHeight, draggable, fade, autoPlay, pageDots, wrapAround, no prev/next buttons). Styling is injected via a <style> tag using the block settings. 3) In product-form.liquid, add a `when 'cro_review_spotlight'` case that renders the snippet with product and block. 4) In Shopify admin, create a Metaobject definition 'CRO | Review Spotlight' (type cro_review_spotlight) with a Name field (display name) and 10 sets of Rating N (integer 1–5), Title N (single-line text) and Content N (multi-line text). 5) Create a product metafield definition 'CRO | PDP | Review Spotlight' (standard.cro_pdp_review_spotlight, Mixed reference, limited to the metaobject, one entry). 6) Per product, create a metaobject entry with the reviews and assign it to the metafield. Then add the block in the theme editor.

name: PDP Product Attributes (Rating Slider Bars)
status: Built — launched (reviewed by team; installation guide rewritten for non-developers in Oct 2025)

what.text: A block on the product page (placed below the add-to-cart / payment icons) that shows a headline such as 'What our customers say', followed by a grey rounded panel with up to 3 attribute rows. Each row has a title (e.g. Quality, Durability, Load capacity), a white horizontal bar with a small dark pill marker positioned by a 0–100 value, and 2 or 3 labels beneath the bar (e.g. 'not good / good / very good' or 'short-lived / long-lasting'). Content is maintained per product through a metaobject linked via a product metafield. Styling is controlled in the theme editor.

why.text: Rating-scale visuals turn product qualities into quick, scannable proof. A marker near the 'very good' end gives an at-a-glance signal of quality, durability and strength. This reduces uncertainty at the moment of purchase and supports the value claim without long copy. Placing it near the CTA keeps reassurance close to the decision point. Because the content is per product, the comparison feels specific rather than generic. Caveat: the scores are self-declared, so credibility depends on honest values.

how.text: 1) In Shopify admin, create a metaobject definition 'CRO | Product Attributes' (type cro_product_attributes). Fields: Name (display name, required), Heading, Title 01–03 (single line text), Progress 01–03 (integer, 0–100), Attributes 01–03 (list of single line text, 2 or 3 labels). 2) Create a product metafield 'CRO | PDP | Product attributes' (standard.cro_product_attributes), type Mixed reference, referencing that metaobject, with storefront access set to Read. 3) Add the snippet ed-cro-product-attributes.liquid, which renders only if the metafield exists. It loops over items 1–3, renders a title only if one is set, and positions the marker with left:calc(progress% - marker width). The marker is 24px wide on desktop and 16px on mobile, so 100 does not overflow the track. A label list with 2 entries is pinned left/right and one with 3 is pinned left/centre/right. 3) Paste the block JSON ('CRO | Product Attributes', limit 1) into the blocks array of the main-product section schema, and render the snippet in that section. 4) Fill in an entry and assign it to each product. Products without the metafield show nothing.

name: Homepage Featured Collection (Bestsellers Slider with Filter Tags, Quick ATC & Variant Swatches)
status: Spec written; dev raised theme-conflict concern (custom section vs. customizing the theme's native featured collection) — decision pending, no launch confirmed

what.text: A homepage section that showcases products from one or more Shopify collections (e.g. "Unsere Bestseller" / Our Bestsellers). It has a headline, optional subheadline and body text, and clickable filter tags above the products (e.g. Pendelleuchte, Stehleuchte, Deckenleuchte, Akkuleuchte). Product cards show an image, a discount badge ("-20%" on mobile, "Bis 50,00€ Ersparnis" (up to €50 savings) on desktop), a quick add-to-cart basket button on the image (mobile), the product name, the price with the strike-through original price ("ab 119,90€" next to "149,90€"), and color-variant swatches. Products display as a horizontal slider with a progress bar and arrows (desktop), plus an "Alle anzeigen" (View all) link. The ticket also asks for Grid and Pagination display modes.

why.text: Bringing bestsellers to the homepage shortens the path to product pages for visitors who aren't yet sure what they want. Category filter tags let shoppers self-select quickly, which reduces browsing effort. Visible discount badges and strike-through prices anchor value and create a sense of a deal. Color swatches and a quick ATC button remove clicks between interest and cart. The bestseller framing acts as implicit social proof.

how.text: Ticket asks for a custom Shopify section with theme-editor settings for typography, colors, collection selection, filter tags, product card display, product count and layout (grid/slider/pagination). The developer (Rana) warned that variant switching with thumbnail updates, Ajax ATC and Quick View are tied to the theme's native code, and a fully custom section could break them. Recommended approach from dev: customize the theme's default featured-collection section to match the design rather than build from scratch. Final decision is not documented in the ticket. Build tip: reuse the theme's product-card snippet so swatches, Ajax ATC and Quick View keep working; implement filter tags as tabs that swap between collections or collection-tag filters; add a discount badge computed from compare_at_price.

Add-to-cart button directly in the grid
Product name: font, size, bold, alignment
Price: font, size, color, bold, alignment, currency symbol
Percentage discount badge (when a compare-at price exists)

name: PDP UGC Customer Photo Carousel (Product Block)
status: Built — launched (setup guide + video documented)

what.text: A product-page block that shows a swipeable carousel of 1–5 customer photo cards (UGC). Each card has a rounded thumbnail with a dark gradient at the bottom. Over the gradient sit a round reviewer avatar, a star rating, the reviewer name (e.g. "Jennifer M.") and a smaller time label (e.g. "Vor 3 Monaten"). An optional centered headline sits above the carousel ("Das sagen unsere Kund*innen"). The block can render as a normal block or inside a collapsible accordion (the screenshot shows it under a "Rückgabe" collapsible, next to the add-to-cart button). Content is stored per product in a metaobject, which is referenced by a product metafield.

why.text: Real customer photos in a real setting are credible social proof. They show the product in use and reduce purchase uncertainty. Placing them next to the add-to-cart button puts the proof at the decision point. Name, star rating and recency ("3 months ago") make the reviews feel authentic. The swipeable carousel keeps the block compact on mobile and invites interaction.

how.text: 1) Create the metaobject definition "CRO | UGC Section" (type cro_ugc_section). Fields: name, collapsible/button title, feedback title, and for each of 5 slots a thumbnail (file), avatar (file), rating (number), name (text) and label (text). 2) Create a product metafield "CRO | UGC Section" as a Mixed reference limited to that metaobject, with Storefront API access enabled. 3) In the product section's {% schema %}, add the block "CRO | UGC Section" (type cro_ugc_section, limit 1) to the blocks[] array, inside the brackets and with a comma if it follows another block. 4) Create the snippet cro_ugc_section.liquid. It reads the product metafield, outputs scoped CSS from the block settings, builds a Flickity config, loops over slots 1–5 and renders only slots that have a thumbnail. It wraps the content in a collapsible when layout = collapsible. 5) Render the snippet from the product section's block loop. 6) For each product, create a metaobject entry, upload the photos and avatars, and assign it to the product. Ticket note: the instructions had to be rewritten step by step so non-developers can follow them regardless of theme (not every theme has main-product.liquid), and a setup video exists.

name: Compare Section (Static Product Comparison Table)
status: Built — launched (documented; a later comment says another ticket has near-identical acceptance criteria, so it may be a duplicate)

what.text: A Shopify section that shows 2–4 shop-owner-selected products side by side in a comparison table. Each product column has an image, title, price (optional), color swatches, and a 'Zum Produkt' (view product) button. Below the products, a table has editor-defined row labels (e.g. Dimensions, Price, Wood type) with a comparison value per product. Values come from product metafields or are typed in manually. Headline and sub-headline are optional blocks above the table, and the table can be collapsed behind an 'Alles einblenden' (show all) toggle. The shopper cannot choose products to compare; the merchant curates them.

why.text: Side-by-side comparison lowers choice overload and cognitive effort. Shoppers can see the differences in specs and price at a glance, which reduces the need to open several tabs or leave the page. A clear 'view product' CTA on each column sends the undecided shopper to the best-fit item. The table also works as cross-sell and upsell, since it puts higher-priced alternatives next to the current product.

how.text: Add the section file ed-cro-compare-section.liquid. Section-level settings cover background color, text color and spacing for desktop and mobile, an optional max width, table background color and table corner radius. Content is built from blocks: heading, subheading, content (rich text), button, and 'item' blocks, one per product. The number of products equals the number of item blocks (2–4). In each item block the merchant picks a shop product and toggles the price. Row names are entered as rich text that supports bold, italic and underline. For each row, the comparison value is either read from a product metafield or entered manually per product, and both modes are supported. Typography is controlled through CSS custom properties set per block (font family, size, line-height, letter-spacing, alignment, text transform, spacing). Separate mobile values are available. Button colors can be customized. The mobile layout keeps the 2-column table with a collapse toggle.

items: Table background color and corner radius
Section padding top/bottom/left/right, separate for desktop and mobile
Heading block: rich text (bold/italic/underline), custom font, size, line-height, letter-spacing, alignment, transform, spacing, max width; separate mobile values
Subheading block: same typography controls, with mobile overrides
Content block: rich text with typography controls
Button block: text color, background color, text transform
Product item blocks: 2, 3 or 4 products selected from the shop
Row names with rich text formatting
Comparison values: product metafield or manual entry per product

dependencies.text: Theme assumed to be the Impact theme: the code uses its global settings (settings.heading_color, settings.background) and its .button--primary and .button--secondary classes. Needs product metafields if the metafield mode is used; the ticket marks metafields as required (MF/J). Product swatches, the compare-at price and the 'Alles einblenden' toggle are visible in the screenshots, but their implementation is not confirmed in the truncated code. No app is needed for the static version. A buyer-selected comparison (option 1) was split into a separate ticket and would likely need an app.

items: Click-through rate on the 'Zum Produkt' buttons
Conversion rate of sessions that see the section vs. those that don't
Average order value / share of higher-priced variants chosen
Scroll depth to and engagement with the section
Bounce and exit rate on the page

name: Shop the Look Info (Image Hotspot Section)
status: Built — client-approved, documented (Slite doc + source ZIP)

what.text: A custom Shopify section, "CRO | Shop the Look Info", that shows a large image on a colored or gradient background with a heading, short text and a pill CTA button (e.g. "Learn more"). Pulsing white "+" hotspot dots sit on top of the image. On desktop, clicking a dot opens an info card next to it. On mobile, it opens a bottom-sheet card with a title and short text, and the dot turns into an "x". The section works when duplicated several times on one page.

why.text: Hotspots turn a static lifestyle or product image into something to explore. The pulsing dots invite interaction and let shoppers pick the details that interest them (curiosity and self-directed discovery) without leaving the page. Feature callouts such as materials or benefits are shown at the moment of attention, which builds perceived value before the shopper reaches the product page. The ticket also aims to show products with price, rating and add-to-cart next to the look, which would shorten the path to purchase, but the built version does not do this.

how.text: 1) Create the section file `ed-cro-shop-the-look-info.liquid` and paste in the provided code, which includes inline CSS, Liquid and a small JS modal controller. 2) In the theme editor, add "CRO | Shop the Look Info" to a template. 3) Set the heading, text, button text and link. 4) Upload the desktop image and an optional mobile image. 5) Pick the background color or gradient. 6) Add one "Item" block per hotspot. Enter its heading and text, and set Left % and Top % to place the dot on the image. Desktop shows the card inline next to the dot and toggles it on click. Mobile (≤999px) shows a bottom sheet with an overlay and locks page scroll. The pulse is a CSS keyframe animation on the dot's ::after element. The JS is scoped per section, so duplicates don't conflict.

name: PDP Image Gallery – Infinite Swipe Loop & Configurable Dots

what.text: An enhancement to the product image slider (mobile swipe gallery). (1) Infinite swipe: after the last product photo, the user can keep swiping left and the gallery loops back to the first photo. (2) Pagination dots with a configurable shape (circles or squares) and three definable color states: Active / filled, Inactive / filled, Inactive / outlined only.

why.text: A looping gallery has no dead end, so browsing product images feels continuous and the user is never stopped at the last image. This encourages more image views, and more image engagement usually means more confidence in the product. Dots that match the brand's design language and clearly show the active state improve orientation (where am I, how many images are there). This is mainly a UX polish, so the expected conversion effect is small.

how.text: Enable loop mode in the slider library the theme gallery uses (e.g. a 'loop' or 'rewind' option in Swiper or Flickity) so that swiping past the last slide shows the first. Expose theme settings for dot shape (circle / square) and for the colors of the three states: active (filled), inactive (filled), inactive (outline only). Render the dots with CSS variables driven by those settings. The source does not describe the base gallery or its implementation, so the details are an inference.

dependencies.text: Requires an existing swipeable product image gallery with pagination dots (the 'version 1.0' this ticket extends). The slider library must support looping. No metafields or apps are mentioned.

what.text: A slide-in cart drawer ('Dein Warenkorb') that uses as many existing Sectionfy theme features as possible. Avatars and the '22,000+' count give social proof and bandwagon reassurance. The payment icons and the word 'sicher' (secure) in the CTA reduce payment-risk anxiety. The Figma design also shows a struck-through price with a 'You save €10' badge, which reinforces the value of the deal.

how.text: Build it as a cart-drawer section in the Sectionfy theme and reuse the existing Sectionfy blocks wherever possible: delivery/USP message, free-shipping progress bar, social-proof avatar line, line-item list, sticky checkout footer and payment-icon row. Order the blocks as in the screenshot. Put the delivery message and progress bar at the top, below the header and above the items. Keep the footer with totals and CTA pinned to the bottom of the drawer. Style the progress box in a warm brand accent colour and the CTA in a dark, high-contrast colour. The Figma 'Finale Variante' is the reference design. The compare-at price and 'Du sparst X€' badge appear only in Figma, not in the built preview.

what.text: A swipeable or arrow-driven image slider inside each product card on the collection page. Shoppers can flip through several images of a product without opening the product page. why.text: Shoppers see several views of a product (angles, details, context) right in the grid. This gives a faster, more intuitive preview and reduces the effort of evaluating items. Known pitfalls from the comments: (1) the slider did not initialise properly in the test theme and needed a fix; (2) on first page load the images rendered incorrectly until a manual reload, which was later fixed, so test first-load rendering in QA; (3) the theme contained an Ablyft script, so confirm the correct Ablyft customer account before launch. why.text: Hypothesis from the ticket: if the PDP offers a product video, conversion rate rises because customers can experience the product better. name: Cart Gift Wrap Upsell
status: Built — A/B test set up in Ablyft (March 2025); result not documented

what.text: An upsell block in the cart (drawer) that offers the shopper a gift-wrapping add-on, shown as an add-to-cart product offer. It uses the Sectionfy.io section 'CRO | Cart | Up-/Cross-Selling'. Products already in the cart are not offered again as upsells.

why.text: Many buyers are willing to pay a little extra for attractive gift packaging, especially when buying for a gift occasion. Showing the offer in the cart, right before checkout, presents it as a low-effort add-on to an order the shopper has already decided on. This raises average order value and revenue per order. Hiding items already in the cart keeps the offer relevant and avoids clutter.

how.text: 1) Install the Sectionfy.io Cart Up-/Cross-Selling section in the cart or cart drawer of the (duplicated) A/B test theme. 2) Configure the gift-wrap product as the upsell item. 3) Exclude any product already in the cart from the upsell list. 4) Make sure the upsell re-renders when the cart changes. On GIVE LOVE the cart theme code could not render Liquid dynamically, which caused three bugs: the upsell did not appear on the first add until the cart was closed and the page reloaded, the list did not update when new items were added, and upsells stayed visible after being added. The developer fixed these. 5) Set up the A/B test in Ablyft with control (no upsell) against the variant (gift-wrap upsell), and check in the first days that KPIs are tracked correctly.

name: Cart Free Gift Progress Bar
status: Built — A/B test set up in Ablyft (Apr 2025); result not documented

what.text: A progress bar in the cart that shows how much more the customer must spend to unlock a free gift. The bar fills as the cart value approaches a configurable minimum amount (100 in the screenshot). The gift product is shown or added once the threshold is reached. The ticket's test compares a cart without the bar against a cart with it.

why.text: A visible progress bar uses the goal-gradient effect: people accelerate as they get closer to a goal. A free gift is a concrete, high-perceived-value reward, and the remaining amount is framed as a small gap to close. This motivates customers to add items and raises AOV. The hypothesis in the ticket says the same: visible progress toward a free reward creates a psychological incentive.

how.text: The section is based on the Sectionfy.io 'CRO | Cart | Shipping-Bar' section. It was first built for the Focal theme and then reworked for the client's different theme in a duplicate theme ('A/B Test (PSY)'). That cart's Liquid does not re-render on cart updates, so the bar needed custom JavaScript hooked into the cart's own JS. This was the main effort. In Theme settings, enable the free item, set a headline and the minimum amount, and pick the gift product. To make the gift free, either duplicate the product at 0.00 and give it the 'hidden' tag so it does not appear elsewhere in the store, or use a conditional automatic discount. Then set up the A/B test (control = no bar, variant = bar) in the testing tool, which was Ablyft, and check KPI tracking in the first days.

name: Sub-Collection Bubble Navigation (Sectionfy)

what.text: A Sectionfy 'Sub-collections' section that shows a row of linked sub-collections or categories as round (or square) image bubbles with a label under each, for example Starter Set, Refill Pack, Fastenzeit 2025 and Bio Gemüsebrühe. It sits directly under the hero and press-logo bar. The ticket (originally titled 'Sub-collection to full width') led to an alignment option (Left / Center) so the items can be centered when only a few are maintained. why.text: Image bubbles give shoppers an immediate, visual way into the main product groups or offers, which cuts clicks and decision effort. Centering a short row keeps it balanced and intentional instead of looking left-heavy or half-empty. That keeps the navigation credible and easy to scan. The seasonal bubble (Fastenzeit 2025) also lets the team promote current offers above the fold.

how.text: Add the 'Sub-collections' section to the template, below the hero and logo bar. Use 'Add Collection' to add one block per sub-collection, each with an image, a label and a link. Set style to 'Show bubbles' and image style to Circle or Square. Set image size (desktop and mobile), font size, text color and gap between items. Set Positioning to Static or Absolute and Alignment to Left or Center. Use Center when only a few items are maintained so the row is centered across the full width. Custom CSS is available for further tweaks.

name: Product Teaser Text (Metafield-Driven Subtitle on Collection Cards & PDP)
status: Built — live; display bug reported Mar 2025 and explained in a Loom (cause not documented in ticket)

what.text: A short, editable one-line teaser text is shown directly under the product title. It appears in the collection grid cards (between title and price) and in the PDP header (between title and price). It is maintained per product in a Rich Text metafield called 'Teaser-Texte' (Teaser texts). Examples seen: 'Das perfekte Produkt für den Start' (The perfect product to get started), 'Nachfüllpack für 6 Riegeltage' (Refill pack for 6 bar days), 'Leckere Ergänzung zu deinen Riegeltagen' (Tasty add-on to your bar days).

why.text: A one-line benefit or use-case message right at the point of decision tells shoppers who the product is for or how it fits their plan (starter, refill, add-on). This reduces the effort of picking between similar bundles and supports cross-sell. It carries the value message into the grid, so shoppers don't need to open the PDP to understand the product. Repeating the same line on the PDP keeps the message consistent. Missing teasers on some cards create visual gaps and uneven cards, which weakens that consistency.

how.text: 1) Create a product metafield 'Teaser-Texte' (type: Rich Text) and fill it in the product admin page. 2) In the theme (Sectionfy section on the collection template and the PDP product-info block), output the metafield below the product title and above the price, only when it is not blank. 3) Render the rich text as inline/short text styled small and regular-weight. 4) QA every product in the collection: if a metafield is filled but nothing appears, check that the section/block reads the correct metafield namespace/key and that the render does not depend on a different condition. The ticket's Loom explains the cause of the original bug, but the details are not captured in the text.

what.text: A fully styleable contact form section for the Shopify theme editor. It has a heading, Name, Email and Message fields, an optional Phone field, and a submit button. why.text: A clear, low-friction contact path reduces uncertainty before purchase. Shoppers with open questions about shipping, sizing or returns can ask instead of abandoning. An approachable form with a friendly image and a visible, on-brand button signals that real people are reachable, which builds trust. Keeping the required fields to email and message minimizes effort. This is an inference: the ticket states no rationale.

how.text: Add the code as a new section file (e.g. cro-contact.liquid). Add it to the contact page template, or to any page via the theme editor. In the editor, set the background, text alignment, optional image and image position, heading text, font, size and color, label styling, input styling, button text, font, size, colors and style (normal, rounded or pill), and whether the phone field shows. The form uses {% form 'contact' %}, so submissions arrive in Shopify's standard customer-message flow. Success and error messages use the theme's translation keys (contact.form.*). On screens up to 768px the layout stacks into one column.

Heading text (default 'Kontaktieren Sie uns'), font, size 16–60px, color

Code-quality notes, inferred from reading the code: the schema defines no heading_style, label_style or input_style settings, though the markup references them. The font_picker values heading_font and label_font are output as CSS classes, which won't apply a font; they need font_face or font_family styles like the input and button fields use. The email field has autocomplete="off", which hurts UX and could be removed. img_url is deprecated in favor of image_url. Schema labels and defaults are in German and need translating or localizing per store.

what.text: A cross-sell block placed directly under the Add to Cart button on the product page. It has a headline ("Passt perfekt dazu" / "Goes perfectly with it") and a social-proof sub-headline ("8 von 10 Kunden kaufen zusätzlich" / "8 out of 10 customers also buy"). Below sit complementary products, each with image, title, price and its own "HINZUFÜGEN" (Add) button. The first version was a one-row carousel with small thumbnails. It became a vertical list, then a 2-column grid with larger images, with title, price and button under each image. The product list is pulled from a product metafield ("Upsell Product Listing") so each PDP can show its own products. Tiles are forced to equal width and height so long titles don't break the grid.

why.text: Shoppers who have just decided to buy are most open to adding complementary items, so showing relevant add-ons near the main CTA lifts AOV with little friction. The "8 out of 10 customers also buy" line adds social proof and normalises the add-on. Larger images, visible prices and one-click add buttons reduce effort and uncertainty. Uniform tile sizes look tidy and trustworthy and keep scanning easy. The stat is a claim to be verified with the customer (see dependencies).

how.text: Build as a section/block in the Sectionfy PDP template, placed below the Add to Cart button. Settings in the theme editor cover headline, sub-headline, product source, text color and background color. Connect the product list to a product-level list metafield ("Upsell Product Listing", type: list of products) via dynamic source so each product shows its own upsell products. Fall back to a manually chosen product list if the metafield is empty. Render a 2-column grid (2×2 for four products) on desktop and mobile: image on top, title, price, then a full-width black "Add" button. Give tiles equal width and equal height (for example CSS grid with equal rows, and a clamped or min-height title area) so differing title lengths don't break the layout. Each button adds only that product to the cart via AJAX. A separate bundle-style variant (checkboxes, auto-add with the main product) was discussed as a different feature requiring its own metafield and about 3–5 h of work, and was not confirmed.

name: PDP Multiple Product Videos (Story Bubbles with Popup)

what.text: A PDP section with a centered heading and a row of round thumbnail 'bubbles', each with a text label below (e.g. 'How to style', 'Material', 'Production'). Clicking a bubble opens a popup (modal) with a main title and a video (or image), followed by several content blocks (Title, Thumbnail, Content 01-03 and more). The section exists in two versions: (1) a static version configured in the theme editor, and (2) a version driven by product metafields and metaobjects, so each product can show its own unique bubbles and content. The metafield version hides itself when a product has no metaobjects.

why.text: Story-style bubbles are a familiar pattern from social media, so shoppers instinctively tap them. They let customers explore usage, material and production details on demand without lengthening the page. Video and image content shows the product in use, reduces uncertainty and communicates product value and brand credibility. Per-product content keeps the information relevant to each item.

how.text: Build a section with 'Item' blocks (one per bubble): button thumbnail image, button label, and a popup with heading plus a video or image. Each item also has multiple content blocks (title, thumbnail, content) shown at 9:16 in the popup. Static version: everything is edited in the theme customizer. Metafield version: create a product metafield that references a list of metaobjects (one metaobject per bubble, with button text, button background, popup heading, media and content blocks). Loop over the referenced metaobjects in Liquid on the product page, since the theme customizer cannot natively bind to them. Hide the section if the product has no metaobjects. Add the section manually to any custom product template (it is pre-set in the Default product template; templates duplicated from Default inherit it). Hide the heading number/icon when the title is empty. Make sure the store grants access to Custom data (product and variant metafields and metaobjects).

name: Cart Drawer Free Shipping Progress Bar with Auto-Added Free Gift
status: Built — launched to live theme (customer enables it via theme settings)

what.text: A cart drawer module with a free-shipping progress bar. A message above the bar gives delivery reassurance ("Great choice! Your order will arrive in 2-3 working days"). Below the bar, a line states how much is still missing for free shipping ("Only €15.40 left for free shipping"). The bar has end-point icons, including a configurable gift icon. A free gift can be unlocked at a minimum cart value and is added to the cart automatically as a €0 line item once the threshold is reached.

why.text: The progress bar uses the goal-gradient effect: the closer shoppers get to a reward, the more motivated they are to finish. The "only X left" wording makes the gap feel small and concrete, which encourages add-ons that raise AOV. A free gift adds a tangible, loss-averse incentive, because shoppers don't want to lose the gift by dropping below the threshold. The delivery-time message lowers purchase anxiety.

how.text: Build it as a cart drawer (mini-cart) section with theme settings. 1) Enable the free-item feature with a toggle. 2) Set a headline for the gift and a minimum cart amount that unlocks it. 3) Pick the gift product(s) with the product picker and turn on 'Auto add'. 4) Paste custom SVG markup for the gift icon on the progress bar. 5) The bar and 'amount missing' text update from the cart total against the free-shipping threshold. The gift product must exist in the shop with a price of €0. If the product is also sold as a normal purchasable item, create a separate free product or variant. Once the condition is met, the rule adds the gift automatically. Customers cannot decline it, and it can only be removed in the editor by removing the product from the gift list. Known caveat: if the gift sells out, it can no longer be added, but the section still shows it as a free gift, so the merchant must disable the free-gift function manually. The original theme had a 'hidden' product tag feature that hid every quantity selector and showed an extra 'remove bundle' button. It conflicted with the gift and was commented out in the live theme.

what.text: A revised cart drawer (the 'Revision' variant in an A/B test for the client GIVE LOVE). why.text: Each part targets a different hesitation at the cart. The reservation timer adds mild urgency to finish checkout. A one-click add with a variant popup keeps the add-on low-friction and raises AOV. The trust chips and payment icons right next to the checkout CTA reduce risk and payment anxiety. Showing the struck-through price and savings anchors perceived value.

how.text: Build it as a custom cart drawer (Liquid plus JS). Render a countdown banner at the top of the drawer. Below the line items, add a recommendation carousel with a headline and a social-proof subline. Each card shows an image, title, price (with compare-at price and savings if on sale) and an ADD button. name: Product Compare Section (Comparison Table)
status: Backlog (spec and design reference only; feasibility question open)

what.text: A standalone, theme-editor-configurable Shopify section called "Compare Section". It shows 2, 3 or 4 hand-picked products side by side in a comparison table. Each product column has an image, title, price (current and struck-through compare-at price), color swatches and a "Zum Produkt" (view product) button. Below the products, rows with a label (e.g. Dimensions, Price, Wood type) show each product's values. An "Alles einblenden" (show all) toggle expands the remaining rows. The section has an optional headline and sub-headline. Desktop shows a label column on the left with product columns to the right. Mobile keeps the same table layout, with 2 products side by side and the labels sitting above their values.

why.text: Shoppers comparing similar products often leave the site to research or abandon because of decision overload. A side-by-side table reduces cognitive load and effort, and makes the differences in specs, price and material explicit. That clarity helps the buyer feel confident choosing, and cuts the back-and-forth between product pages. The "show all" toggle keeps the table short and scannable while the detail stays available. Direct CTA buttons under each product shorten the path from comparison to purchase and can steer shoppers to higher-value options.

how.text: Build a custom section with blocks. Section settings: background color, text color, font size, headline and sub-headline (rich text with bold, italic and underline), number of products (2/3/4), show/hide price toggle, and button color. Product blocks use a product picker. Row-name blocks use rich text for the labels (e.g. Dimensions, Price, Wood type). Each row's comparison values can come from a product metafield or be typed in manually (both options must be supported). Render the product header (image, title, price, swatches, button) first, then a row for each label. Collapse rows beyond the first few behind an "Alles einblenden" toggle. Use a responsive grid so mobile keeps the columns side by side, with the label above the values. One open question from the comments: since metafield names differ per store/theme, the row block should let the merchant pick which existing metafield (namespace.key) feeds each row, instead of fixed 'Comparison Value 1/2/3' fields.

items: Row names (rich text: bold/italic/underline), e.g. Dimensions, Price, Wood type
Comparison data source per row: metafield or manual entry (both supported)
Collapse/expand rows ("Alles einblenden") – visible in the design; not listed as a setting in the ticket

dependencies.text: Product metafields for comparison values, if the metafield data source is used. Metafield definitions differ per store, so the section needs a way to select the metafield for each row (open question in comments). Manual entry removes the metafield dependency. Needs a theme that supports Online Store 2.0 sections/blocks. The reference design is the Impact theme on Holz4Home PDP. No app is required.

items: Click-through rate on the "Zum Produkt" buttons
Add-to-cart rate / conversion rate for sessions that see the section
Scroll depth and visibility of the section
Bounce/exit rate on pages with the section

name: Feature Bubbles (Tabbed Product Component Benefits)
status: Built — launched (tested internally by Christoph and Chris; developed by Rana)

what.text: A tabbed section that shows a row of round image 'bubbles' (e.g. Safety razor, Shaving brush set, Razor stand, Alum stone). Each bubble has a label underneath. Clicking one swaps the large hero image above and the benefit text below (a checkmark bullet list plus a short paragraph). The first tab is active by default and the active bubble gets a highlighted border and underlined label in an accent color. The bubbles overlap the bottom edge of the hero image. The block sits in a dark rounded box (boxed layout), with an optional full-width layout. It is a 1:1 recreation of the Störtebecker PDP section for a bundle/set product.

why.text: Bundle and set products are hard to scan, because shoppers cannot see what each component contributes. Clickable bubbles let shoppers explore each item's benefit on demand (progressive disclosure), which reduces clutter and raises perceived value of the whole set. Concrete benefit bullets with checkmarks answer 'why do I need this?' per item. Trust cues such as a test-winner badge on the hero image add credibility. Visual, tappable navigation also encourages engagement and scrolling depth on the PDP.

how.text: Create the section file ed-feature-bubbles.liquid and paste the provided code. Add one 'item' block per bubble, each with a bubble image, label, hero image, optional overlay avatar/badge (e.g. test-winner seal) and rich-text content (bullet list plus paragraph). Choose boxed or full-width layout, then set colors, sizes and spacing for desktop and mobile. A small vanilla JS script toggles the 'active' class on the clicked button, its content and its thumbnail, and activates the first tab on load. It also re-initializes on the shopify:section:load event in the theme editor. List bullets use a custom icon (list_icon) or a default star.svg fallback.

items: Section background and content background colors
Boxed: top/bottom and left/right padding, max width, corner radius, hero thumbnail height, avatar/badge size
Full-width: content position (left/center/right), max width, thumbnail height, avatar size
Bubble style (circle or rounded), size, position, gap, border toggle, border size
Label font size, weight, uppercase toggle, active underline toggle
Bubble text, active text, border and active border colors (global with per-block overrides)
Mobile: thumbnail height, avatar width, bubble size, font size, gaps, alignment, content alignment, option to hide labels
Per block: bubble image, label, hero image, overlay avatar/badge, rich-text content

dependencies.text: No app or metafields required; all content is configured in the theme editor blocks. Assumes an OS 2.0 theme with section blocks, and that the theme provides a .container class and a .heading font class. Default list icon expects /cdn/shop/files/star.svg to exist. Placed on the PDP, mainly for set/bundle products.

name: PDP Buy Box (Bordered Container with Sticky Option)
status: Built — launched (tested internally by Christoph and Chris)

what.text: A theme-editor toggle on the product page that wraps the whole product info column (title, price, stock status, add-to-cart button, payment icons, Klarna note) in a visible bordered, optionally background-colored box with rounded corners. An optional 'Sticky Buy Box' setting keeps the box pinned while the customer scrolls past the gallery. This recreates the 'Buy Box' feature of the Focal theme (elbdev) as a section setting.

why.text: Visually grouping the price, availability, CTA and payment/trust icons into one framed unit sets the purchase decision area apart from the rest of the page and focuses attention on the buy action. A card-like container signals 'this is where you act', reduces visual noise and keeps the CTA and reassurance in view. The sticky option keeps the CTA reachable while users read the gallery and description. Mostly a visual-hierarchy effect, so expect a modest lift.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add schema settings: a 'Buy Box' header, the checkboxes enable_buy_box and sticky_buy_box, the color pickers buy_box_border_color and buy_box_background_color, and a border-radius range (0–16px, default 8). 2) In product-info.liquid, inside the .product__info wrapper, conditionally wrap the content in <div class="ed-pdp-buy-box"> when enable_buy_box is on. 3) Output a scoped <style> block: transparent colors fall back to theme background and a mix of background and text color (90%) for the border; colors are exposed as RGB CSS variables (--buybox-border-color / --buybox-background-color). The box gets a 1px border, the chosen radius and 16px padding (12px 8px on mobile ≤767px). If sticky is on, .product__info gets position: sticky with top: 100px. 4) Enable it in the theme editor under Product page > Buy Box.

name: PDP Collapsible Description with Default-Open Option
status: Built — tested internally, documented

what.text: A Description block for the PDP buy box that can be shown in two layouts: 'Collapsible' (an accordion-style header with an arrow icon, which expands and collapses the product description) or 'Normal' (plain description text). In Collapsible layout, a checkbox lets you choose whether the description is open on page load. This gives two test variants: (1) nothing expanded initially, (2) the 'Description' tab expanded initially. The ticket asked for a universal section that works in any Shopify theme. What was built is a Description block only, not a generic multi-tab component.

why.text: Open by default: product information is visible immediately, so there is less friction for shoppers who want details before buying. This helps users who don't notice or don't click collapsed accordions, and keeps key value messaging in view near the add-to-cart button. Collapsed by default: a shorter page keeps the buy box compact, so the CTA, reviews and cross-sell blocks below stay close to the fold, and users can open only what they need. Which one wins depends on the product and audience, which is why it is worth testing.

how.text: Three code steps in a Shopify theme. (1) In main-product.liquid, replace the 'description' block schema with an extended one. It adds settings for top/bottom spacing, layout (Collapsible/Normal), 'Open button as default', border, header text, font size, padding and colors. (2) Create the snippet ed-collapsible-description.liquid. It outputs scoped CSS, a toggle button with a circular arrow icon (aria-expanded), and a collapsible content container holding product.description. A small JS handler animates height over 500ms and rotates the arrow. When layout is 'normal', it renders the plain description. (3) In product-form.liquid, replace the `when 'description'` case with `{% render 'ed-collapsible-description', section: section, block: block, product: product %}`. In the theme editor, select the Description block, set Layout = Collapsible, and toggle 'Open button as default' on or off to create the A/B variants.

items: Open button as default (checkbox, default off)

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps. It uses the native product.description and the theme's main-product.liquid and product-form.liquid files, whose structure must match (a 'description' block type and `when 'description'` case). The theme should support the `rte` and `product-form__description` classes. Implementation caveats (inferred from the code): the aria-controls/ID is hardcoded as 'block-id-2', so multiple instances on one page would conflict. The schema snippet has a trailing comma after the last setting, which must be removed or the JSON schema will be invalid. The JS query is global (.ed-collapsible-toggle) and shows no guard against double-binding on section reload. Only the Description tab is covered, not other product tabs.

status: Built — delivered (source code zip + docs); theme-integration instructions revised Oct 2025

what.text: A standalone, theme-independent header section (modelled on the Focal theme header) that lets the merchant assign one navigation menu for desktop and a different menu for the mobile drawer in the Theme Editor. If no mobile menu is chosen, it falls back to the main menu. The section also includes logo settings (desktop and mobile width, optional transparent logo on the homepage), sticky and transparent header options, header layout choices, a mega menu with a maximum of 4 images, search, account and cart icons with a cart count, and country and language selectors. The Focal theme already has the separate-menu setting; this ticket makes it reusable in other themes, tested on Dawn.

why.text: Mobile and desktop users navigate differently. Desktop has room for wide mega menus with many categories, while mobile needs a short, thumb-friendly list of the top categories. A tailored menu per device shortens the path to product and collection pages and reduces menu overload and bounce on mobile. It also lets the agency A/B test navigation structure per device without touching the other. This reasoning is inferred and was not stated in the ticket.

how.text: 1) Create a section file header.liquid in the target theme and paste the provided code, adapted from the Focal header. 2) Add the required translation keys (header.general.navigation, newsletter, login, account, cart, language, country) to locales/en.default.json. They must go inside the existing top-level JSON braces, not after the final closing bracket, or the file will throw a syntax error. 3) In the Theme Editor, open the Header group and, under Navigation, pick the 'Menu' (desktop) and the 'Mobile menu' (mobile drawer). The mobile menu falls back to the main menu if empty. 4) Configure layout, logo, sticky and transparent header, icons and selectors. The ticket's code file is truncated and has further steps (up to at least Step 8) that are not visible here, so the full build needs the original zip and doc.

what.text: A configurable quantity picker (– / number / +) placed inline next to the Add-to-Cart (ATC) button on the product page. It can sit to the left or right of the ATC button, has rounded (pill) corners instead of square ones, takes custom text and background colors, matches the ATC button height, and can be hidden completely (or on mobile only). Two design variants exist: (1) the picker to the LEFT of the ATC button, and (2) the picker hidden entirely, leaving a full-width ATC button.

why.text: Placing the quantity control right beside the primary CTA keeps the buying decision in one compact row and makes multi-unit purchases easy, which can lift units per order for consumables or bundle-friendly products. Hiding it removes a decision point and a bit of visual noise for single-purchase products, giving a cleaner, more focused CTA. Making both variants available lets the agency A/B test 'more choice and higher AOV' against 'less friction'.

how.text: In the Dawn-style theme: 1) In main-product.liquid, remove the separate quantity_selector block and replace the buy_buttons block schema with one that includes quantity settings (hide, hide on mobile, hide label, text color, background color, position left/right, full-width on mobile, default style on mobile) plus ATC and Buy-now color settings. 2) In product-form.liquid, remove the old quantity_selector code and replace the product-payment-container markup with a flex wrapper (.ed_quantity_and_atc_wrap, with qtty-pos-left/right class) containing the quantity-selector and the ATC button. CSS makes both elements pill-shaped (border-radius 50px) and equal height (--button-height). Position right uses flex order -1 on the ATC button. On mobile, the wrapper stacks in a column with a full-width picker. The dynamic checkout button stays below.

name: PDP Color Variant Selector (Swatches / Product Images / Text Buttons)
status: Backlog — not built (spec only; ticket reassigned and parked in backlog)

what.text: A custom Shopify section, "CRO | PDP | Farbvarianten" (Color Variants), that replaces the default color option picker on the product page. The merchant picks one of three display modes: (1) round or square color swatches, (2) product-image thumbnails per color, or (3) text buttons. Every mode shows the label with the active color name (e.g. "Color: khaki" or "Farbe: Washed black"), highlights the current selection, and updates image, price and availability when a color is chosen. The text-button mode shows unavailable variants struck through and disabled (e.g. "Denim"). The ticket allows building this as one section with a mode setting or as three separate sections.

why.text: Visual color pickers reduce effort and uncertainty: shoppers see the real product or true color instead of decoding a dropdown or text label. Image thumbnails show how each colorway looks on the product, which supports confident choices and encourages browsing other colors. Showing the active color name and a clear selected state gives constant feedback. Struck-through, disabled unavailable options prevent dead-end clicks and frustration. Together this lowers friction at the key variant-selection step.

how.text: Build one theme section (or three) with a display-mode select: swatches, images or text. Render the option values for the color option from the product variants. Swatches use a color value from a metafield or a mapping of color names to hex. Image mode uses the variant's featured image or a metafield, and the ticket says color values can be maintained via metafield or variant logic. On click, switch the variant, then update the main gallery image, price and availability via the variant-change event or section rendering. Mark unavailable variants as disabled with a strikethrough. Expose typography, color, bold, alignment, shape and order settings in the theme editor.

name: Cart Tiered Rewards Progress Bar (Free Shipping + 3 Free Gifts)
status: Built — launched (merged to live theme 2025-06-01)

what.text: A progress bar at the top of the cart drawer. It shows cart value against several reward thresholds: free shipping first, then up to three free-gift tiers. Each tier is marked by an icon (truck for shipping, gift boxes for gifts) on the bar. The bar fills as the cart grows, and a message below states the next step, e.g. 'Only €43.05 left for free shipping' or 'Your shipping is now free. €11.20 left until your free gift!'. Unlocked tiers show a success message. In the customer's setup the bar only visualises the tiers. Adding the free gift to the cart is handled by the customer's existing app, not by this section.

why.text: The goal-gradient effect: people accelerate toward a goal the closer they get. A visible bar with a concrete 'X € left' amount makes the next reward feel within reach, which nudges shoppers to add items and raises AOV. Stacking several milestones (free shipping, then three gifts) gives repeated small goals and rewards. Instant success messages reinforce each win. Showing every tier upfront also communicates the full value of the offer.

how.text: Build it as a theme section/snippet rendered in the cart drawer above the line items. Take the cart total and compare it with merchant-defined thresholds (customer example: €60 free shipping, €79 / €89 / €109 gifts). Icon positions are calculated dynamically from the highest threshold, so the bar and icons always stay aligned with the real values. Icon spacing was adjusted by about 10px so close tiers (e.g. the 2nd and 3rd gifts) don't overlap. Progress messages (before a tier, after each tier is reached, and a final message) are editable text in the theme settings. Free-gift add-to-cart logic can be turned off when an external app handles it. The merchant can change thresholds, for instance during sales, without code. The section was extended from 2 to 3 gift tiers.

name: PDP Variant Cards with Unit Price, Savings Badge & Popular Variant Label
status: Built — delivered, awaiting customer feedback

what.text: A product-page variant selector that replaces dropdowns or plain swatches with clickable cards, one per pack size. Each card shows the variant name (e.g. '1.7kg - 85m²') and its price. The final UI also shows a per-unit price (e.g. €8,81/kg) and a dark 'Spare 37%' savings strip on the larger packs. One variant can be flagged as the popular choice, which gets a coloured 'Bestseller' tag above its card. The selected card has a dark outline. On desktop at least four cards fit in one row and extra cards wrap. On mobile the cards scroll horizontally instead of wrapping.

why.text: Showing every pack size side by side with its unit price makes the volume discount visible at a glance. The savings strip is a price anchor that pushes buyers toward bigger, higher-AOV packs. The 'Bestseller' tag adds social proof and reduces choice paralysis by suggesting a default. The distinct colour makes the recommended option stand out.

how.text: Build the cards as variant blocks inside the PDP buy box in the theme editor. Flag the popular variant per product with a variant metafield ('Popular variant' = true), so the merchant picks it per product without code. The label text is editable in the section settings (default 'Bestseller') and is shown as a coloured tag on the flagged card. Size the cards so at least four fit per row on desktop. On mobile use a horizontally scrollable row with no wrapping. The savings % appears to be computed against the first variant's per-unit price (8.81→5.55 = 37%, →3.69 = 58%, →2.39 = 73%). That formula is an inference and was not confirmed in the ticket.

name: Image with Slides (Synced Image + Content Carousel)
status: Built — launched (bug fix delivered; documentation in Slite)

what.text: A custom Shopify section ('CRO | Image with Slides') that pairs a rotated two-image collage with a text panel (subheading, large heading, body text). Round prev/next arrow buttons switch to the next slide. The image slides and text slides are two Swiper carousels kept in sync, so one click changes both. Each slide holds up to two images (a single image is also supported). The image side can sit left or right of the text. In the theme editor, a basic preview appears in the section picker.

why.text: Splits a brand, feature or benefit story into short, scannable chapters instead of one long text block. The visual + text pairing, and the arrows' sense of progression, invite interaction and keep attention on the value propositions. Showing several benefits in one compact spot saves vertical space and lets the page convey more USPs without long scrolling. The tilted, overlapping images add a more premium, editorial feel. Conversion impact is indirect; this is a storytelling and engagement element, not a direct purchase driver.

how.text: Create the section file 'ed-cro-multiple-image-with-slides.liquid' and paste the provided code. The section needs Swiper to be available in the theme (the code calls `new Swiper` but does not load it). Add 'slide' blocks, each with subheading, heading, text, and thumbnail 1 and 2. The code renders two Swiper instances (a content swiper and a media swiper) with fade effect and loop. They are linked via `controller.control`, so one arrow click syncs both. Instances are scoped by `section.id`, so the section can be added multiple times on a page and each slider works independently. This fixes the earlier bug where arrows showed the same pictures. The Shopify design-mode event `shopify:section:load` re-initialises the sliders in the theme editor. Spacing, sizes and colors are driven by CSS variables set from the section settings, with separate mobile and desktop values (breakpoint 1000px). One caveat from comments: the code file contains 'Step 1' twice, which may be a documentation error. Another: the arrow selectors `.contentSwiper_next/prev` are not scoped by section ID, which could cause cross-talk with multiple instances (my inference from the code).

what.text: A PDP block that shows a headline (e.g. "Die Verwendung" / how to use) with a row of round video thumbnail buttons, each with a label underneath (e.g. "STYLE", "TEST"). Clicking a button opens a modal popup with the video (default 340px wide) next to a details list. The details list uses an icon, a title, a thumbnail and a paragraph per item (read from the code's CSS classes, I). The original ticket asked for a "Multiple Produktvideos" section with a headline, sub-headline, and one sub-section per video (thumbnail, video, title, popup description). The final build is a block with limit 1 inside main-product.liquid, named "PDP| MPV via Metafields". It stays hidden unless the product has metaobject values.

why.text: Short usage or style videos show the product in real use and answer "how does it look or work?" without a long text. This lowers uncertainty and the perceived risk of buying. Putting the videos in a popup keeps the PDP compact and the buyer in context, with no page navigation. Round, labeled thumbnails invite a tap and make the content easy to scan.

how.text: 1) Set up a metaobject definition with video, thumbnail, title and description (and the detail entries). 2) Create a product metafield (list of metaobjects) named cro_multiple_product_videos in the standard namespace. 3) Add the schema block "pdp_mvp_via_metafields" (limit 1) to the schema of main-product.liquid. 4) Create the snippet pdp-multiple-product-videos-via-metafields.liquid. It reads the metafield, renders the headline and the thumbnail button list, and outputs scoped <style> for the block settings. It also renders the modal with video and detail list, and the open/close JS. 5) In the theme editor, add the block to the product template and fill in the metafield on each product. The block only renders if the metafield has a value. The supplied code was truncated (mobile CSS, markup and JS are not fully visible).

name: Cart Free Gift with Progress Bar (€0 Gift Line Item)
status: Built — live in theme, but customer deactivated it; €0 pricing needs a discount app (workaround proposed, awaiting customer feedback)

what.text: A free-gift mechanic in the cart drawer/cart page. The cart progress bar has two milestones (free shipping and free gift). When the customer reaches the threshold, a message appears ("Congratulations! Add your free gift!") and the chosen gift product shows in the cart as a line item at €0.00. The gift line has a Remove link, so customers can decline it. Per the ticket history, the gift is no longer shown with a quantity selector.

why.text: A free gift gives shoppers a tangible reward for hitting a spend threshold. The progress bar makes the goal visible (goal-gradient effect) and nudges people to add items to reach it, which raises AOV. Showing the gift at €0.00 reinforces the 'free' framing (reciprocity). Letting people remove the gift keeps them in control and avoids friction or distrust.

how.text: 1) Add the gift milestone to the cart progress bar next to the free-shipping milestone, with a congratulation message. 2) Add the designated gift product to the cart when the threshold is met and show it at €0.00 with a Remove link. 3) To make the price truly €0 at checkout without cloning the product, use a discount app (e.g. 'Every Possible Discount') that discounts the gift SKU by 100% when the cart condition is met. Theme code alone can only display €0 and does not change the checkout price. A first build charged the gift at checkout for this reason. 4) Cloning the product to a €0 variant breaks inventory when stock is managed externally (here JTL, where a clone drove stock negative), so avoid it in such setups.

Needs the cart drawer/cart page theme with a progress bar (the Sectionfy live theme in the screenshots). The exact gift-product metafield or setting is not documented.

name: FAQ Section with Category Tabs and Thumbnail (Variant 2)
status: Built — launched (documented; product image supplied for docs)

what.text: A custom Shopify FAQ section ("CRO | FAQ with Tabs") for the Impact theme. It shows a heading and subline, an optional thumbnail/product image beside (left or right) a white card of accordion questions. Questions can be grouped by category, with pill-shaped filter tabs above the accordion (a "Filter" label plus buttons such as General, Recipe, Intake, Shipping). The first category can act as an "All questions" view. Each Category block holds its own FAQ items. The accordion uses +/– icons, and the answer text opens beneath the question.

why.text: Unanswered questions at the point of decision cause hesitation and drop-off. Surfacing answers to common objections (origin, price justification, dosage, shipping) in a scannable accordion lowers perceived risk and support effort without crowding the page. Category filters let shoppers jump to the topic they care about, which reduces cognitive load on long FAQ lists. A product image alongside keeps the visual context and brand feel. The card with shadow lifts the FAQ from the background and makes it feel like an interactive tool.

how.text: Create the snippet ed-cro-faq-section-two.liquid and the matching section in the theme (Impact). The section uses CSS custom properties driven by section and block settings, with separate mobile and desktop values (breakpoint 1000px for layout, 768px for text). Blocks: Heading (rich text heading with a highlighted word), Content (subline) and Category blocks (each containing FAQ items). Tabs use a custom element (skb-universal-tabs-wrap) with horizontally scrollable pill buttons. The active tab gets a configurable background and text colour. FAQs use a custom collapsible element (ed-collapsible) with a toggle button, plus/minus icon rotation and bordered rows. Layout: flex row on desktop with the thumbnail taking a set width percentage (default 40%), stacked on screens under 1000px. Enable "Group FAQ's by category" to show the tabs, and "Multiple accordions open at once" to allow several open answers. The code file in the ticket is truncated (the plus-icon rule is cut off), and the JS for the tabs and collapsible is not shown.

what.text: A reusable Shopify section that pairs one large rounded image with a stack of up to 6 accordion cards. Each card has an icon, a bold heading, a subheading, and a round plus/close button. Clicking a card expands it to reveal rich-text content. The image on the left switches to match the open item (each item has its own thumbnail). Section, image and accordion styling are fully configurable in the theme editor.

why.text: The element condenses several benefits, features or USPs into a scannable list. Visitors self-select the information they care about (progressive disclosure), which lowers cognitive load and keeps the page short. The image that changes with the open item adds visual context and emotional appeal. Icons and short sublines let people scan benefits quickly, and expanding a card is a micro-commitment that deepens engagement.

how.text: Create the section file ed-cro-exciting-collapsible-image-content.liquid and paste in the provided code. It uses custom HTML, CSS, Liquid and vanilla JS (an <ed-collapsible-wrap> / <ed-collapsible> structure, no third-party plugins). Add 'Item' blocks (up to 6). For each block, set a thumbnail image, an icon (uploaded as an image or pasted as SVG, with custom width), a heading, a subheading and rich-text content. The first block or any block flagged 'open by default' is open at load. Single-open mode is on by default (opening one item closes the others). Then set the layout (image width %, gap, image position left/right, match content height), colors, corner radii, font sizes, plus-or-arrow toggle style, and desktop/mobile spacing. On mobile the layout stacks (image above the accordion) and icons can be hidden.

why.text: Showing the product's key features as quick-scan icons makes the main selling points visible at a glance, so buyers take them in without reading long copy. The headline with a number ("6 adjustable points") and the subheadline ("You are an original. SitOne adapts to you.") frame the product as customizable and personal.
