Render the blocks in a horizontal track and duplicate the set so the loop is seamless. Animate with CSS (a translate keyframe) or a lightweight JS slider (e.g. Swiper or Splide) using linear easing and constant speed, so there is no stutter or visible jump at the loop point. Offer manual control (swipe/drag) alongside the autoplay. Use responsive items-per-view: at least 5 on desktop, about 3 on tablet and 1–2 on mobile. Keep the motion running at every viewport. Make the speed a select setting (slow/medium/fast) that maps to the animation duration. Blocks are sortable in the Customizer.

name: PDP Animated Time Indicator (Progress Ring Counter)
status: Built — code delivered by dev (ed-pdp-time-indicator.liquid), product image added for the example; no launch or test result recorded

what.text: A PDP section that shows 1–3 time-based key figures (e.g. setup time 25 Min, delivery time 48 Hours, return time 72 Hours) as large numbers inside circular progress rings. When the section scrolls into view, the number counts up from 0 to its target value while a coloured arc around it fills in sync. Each tile has a unit label (Min / Hours / Sec) inside the ring and a bold headline below it (e.g. 'Average setup time'). The section is centred on all viewports.

why.text: Concrete numbers make a product's promise tangible and quantifiable. A statement like 'assembles in 25 minutes' lowers perceived effort and risk, which are common objections for bulky products such as office chairs. Fast delivery and easy returns reduce purchase anxiety. The count-up and ring animation catches the eye, helps the figures stick, and makes the facts look like a credible, scannable 'dashboard' rather than marketing copy.

how.text: 1) Create a new theme section file 'ed-pdp-time-indicator.liquid' and paste in the delivered code (CSS, markup, JS and schema). The section appears in the theme editor as 'PDP | Time Indicator'. 2) Add it to the product template and add one 'Item' block per figure, up to 3 per the ticket. 3) For each block set the time value, unit and richtext headline, plus the ring colours, background and border colour. 4) Set section-level options: card size, gaps, ring width, content direction (unit below or beside the number), font sizes and spacing, with separate mobile values. Under the hood, each tile is an SVG with two circles (a track and an active arc). An IntersectionObserver at 50% visibility triggers a one-off setInterval count-up (about 1.2 s). It increments the number and animates stroke-dashoffset at the same time. An 'animated' class and a data-initialized flag stop it re-running. The code also re-initialises on Shopify theme-editor section/block events. Tiles sit in a centred flex-wrap row, so they stack on mobile.

items: Per block: unit text (e.g. Min, Hours)
Per block: richtext headline (bold / italic / underline possible)
Per block: ring colour, active/progress arc colour, text colour, inner circle background, border/fill colour
Section: text colour and background colour (transparent = fall back to theme colours)
Card (ring) size: 140–300 px desktop, separate mobile value (default 250 / 200)
Gap between cards (rem), desktop and mobile

name: PDP Bulk Discount Tiers (Tabbed)
status: Built — launched (code delivered with install instructions; documentation reviewed)

what.text: A custom Shopify section, 'PDP | Bulk Discounts', shown on the product page. It displays volume-discount tiers as a row of cards, e.g. '50+ desks – For large companies – 20% discount'. Product-type tabs (Desks / Chairs / Frames) sit above the cards. One card can carry a green 'Best value' badge and each card has an icon. Below the cards is a footer CTA box with a headline, a bullet list of reassurances (free shipping, 30-day money-back guarantee, customer service, extended warranty) and a button with an optional arrow icon. The section is meant for every product, not one product only.

why.text: Tiered volume discounts show buyers that ordering more lowers the unit price, which raises quantity and AOV, especially for B2B or office buyers. The 'Best value' badge anchors attention on the top tier. Each tier is tied to a customer segment ('for start-ups', 'for large companies'), so buyers can self-identify. Reassurance bullets next to the CTA reduce risk at the moment of decision. Tabs let one block cover several product categories without clutter.

how.text: Create the section file ed-pdp-bulk-discounts.liquid and paste in the supplied code (the ticket attachment includes install steps). Content is managed in the theme customizer through blocks: one 'Tab-item' block per product type or discount tier and a 'Footer' block for the CTA area. Colours and sizes are driven by CSS variables set from section settings, with theme-level fallbacks when a colour is left transparent. The active tab is black with white text and inactive tabs are muted. The tab switcher is JS-driven, with a sliding active indicator. The cards form a responsive row of 2–5 on desktop and stack on mobile. Tabs scroll horizontally or wrap on mobile. The footer button is a pill with an arrow icon that animates on hover. The section can be previewed before it is added to the theme customizer. Because it applies to every product, it is added to the default product template.

status: Built — delivered by dev (July 2025); documentation reviewed, product image supplied

what.text: A PDP section that shows 2–4 of the store's own products side by side in a horizontal, symmetric comparison table. Each column has a product image, name, short description, price and up to 5 technical bullet points. The product currently being viewed is marked "This model" (accent label plus underline), so shoppers see where it sits in the range. Optional subheading, heading and download button (e.g. PDF data sheet). The section hides itself on products without comparison data.

why.text: Comparing within the range reduces choice uncertainty. Shoppers can check that the product fits their needs without leaving for a competitor's site. Anchoring on "this model" makes the higher- and lower-priced siblings read as reference points. This enables confident upsell (a better model) or downsell (a cheaper one) instead of a bounce. Aligned rows of specs make differences scannable, which lowers cognitive load for technical, higher-consideration products. Inference: the buyer-psychology rationale is not stated in the ticket.

how.text: Built as a custom Shopify section (file ed-dynamic-compare.liquid) with blocks: Subheading, Heading and Product card (up to 4 cards). The comparison content is driven by three product metafields created by the dev, so values can differ per product. The section stays hidden when those metafields are empty. Layout is a symmetric table-like grid with aligned name, description, price and bullet rows. On mobile the products stack or scroll horizontally; the screenshot shows the row overflowing with the 4th column cut off, which suggests horizontal scroll. The current product is flagged via a per-product setting (checkbox in the Customizer per the ticket) and styled with a secondary accent colour. An optional download button (top right) has configurable text, icon and link. Style variables are exposed as CSS custom properties per section ID. The code file is truncated, so the exact metafield names and the Liquid markup of the table are not visible.

name: PDP Fullscreen Image Slider with Floating Buy Box
status: Built — delivered (code + install instructions provided; docs reviewed)

what.text: Replaces the default PDP gallery with a full-viewport, horizontally swipeable image/video slider (Swiper). On desktop (≥1000px) the slider fills the screen below the header and the buy box floats as a card over the images at the bottom-right (offset from right/bottom is configurable). The buy box shows the product title, price, variant selection, add-to-cart button and delivery/returns info. On mobile the buy box sits below the slider and the images remain swipeable. Navigation is via swipe, mouse drag, keyboard or prev/next arrows, with optional pagination dots. Reference: Marshall Major V PDP.

why.text: Immersive, edge-to-edge imagery builds emotional desire and perceived product quality, which is especially effective for lifestyle and premium products. Keeping the buy box permanently visible over the gallery means price, variant choice and CTA are always in view, so the shopper never has to scroll to find the purchase action. Peeking at the next slide on mobile and visible arrows encourage image exploration and reduce friction.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add the 'Fullscreen slider Settings' schema block (slides per view for desktop/tablet/mobile, next-slide peek %, video autoplay, pagination, arrows, autoplay with freeMode, duration, stop on interaction, buy box offsets from right/bottom). 2) Create the snippet pdp-fullscreen-image-slider.liquid, which loops product.media and renders image slides (lazy-loaded unless the selected media), video slides (custom play/pause overlay) and optional cross-sell image blocks. It initialises Swiper with loop and breakpoints at 740px and 1000px. 3) Load Swiper 11 CSS/JS from the jsDelivr CDN in theme.liquid. 4) In main-product.liquid, replace the default slider with {% render 'pdp-fullscreen-image-slider' %}. On ≥1000px the wrapper is absolutely positioned over a 100vh container, and .product__info is pushed to the bottom-right with configurable margins. On <1000px the buy box flows below the slider with 24px padding.

Info box offset from bottom (0–200px, default 60)

name: PDP Product Tabs (Expandable Image Cards)
status: Built — launched (documented; product image for docs added later)

what.text: A Shopify section named 'CRO | PDP Producttabs' for the product page. It shows a row of rounded cards, each with an image, a heading, and an optional description and button/link. Cards expand and collapse like an accordion, using a +/− icon beside the heading. In the reference, the collapsed cards show only image + title, and the open card reveals its description. An optional CTA pill button (e.g. 'Discover key features') sits below the cards. Content is unique per product.

why.text: Image-led cards let shoppers scan product benefits visually and open only the ones that interest them. This reduces text overload and keeps the page short, while still giving depth on demand (progressive disclosure). Benefit-led headings communicate value and answer objections near the buy decision. The optional CTA gives engaged shoppers a clear next step. Mechanism is inferred; the ticket does not state a rationale.

how.text: Create the section file cro_pdp_product_tabs.liquid and paste the supplied code. The section has blocks for subheading, heading, content (rich text) and image, with per-block typography and spacing controlled via CSS variables. The cards live in a 3-column grid (.cro_pdp_product_tabs_list) with rounded corners (.cro_pdp_product_tabs__item). Colors fall back to global theme settings when the section color is transparent. Per-product content is delivered through a metaobject plus product metafield, set up by the developer (details are in the plain-text install instructions and the Slite doc, not fully visible in the source). Accordion behavior must expose aria-expanded and aria-controls, keyboard focus, and WCAG AA contrast. Cards stack on mobile (breakpoint at 1000px).

name: PDP Size Slider (Fit Scale)
status: Built — delivered, preview link provided (product image for documentation was requested afterwards)

what.text: A fit-information box for the product page. It shows a horizontal scale with three labels ("Runs small" / "True to size" / "Runs large") and a filled circle that marks where this product's fit falls. A headline sits above the scale (the screenshot shows "Size Information" with the last word in bold). The box has an optional border and rounded corners. The position and labels are stored per product in a metaobject referenced by a product metafield. If no data is stored for a product, the block does not render. The ticket calls it a "section", but the delivered code is a theme block (type cro_pdp_size_slider, limit 1) inside the main-product section.

why.text: Uncertainty about sizing is a major barrier to buying apparel and accessories online, and a major cause of returns. A quick visual that shows whether an item runs small or large answers the "will it fit?" question right where the size is chosen. This reduces perceived risk and hesitation, and it can also cut size-related returns. A visual scale takes less effort to read than a text note, and the same pattern works across the whole catalog.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add a new block schema entry "CRO | Size Slider" (type cro_pdp_size_slider, limit 1) with the settings listed below. 2) In product-form.liquid, add a `when 'cro_pdp_size_slider'` case that renders the snippet 'ed-cro-pdp-size-slider' with product and block. 3) Create the snippet ed-cro-pdp-size-slider.liquid. It reads product.metafields.standard.cro_size_slider.value and outputs a heading, a scale bar span, and a list of labels. The indicator is a 16px filled circle drawn with a ::before pseudo-element, positioned with left: scale_position%. 4) In Shopify admin, create the metaobject definition "CRO | PDP | Size Slider" (type cro_pdp_size_slider) with fields name (required, display name), heading (single line text), labels (list of single line text, required) and scale_position (integer 0–100, required). 5) Create the product metafield "CRO | Size Slider" (standard.cro_size_slider, mixed reference to that metaobject). 6) Fill in the metaobject entries per product (or via an app/import) and assign them to the products. 7) Add the block to the product template in the theme editor, below the variant picker (as in the screenshot).

items: Scale size / bar thickness (1–8 px, step 0.5, default 4)
Per product (metaobject): heading text, list of three labels, scale position 0–100 %

dependencies.text: Needs a Shopify theme with a main-product section and product-form.liquid (it uses a block-based product template). Needs a metaobject definition (cro_pdp_size_slider) and a product metafield (standard.cro_size_slider, mixed reference), with values filled in per product. The snippet relies on a theme `visually-hidden` utility class. No app is required. The data can optionally be filled by an app or bulk import. The ticket also mentions that the value could come from a product rating, but the delivered code only supports the metafield/metaobject route.

name: PDP Product Badges (metafield-driven, up to 3)
status: Built — delivered, docs reviewed

what.text: A block in the main product section that shows up to three small badges (e.g. 'Bestseller', 'New', 'Limited') directly above the product title on the PDP. Badge text comes from three product metafields, so each product can carry different badges. Each badge has its own text color, border color, background and optional icon. Position, spacing, padding, corner radius and typography are configurable in the theme editor.

why.text: Badges give shoppers an instant cue at the point of decision. 'Bestseller' acts as social proof, 'Limited' adds scarcity or urgency, and 'New' signals relevance. They are scannable, sit next to the title and price, and need no extra reading. Because they are set per product, the cues stay credible and avoid blanket claims. Three styles (solid, outlined, tinted) let the badges be visually ranked.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add the schema block 'pdp_product_badges' (limit 1). 2) Create the snippet pdp_product_badges.liquid. It renders only if at least one badge metafield is filled. It outputs a flex list of three badge divs (badge_1..3), each with an optional icon image and the metafield text, plus the product title (h1 on the PDP) inside a wrapper whose position class is top-left, top-right or below-title. CSS is injected inline from block settings, with a mobile font-size override at max-width 767px. 3) In product-info.liquid, call {% render 'pdp_product_badges', product: product, block: block %}. 4) Create three single-line-text product metafields: standard.pdp_product_badge_01, _02, _03. 5) Fill the metafields per product and style the block in the theme editor.

Position: top left / top right / below the title

Per badge 1/2/3: icon image, text color, border color, background (defaults: solid dark, outlined transparent, solid dark)

The theme must have main-product.liquid and a product-info.liquid snippet that renders blocks. The title markup uses the classes product-meta__title heading h3 (Prestige-style theme assumption). name: Quantity Tier Discount Spotlight Card (Collection Grid)
status: Reference only (ticket marked 'updated'; no description or comments, one reference screenshot)

what.text: A full-width, high-contrast promo card inserted between product cards in the collection grid. It spotlights the volume discount ladder: a 'Buy & save' headline, three tier rows (Buy 3 items | Get 10% OFF, Buy 4 items | Get 15% OFF, Buy 5+ items | Get 20% OFF) and an underlined 'LEARN MORE' link. why.text: Shoppers rarely notice volume discounts that only appear in the cart. Placing the ladder in the browsing flow sets the 'buy more, save more' anchor before the first add-to-cart. The tiered percentages create a visible goal gradient, and the next tier always looks like a small step for a bigger reward. This raises units per order and AOV. The full-bleed colored block breaks the grid pattern, so it works as a pattern interrupt and catches scanning eyes.

how.text: Build it as a custom grid-injected block, or a section rendered inside the collection product loop after product N (the screenshot shows it after roughly the 1st-2nd product on mobile). Use a solid brand-accent background with rounded corners and white text. Add a centered heading and one row per tier, with the threshold on the left, a thin vertical divider, and the bold discount on the right. Below the rows, add an underlined 'Learn more' link to a terms page, modal or drawer. The discount itself must be configured separately (automatic discount or a Shopify Function with quantity tiers). The card only communicates it. In the screenshot, a sticky progress bar with a countdown ('Add 3 items, get 10% OFF + free US shipping') and a floating 'Get up to 20% OFF' pill support the same offer. These look like separate companion elements, not part of this card.

name: Post-Add-to-Cart Protection Plan Pop-up (Warranty Upsell)
status: Reference only (duplicate ticket, no written spec)

what.text: A modal that opens on the PDP right after the shopper adds a product to the cart. The top bar confirms the add (small product thumbnail, check mark, 'Added to Cart') and offers a 'Checkout Now' button plus a close (X). The body offers a lifetime protection plan for a one-time fee ($199.99 in the reference). It has a headline with price, a short benefit list (tighten loose stones, resize rings and bands, expert clean and polish), a 'Learn more' link, an explainer video with a play button on the left, and a prominent black 'Add To Bag' button that adds the plan to the order. The PDP behind it shows the same offer as an expandable checkbox row under the size selector.

why.text: The shopper has just committed to the purchase, so the pop-up appears at peak intent, when the risk of a high-value purchase is most on their mind. A one-time payment for 'lifetime' protection lowers the fear of damage or loss and justifies the price. A concrete list of covered services and a human explainer video make the value tangible and build trust. Because the offer comes after the main add-to-cart, it works as a low-friction add-on that raises AOV and margin. The 'Checkout Now' button next to it keeps the path to purchase clear, so the upsell does not block the funnel.

how.text: Trigger the modal after a successful add-to-cart (AJAX) on the PDP, only for eligible products such as high-value or damage-prone items. Layout: a header row with thumbnail, 'Added to Cart' and a secondary 'Checkout Now' button; a body with video or image on the left and offer title, price, bullets and 'Learn more' on the right; a primary 'Add To Bag' button for the plan. Implement the plan as a separate hidden product or variant, priced fixed or by percentage, and add it to the cart with the main product on click. Mirror the offer on the PDP as an optional checkbox row, as shown in the screenshot. Keep the close button obvious so the shopper can decline without friction.

Ajax cart or cart-drawer hooks to catch the add-to-cart event. Optional product metafield for eligibility. Optional video hosting. No app was specified in the ticket.

what.text: A reusable theme section with a draggable before/after (compare) slider. Two images of the same product (e.g. the same bag with two different flaps) sit on top of each other and a vertical handle reveals one or the other as the visitor drags it. A subheading and heading (with an underlined accent word) sit above the image. Each compare item has its own short caption (Lorem / Lorem ipsum) at the bottom-left and bottom-right. why.text: Interactive comparison turns passive scrolling into engagement and lets shoppers see product variants or interchangeable parts side by side without leaving the page. This makes the value of the modular or 2-for-1 offer tangible, reduces choice paralysis ('classy or unique?') and reduces uncertainty about what they will get. Dragging the handle creates a small commitment and curiosity loop that increases time on page and intent to click the CTA.

Set heights per device, image style (Cover/Contain), corner radius, text and button colors, font sizes and fonts, and section width (Container/Full). Use the max-width setting to shrink the section on desktop (e.g. 950px). Because the store hit the theme limit, it was added directly to the live theme and hidden until approved.

name: Conversion-Optimized PDP Template (Gallery Labels, Savings Badge, Variant Picker, Info Box, Rating Sliders, Cross-Sell, Comparison Table)
status: Built — live on Ardap; cross-sell variant selection still open with client

what.text: A complete product page template built 1:1 from a Figma mockup, mostly from existing Sectionfy.io sections plus a few custom-coded ones. The gallery has a label ("Mit Langzeitwirkung"), a video thumbnail and an info bar below the image ("Wirkt sofort und dauerhaft bis zu 6 Wochen"). The buy box contains: a social-proof strip ("Kian, Max & 20.000+ andere lieben ARDAP"), title, short description with check-mark bullets, star rating, compare-at price with unit price in brackets and a single-line green "Du sparst - 20%" badge, a size variant picker with a "Bestseller" tag, a stock line, and a blue collapsible "Abgabegespräch erforderlich" box with an embedded video. Below that come a compact quantity selector, an orange Add-to-Cart button, an outlined "Zum Storefinder" button, a payment icon row, slider-style rating bars (Wirkungsdauer / Effektivität / Einfache Anwendung), a "Ergänzende Produkte" cross-sell row and a "PRO vs Repell" comparison table. Above the page sit a slideshow announcement bar and an optional breadcrumb.

why.text: The page stacks several conversion levers in the order a buyer's questions arise. Social proof and the benefit label build trust at first glance. A visible strike-through price, a savings badge and a "Bestseller" tag anchor value and steer the size choice. A stock line and an info box with video reduce uncertainty for a product that requires a handover consultation. A prominent single ATC plus a secondary store-finder button capture both online and offline buyers. Payment logos reduce checkout anxiety. Rating sliders and the comparison table answer "which product is right for me?" without leaving the page. The cross-sell row lifts AOV, and legally required unit prices in brackets keep the page compliant.

how.text: 1) Duplicate the live theme and build on a copy. 2) Assemble the product template from existing Sectionfy.io / CRO sections, as the theme editor shows: Media Label, Media info, Description, Bulletpoints, Social Proof, Product Review Badge, Variant picker, Inventory, Collapsible box, Custom Liquid, Buy buttons, a Button ("Zum Storefinder"), Store benefits. 3) Custom-code the sections that do not exist yet: the rating sliders, the PRO vs Repell comparison table and the cross-sell block. 4) Render the price as: compare-at (struck through), current price, unit price in a single pair of brackets, and a one-line savings badge. Recalculate the savings % per selected variant. 5) For cross-sell, pick the products through a product metafield on each product, and show the compare-at price and unit price in brackets. 6) Handle sold-out states: red/neutral label instead of green, no green check on the inventory line, and the sold-out button colour matching the label. 7) Each product has its own template, so port the main-product section JSON from the reference template to the others.

name: PDP Collapsible Info Box with Tooltip & Video
status: Built — documented (Slite doc reviewed, product image added)

what.text: A colored info box placed in the PDP buy box, near the variant picker and ATC button. It shows a bold heading with an optional '?' tooltip icon, a short text paragraph and an optional video with a poster image and play button. The box can be made collapsible: a chevron at the right toggles it open or closed, and it can open by default. Content is set per product via metafields, so the box only appears on products that have data. Examples: 'Handover meeting required' on the ARDAP pest-control spray and a similar test on a demo store.

why.text: It puts product-specific information (conditions, requirements, usage or handover notes) right at the decision point, so surprises don't appear after the click. The tooltip adds detail on demand without cluttering the page. A short video explains complex or advice-heavy products better than text and builds trust. The collapsible mode keeps the buy box compact for users who don't need the details. The tinted, bordered box makes the message stand out from surrounding content.

how.text: 1) In main-product.liquid, add the schema block 'CRO | Collapsible box' (type cro_pdp_collapsible_box, limit 1). 2) Create the snippet ed-cro-pdp-collapsible-box.liquid. It renders only if the product metafield standard.pdp_collapsible_box exists. It outputs scoped CSS from the block settings, the heading with an optional tooltip (pure CSS, data-tip, hover/focus), the paragraph, and a video with poster and play overlay. 3) If 'Enable Collapsible' is on, the content is wrapped in a button/accordion with an animated chevron (aria-expanded) and a small JS toggle script; otherwise it is always open. 4) Render the snippet from the block in the PDP template, then fill the metafield per product. Following feedback, content entry was changed from one raw JSON to separate fields (title, tooltip content, text content, video, video thumbnail) via a metaobject-style structure. The full code is in the ticket attachment (the JS part of the snippet is truncated in the source).

name: PDP Product Comparison Chart (Metaobject-driven)
status: Built — launched (reusable setup guide delivered; documented in Slite)

what.text: A theme-editor block on the product page that shows a side-by-side comparison of two products. It has a centered title and subtitle, then a table. The left column holds row labels (e.g. product group, availability, mechanism of action, target use, long-term effect, purchase conditions). The right side shows two product columns on a grey background, each with a product image, a bold product name and one value per row. On mobile the product columns scroll horizontally.

why.text: A comparison chart helps visitors who are unsure which variant or product fits them. It cuts decision effort and choice overload, and it answers pre-purchase questions on the page so shoppers don't leave to look elsewhere. Putting the current product next to a close alternative also supports cross-selling and reduces wrong-product purchases and returns. Consistent row labels make differences easy to scan.

how.text: 1) Duplicate the theme first. 2) Create the metaobject definition 'CRO | PDP | Compare chart' (type cro_pdp_compare_chart) with fields: name (display name, required), title, content, chart_heading_list (list of single-line text), product_01/02 image (file), product_01/02 heading, and product_01/02 content list (list of single-line text). 3) Create a product metafield 'CRO | PDP | Compare chart' (namespace/key standard.cro_pdp_compare_chart), type Mixed reference, pointing to the metaobject. If Mixed reference is unavailable, use a Reference to the metaobject instead. 4) Add the schema block 'cro_compare_chart' (limit 1) to sections/main-product.liquid. 5) Create the snippet ed-cro-pdp-compare-chart.liquid, which renders the header, the heading column and a two-column product grid. The table is a 2-column grid (144px label column, 120px on mobile) and the product columns scroll horizontally at 70% width (85% on mobile). 6) In the product form snippet, loop over section.blocks and render the snippet for the 'cro_compare_chart' block type. 7) Assign the metaobject entry to each product via its metafield, then test on the duplicate theme before publishing. The block only renders when the product metafield is set.

items: Content (via metaobject): title, subtitle, row-label list, and for each of 2 products an image, heading and list of row values

dependencies.text: Needs a Shopify Online Store 2.0 theme with a product section that supports blocks (e.g. main-product.liquid) and a product form snippet. Requires the metaobject definition 'CRO | PDP | Compare chart' and the product metafield standard.cro_pdp_compare_chart (Mixed reference, or Reference as a fallback). Each product needs a metaobject entry assigned. Rows of the two products must line up with the shared heading list. The snippet is hard-coded for exactly 2 products. No app required. Developer-oriented install, so the setup guide was rewritten for non-developers.

items: Click-through to the alternative product (if linked)
Scroll depth and engagement with the chart (horizontal scroll on mobile)

name: Announcement Bar with Slideshow (Trust/Rating Ticker)
status: Built — code archived for reuse (originally from ARDAP PDP test)

what.text: A full-width colored bar at the very top of the page (above the header) that shows up to 5 short message items in a Swiper-based slider. Each item can combine a bold title, 5 rating stars, a content line (e.g. '4.9 ★★★★★ over 10,000 reviews') and an icon (uploaded image or inline SVG) placed left or right. On desktop 1–4 items are visible at once; on mobile one item is shown with prev/next arrows. The bar can be non-sticky or sticky on desktop, mobile or everywhere.

why.text: Placing review ratings and key benefit messages in the first thing the visitor sees delivers social proof and trust immediately, before they scroll. A high-contrast brand-colored bar draws attention without taking much space. The slider lets several messages (reviews, shipping, guarantee) share one slot. A sticky option keeps the trust signal visible while scrolling.

how.text: Create a section 'announcement-bar.liquid' with up to 5 'Item' blocks. The section renders a custom element <ed-announcement-bar> containing a Swiper container; each block becomes a swiper-slide with a list of icon, title, optional 5 stars (rendered via the theme's 'icon' snippet 'rating-star'), and content text. Swiper 11 CSS/JS is loaded lazily from jsDelivr and initialised with slidesPerView 1 on mobile and a configurable number from 768px up. Navigation arrows are shown, and hidden on desktop when all blocks fit in the view. Autoplay setting toggles 'loop'. Sticky behavior is done with CSS position: sticky and CSS variables (--announcement-bar-height, --enable-sticky-announcement-bar) which other header code can use for offsets; height is also measured via JS. Colors are passed as RGB CSS variables. Add the section to the header group in the theme editor.

Uses hard-coded bar heights (33px mobile / 41px desktop) for sticky offset. Original ticket wish-list (arrow color, content size, section paddings, slideshow on mobile/desktop/all) is only partially in the code: arrow color is hard-coded white, padding is hard-coded 7px. name: Free Gift Progress Bar with Quantity-Locked Gift Line Item (Cart Drawer)
status: Built — launched as A/B test; quantity-selector bug fixed 2025-06-30

what.text: A free-gift incentive in the cart drawer. A progress bar with two milestones (a free-shipping truck icon at mid-point and a gift icon at the end) shows how close the customer is to a reward. Once the threshold is reached, a message reads 'Congratulations! Add your free gift!'. The gift then appears as a normal cart line item named '<Product> - FREE GIFT'. It shows the variant (e.g. 'Veredelung: Gold') and the price as 'Kostenlos' (free) next to the struck-through original price (€19.90). The gift's quantity is capped at 1 and its quantity selector is disabled.

why.text: Reward-based progress bars use the goal-gradient effect: customers add items to reach the next milestone, which raises AOV. A free gift reframes the spend as a gain, and the struck-through €19.90 next to 'Free' anchors its perceived value. Capping the gift at 1 keeps the offer credible and protects margin; allowing several free gifts would break the logic of the promotion.

how.text: 1) Add a multi-step progress bar to the cart drawer, with icon milestones for free shipping and the gift, driven by cart subtotal versus the thresholds. 2) Show a congratulation message when the gift threshold is reached. 3) Add the gift product/variant to the cart as a line item priced at €0 (via discount or a zero-price gift variant) and label it 'FREE GIFT' with 'Kostenlos' plus the struck-through compare-at price. 4) Lock the gift line's quantity to a maximum of 1 by disabling the +/- selector (greyed out, fixed at 1). The ticket confirms the fix was made to the quantity selector; the exact mechanism is not described. 5) Optionally harden the lock against quantity changes via cart AJAX calls and against removing the gift while the threshold is still met.

name: Cart Drawer Up-/Cross-Sell Block (Product-Metafield Driven)
status: Built — launched (customer-approved Aug 2025)

what.text: A 'Goes perfectly with it' (German: 'Passt perfekt dazu') up-sell/cross-sell block inside the cart drawer. It shows a headline, a social-proof sub-headline ('8 out of 10 customers also buy'), and a vertical list (or carousel, depending on the display setting) of recommended products. Each product shows an image, title, star rating, current and compare-at price, a green 'You save X €' note, and a yellow 'ADD' button. Products are chosen per cart item through a product metafield 'Cart upsell' (a list of products). If the product in the cart has no metafield value, the block falls back to the global theme-settings list 'Cart upsell products'.

why.text: Shoppers are at their highest purchase intent in the cart, so a one-click add of a complementary item raises AOV with little friction. The sub-headline uses a social-proof claim ('8 of 10 customers also buy'), which normalises the add-on. Star ratings reduce doubt about the extra item. The struck-through price with the green 'You save' amount frames the add-on as a deal. Metafield-driven selection keeps recommendations relevant to the specific cart item (e.g., a bathroom set suggests the ALL IN set and the refill bottle), which beats a generic list.

how.text: 1) Create a product metafield 'Cart upsell' (list of product references). 2) In the cart drawer snippet, loop over cart items and collect the products referenced in each item's metafield, skipping items already in the cart. 3) If no metafield products are found, fall back to the theme-settings 'Cart upsell products' product list. 4) Render each card with a snippet (upsell-product-temp) showing image (6x6rem), title, rating snippet, price/compare-at price/savings, and an Add button that adds via the cart AJAX API. 5) Expose theme settings for layout, copy, colours and toggles for teaser, price and reviews. The star-rating snippet link had to be fixed so reviews display correctly.

Product metafield 'Cart upsell' (list of products, set per product)

why.text: The homepage has a different job from inner pages. Mobile keeps the drawer built from the main menu. 4) Fall back to the main menu if no homepage menu is selected. 5) In the theme editor, create or choose the menu in Shopify Navigation, then select it in Header > Homepage menu. The ticket says integration is 'very simple': one extra input field. The fallback and the desktop/mobile split are inferred.

name: PDP Gallery Image Info Button (Caption + Tooltip)
status: Built — launched (client setup/usability feedback ongoing)

what.text: A caption bar sits directly under the main PDP product image. It shows a short line of text (e.g. a product or image note) with a round "i" info icon on the right. Tapping or hovering the icon opens a small tooltip bubble with the same or extended text, pointing at the icon. The text is set per product (via a product metafield 'info buttons') and can be shown for specific gallery images.

why.text: Short image-level notes answer small questions at the moment the shopper is looking at the image, e.g. what is included, a size or usage note, or a disclaimer. This reduces uncertainty and the need to scroll to the description. The tooltip is progressive disclosure: the page stays clean and detail is available on demand. This is an inference; the ticket does not state the reasoning.

how.text: Add a product metafield (single-line text, 'info buttons') in the Shopify admin under Product metafields. The theme's gallery media block reads it and renders a caption row under the image, with an 'i' icon that toggles a tooltip. Per the comments, the first version showed one text on all images. It was later reworked so individual points can be created and sorted and assigned to specific images, with a video walkthrough as the client guide. The layout is fixed: the position can be above the image, at the top or bottom, or underneath it. Colour, background colour and font size are editable in the theme customizer. Fully unique content per image or product needs a metafield or image alt-text solution. The exact structure of the reworked multi-point setup is only shown in Loom videos, which are not visible here.

what.text: A compact banner block placed directly above the product title on the PDP, with two switchable types. 'Social' shows up to 5 overlapping round avatars next to an influencer/name line plus a social proof sentence, e.g. 'matiamu and 63,000 others are thrilled by us', with an optional Instagram verified checkmark. 'Rating' shows a review sentence with star icons, e.g. '18,386+ customers rated us 5 stars ★★★★★', where the '(rating)' placeholder in the text is replaced by star icons.

why.text: Placing the proof right at the top of the buy box, before the title and price, builds trust early. The Rating variant uses a concrete review count and a 5-star score as quantified proof, which reduces perceived purchase risk.

how.text: Build a custom Shopify theme block (named 'CRO | Social Proof') for the product information section, positioned above the title. Social: upload up to 5 avatar images, enter the influencer name(s), toggle the Instagram checkmark, enter rich text content and optionally bold it. Rating: enter rich text with the '(rating)' token, which the Liquid/JS replaces with the star icons in the rating color. Style options cover colors, border and rounded/corners shape. Spacing and font size are set separately for desktop and mobile. Text fields can be dynamic-source enabled (database icon), which suggests metafield support. The name and the text are separate fields, so avoid extra whitespace between them (a customer-reported bug).

status: Built — delivered to client, tested and approved (Carl Henkel dev theme)

what.text: A bundle of two cart-drawer sections ordered by Sectionfy for Carl Henkel. (1) A progress bar with three milestones (a free-shipping truck icon and two gift icons). It shows a live message such as 'Only €X to go until your free gift!', and below it a 'Free gift' card with the gift product, the label 'Für dich gratis' and an Add button. (2) An up/cross-sell block titled 'Fits perfectly' with the line '8 out of 10 customers also buy', a carousel with arrows, product name and an Add button. Tapping Add on a product with variants opens a bottom-sheet variant picker (image, title, price, size options, full-width 'Add to cart' button).

why.text: The progress bar uses the goal-gradient effect: the closer the shopper gets to a visible reward, the more motivated they are to add to the cart. A free gift is perceived as more valuable than an equivalent discount and increases AOV. The cross-sell block uses a social-proof line ('8 of 10 customers also buy') and a low-friction one-tap add to raise items per order. Showing the gift as clearly free removes price confusion.

how.text: Build as a cart-drawer section/app block in the theme. Compute the gap between cart subtotal and the gift threshold and render the progress fill, milestone icons and message from it. Show a 'Free gift' card with the configured gift product. Add it to the cart at €0 only once the threshold is reached (the Add button appears greyed out before then). In the cart line, the gift's price must NOT be shown (the client was confused by '€50' next to the free gift), and it should be clearly labelled as free. Render the cross-sell as a carousel of recommended products. For products with variants, open a bottom-sheet variant picker with selectable size options, and make sure all variants (e.g. 0.6 l) are selectable. Use the store's body font (Futura) across all new UI. Also reduce spacing in the drawer. The exact implementation is not in the ticket, so this is inferred from the comments and screenshots.

what.text: Product cards in the collection grid get two upgrades. (1) A swipeable image gallery on each card, with a thin progress bar under the image on mobile and no dots or arrows. This follows the LFDY reference, and the bar is meant to signal that more images exist. (2) A Quick Add to Cart (QATC) button, a cart-bag icon at the bottom-right of the image, that opens a size selector and adds to cart without leaving the grid. After adding, the cart drawer opens. The card also shows badges (NEW, BESTSELLER, AUSVERKAUFT), title and price. This record bundles two sections from a multi-section order, 'CRO | CP | Product Slider' and 'CRO | CP | Quick Add to Cart (Fashion)'. The ticket text only lists the order as linked subtasks, so the detail comes from the comments.

why.text: Showing more product images in the grid lets shoppers judge fit and look without a PDP visit, which reduces friction and sharpens their choice. A subtle bar under the image signals that more images exist without cluttering the card, which matters on mobile. QATC shortens the path to purchase for shoppers who already know what they want, and opening the cart drawer afterwards keeps momentum toward checkout.

how.text: 1) Add a product-card media slider to the collection grid. Enable swipe on mobile and hide dots and arrows. Render a thin (1px) indicator bar under the image, left-aligned on the first image like the LFDY reference. Show the bar only when a product has multiple images. Desktop hover can alternatively show the 2nd image. 2) Add a QATC button using the theme's default cart icon, so it matches the header cart icon. It opens a variant (size) selector with the same size and corner style as the PDP. The variant selector is left-aligned with the ATC button and the label text comes from theme content ('Size'). The article-specific hint in the popup is read from product.metafields.standard.size_guide_hint. After a successful add, trigger the sidebar cart drawer. 3) Make the QATC a theme-editor toggle; it was disabled on desktop (about 5% of users) and kept on mobile. Keep product images clickable through to the PDP.

name: Collection Grid Quick Add to Cart (with Mobile Bottom Size Picker)
status: Built — merged into live theme (disabled by default, client decides when to enable)

what.text: A small cart/bag icon in the bottom-right corner of each product card image in the collection grid. Tapping it lets shoppers add a product straight from the grid without opening the PDP. On mobile, the variant (size) selector slides up as a bar at the bottom of the screen with size buttons (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL) and a close (X) button. Sold-out sizes show an envelope icon (apparently a back-in-stock notification). It is available as a theme setting called 'Quick Add to Cart (custom)' under 'Products grid'.

why.text: It removes steps between browsing and adding to cart (collection → PDP → select size → add). Less friction means more add-to-carts, especially on mobile, where page loads are costly. A bottom-anchored picker sits in the thumb zone and keeps the shopper in the browsing context. Showing every size, including sold-out ones with a notify option, sets clear availability expectations and captures demand.

how.text: Add a quick-add button, absolutely positioned bottom-right on the product card media, and render it conditionally from a theme setting under 'Products grid' (disabled by default). On click, show variant options. On desktop, the selector appears within or on the card. On mobile, it appears as a fixed bottom sheet or bar. Selecting a size posts to /cart/add.js and updates the cart count and drawer. Render ALL variants, not only the first few, because the client reported that sizes above L were missing even though XL and XXL were in stock. Mark unavailable variants distinctly, with a notify icon. Inherit the theme font-family instead of hardcoding it. Size the icon separately for mobile and desktop: on mobile it was too large and overlapped the product images, and on desktop it was slightly too small. Make sure it stays visible on dark product images (the black hoodie).

Icon size (separate for mobile and desktop) and placement over the product image
Mobile: bottom-sheet size selector instead of an in-card popup

name: Product Image Slider with Progress-Bar / Dot Indicator
status: Built — approved by PM 2025-11-14, cleared to merge into live theme

what.text: A swipeable product image slider with a minimal position indicator. On collection product cards (desktop and mobile) a thin black progress bar sits under each image, with the bar length reflecting how many images the product has. On the mobile PDP, the bar is replaced by subtle dots (active dot black, inactive dots light grey) in the style of the LFDY reference. Desktop was approved with the LFDY-style layout.

why.text: A visible position indicator signals that more images exist and shows where the shopper is in the set, which encourages swiping and exploring (more product visuals reduce uncertainty). Minimal indicators keep the product imagery clean and premium for a fashion brand. On the PDP, dots are a familiar mobile pattern and are less visually heavy than a bar sitting under the hero image.

how.text: Build the product card/PDP media as a scroll-snap or Swiper-type slider. Render a progress-bar indicator on collection cards and desktop, with the thumb width set to 100% divided by the number of slides and its position following scroll progress. On the mobile PDP template, switch the indicator to circle dots: the active dot is black and the others light grey, centred at the bottom of the image. The ticket's reference for the dots is the LFDY PDP.

name: A/B Test-Ready Section Visibility Toggle ("Display Section")
status: Built — checkbox added to 14 Sectionfy sections (Sept 2025); coverage of any other sections unconfirmed

what.text: A "Display Section" toggle in the theme-editor settings of each Sectionfy section. When it is switched off, the section is hidden by default for all visitors. An A/B testing tool can then reveal it for the variant group only, by injecting a short CSS override. The setting is built into every existing section, so a test can be set up without any theme-code changes.

why.text: This element does not persuade shoppers directly. It removes the setup effort for tests of the sections it is attached to, such as social proof banners, upsells, free-gift bars and store benefits. Tests can launch faster and more cleanly, with no flicker or theme duplication. The control group never sees the section, and the variant group sees it only once the CSS is injected. That gives a clean split and more tests per month, which compounds into conversion and AOV gains over time.

how.text: 1) In each section's schema, add a boolean setting "Display Section" (default on). 2) When it is off, the section outputs CSS that hides its wrapper (display:none), using the section's wrapper class such as .shopify-section-story-icon-slider. 3) Leave the toggle off in the theme. 4) In the A/B tool (e.g. Convert, VWO or Shopify-native tools), add the variant CSS from the helper text: .shopify-section-<section-name> { display: block !important; }. 5) Run the test, then switch the toggle on permanently if the variant wins. The lead developer estimated about 5 minutes per section, and the setting must be added to each section individually.

items: Display Section (on/off toggle, default on) — off hides the section for everyone
Helper text in the editor shows the exact CSS override to paste into the A/B tool, using the section's own wrapper class (e.g. .shopify-section-story-icon-slider { display: block !important; })

dependencies.text: Requires a Sectionfy-based Shopify theme and an A/B testing tool that can inject custom CSS for the variant. No metafields or apps are needed for the toggle itself. The CSS class name differs per section. Sections covered per the developer's comment: Announcement bar, Sub-collections, Testimonial Videos, CP product slider, PDP Store benefits, PDP Styling of payment bar, PDP Social proof banner, Cart Reservation Label, Cart Upsell, Cart Free Gift, Cart Store Benefits, Cart Styling of Payment Bar, Cart Promo Banner, Video Play Button Thank you.

Number of tests launched per month

name: Section Spacing Controls (Spacing Section + per-section margin/padding)
status: Built — merged into live theme (Nordlichtstore)

what.text: Two related spacing tools for a Shopify theme. (1) A standalone 'Spacing Section' that can be dropped between any two sections to add a blank band of vertical space, with its own background color, text color, top/bottom space in px, and separate mobile top/bottom space. (2) Desktop and mobile margin and padding sliders added to every existing section (99 in this theme). Margins can go negative and default to 0, so spacing can be reduced or removed, which the standalone section cannot do.

why.text: Spacing and visual rhythm decide whether page blocks read as one coherent flow or as cramped or disconnected pieces. Fine control over whitespace makes it faster to test layout variants: tighter spacing to pull key content above the fold, or more breathing room to separate offers. This is a utility with no direct conversion mechanism, so the lift comes indirectly from faster, cleaner A/B test builds.

how.text: Spacing Section: create a section with color pickers for background and text, range sliders for top and bottom space (desktop, e.g. 100px), and a 'Mobile settings' group with its own sliders (e.g. 50px), all rendered as padding on a wrapper div. Per-section controls: add a shared spacing snippet or schema block to every section file. It provides 'Desktop spacing' (Top/Bottom Margin, Top/Bottom Padding) and 'Mobile spacing' (the same four fields), output as scoped CSS variables or inline styles. Margin sliders allow negative values and default to 0, and padding defaults match each section's existing spacing so the live layout doesn't change. Set a section's top padding to 0 to close unwanted gaps. Work in a duplicated theme connected to GitHub, then merge to the live theme.

items: Spacing Section: background color (e.g. #F6A429 in the demo)
Spacing Section: text color (can be transparent)
Spacing Section: top space (px) and bottom space (px) on desktop
Spacing Section: top space (mobile) and bottom space (mobile) in px
All sections: desktop Top Margin and Bottom Margin (negative allowed, default 0)
All sections: desktop Top Padding and Bottom Padding (e.g. 64px on Featured collections)
All sections: mobile Top Margin, Bottom Margin, Top Padding and Bottom Padding (e.g. 36px padding on Featured collections)

dependencies.text: Custom Shopify theme (Nordlichtstore, based on theme version 8.11.4) with editable section files and a GitHub-connected theme branch. No apps or metafields. The negative margin and padding schema has to be added to every section file (99 sections, about 4+ hours of dev work). Existing sections' default padding values must be preserved to avoid layout regressions.

items: Conversion rate of the A/B variant that uses layout/spacing changes
Scroll depth and visibility of key blocks (e.g. products above the fold)
Bounce rate on pages where spacing was changed
Dev time to ship a layout test (internal efficiency)

The list can sit in a tinted box with a border and rounded corners. The example shows a bundle PDP with six bullets: set savings, kitchen-front cleaner, bathroom cleaner, universal cleaning stone, signature scent, and a good-conscience guarantee (biodegradable, free of microplastics and dyes).

why.text: Shoppers skim the buy box and decide quickly. Placing the 4-6 strongest reasons to buy next to the price answers 'why this, why now?' before they scroll. Bold lead phrases make the list scannable, and the icons and tinted box set it apart from the plain-text description. Bullets that mention the saving and a guarantee (a sustainability or safety promise) also lower price and risk doubts at the moment of decision.

how.text: Add the 'CRO | Bulletpoints' block to the Product information section in the theme editor. Put it under Star Rating and Price and above the variant picker and buy buttons (in the example it sits above the USPs/Infobox blocks). Write the headline in the rich-text Title field. Add the bullets with the lead phrase in bold. Set the list style to SVG and add an icon, either as an uploaded image or pasted inline SVG code. Turn on the border and set the border colour, corner radius and background colour to match the brand. Use Space top, Space bottom and Gap items to tune the spacing. Use this block instead of the older 'USPs' block. According to the developer, both do the same job, but Bulletpoints has more styling options such as a background and border.

items: Gap between items (10 px in example)
List style (SVG; the icon settings are required for this style)
Icon as image (upload or pick from free images)
Bullet items with bold lead phrase and text

dependencies.text: Needs a theme that includes the custom 'CRO | Bulletpoints' block in the Product information section. No app is visible in the source. An icon asset (image or SVG code) is needed for the SVG list style. The older 'USPs' block still exists in the theme and overlaps with it; whether bullet text is stored in block settings or in metafields is not shown.

items: Revenue per visitor / AOV (especially on bundle PDPs)
Scroll depth and interaction in the buy box
Bounce rate / exit rate on PDP

name: PDP Product Compare Chart (Horizontal Carousel, BuyBox + Full-Width)
status: Built — launched (live theme, client-approved)

what.text: A comparison table on the PDP headed by a question such as "Which product is right for you?". The first column holds row labels (Special feature, Mode of action, Works against, Duration, Application area). Each further column is a product with image, title and attribute values. The current product comes first, followed by up to 5 selectable products. Columns scroll horizontally, with prev/next arrows on desktop. There are two variants: a compact one inside the BuyBox and a full-width one placed anywhere on the PDP outside the BuyBox. Both can sit on the same page and work independently.

why.text: Side-by-side comparison lowers choice overload and helps shoppers pick the right variant or product without leaving the PDP. Spelling out the differences (use case, duration, target pests) reduces the risk of a wrong purchase and returns. It also exposes cross-sell or upsell alternatives at the moment of decision. The question-style heading frames the table as guidance.

how.text: Build the BuyBox version as a block (snippet) in the product info area, e.g. 'CRO | Compare chart'. Build the full-width version as a separate section, with its own unique code and scoped JS/CSS so the two never conflict. Each merchant picks up to 5 products in the theme editor, and attribute rows come from content fields. Use a horizontal scroll container with a sticky label column and prev/next arrow buttons. Hide arrows on mobile (touch swipe only), and show arrows on desktop for the BuyBox version. Hide the empty grey placeholder columns when fewer products are selected.

Auto-hide empty columns when fewer products are chosen

name: Sub-Collection Bubble Navigation (Full-Width Row)
status: Built — live in theme editor (alignment and gap settings visible)

what.text: A Sectionfy 'Sub-collections' section that shows a row of clickable collection shortcuts, each a circular image with a label underneath. In the screenshots it sits directly under the press-logo bar on the homepage and links to Starter Set, Refill Pack - 60 Stk, Fastenzeit 2025 and Bio Gemüsebrühe. The ticket title ('Sub-Collection auf gesamte Breite') says the row should use the full content width. In the screenshots this is handled through the 'Gap between items' and 'Alignment' (Left/Center) settings.

why.text: Image bubbles above the fold give visitors a fast, visual way to jump to the product group they want, which shortens the path to a product and reduces decision effort. Spreading the row evenly across the full width makes every option equally visible and looks deliberate rather than crammed into the left corner. Showing seasonal or bundle collections such as 'Fastenzeit 2025' and 'Starter Set' on the homepage also pushes high-intent offers, which can lift AOV.

how.text: Add the Sectionfy 'Sub-collections' section to the template, below the hero or logo bar, then click 'Add Collection' for each bubble. Set Style to 'Show bubbles' and Image style to Circle. Set image size to about 80px on desktop and 65px on mobile. Increase 'Gap between items' (the slider goes up to 100px) and choose Alignment Left or Center so the row spans the full width. Keep the gap small on mobile (about 10px). Use Custom CSS for fine adjustments if needed.

name: Sidebar + Article Glossary Section with Embedded Product Card
status: Built — launched (rebuilt as block-based after a metaobject attempt failed)

what.text: A long-form article / encyclopedia section ("CRO | Sidebar + Article") with a left sidebar and a main content column. The sidebar shows an anchor navigation (e.g. "Verstehen & Erkennen", "Von Ei bis Kolonie", "Anzeichen für einen Befall", "Natürlich gegen Ameisen vorgehen", with the active item underlined). Below the navigation sits a product card (image, title, price, "Schnellansicht" quick-view button). Each article block in the main column has an optional image, an uppercase heading and rich-text content. A block can instead show a "Recommended product" badge, a short bullet list and an inline horizontal product card. It was built for a pest-control glossary (Green Guardia) where tiles on the collection page link to these detailed pest articles.

why.text: Educational content builds expertise and trust at the moment a shopper is diagnosing a problem (e.g. which pest they have). A persistent sidebar nav makes long articles easy to scan and lowers bounce. The product card sits right next to the 'problem → solution' content, so the shopper meets the matching product (e.g. an ant repellent spray) when intent is highest. A quick-view button keeps them in the reading flow instead of sending them to the PDP.

how.text:
Build one section with repeatable blocks, where each block is one article chapter. Block fields: image, image size, badge text, aside navigation text (the label in the sidebar), heading (HTML
allowed) with a heading-size selector, rich-text content, and an optional product picker. Section settings: a product shown in the sidebar, content max-width, corner radius, padding, product-card options and mobile spacing. The sidebar nav is generated from the blocks' 'Aside Navigation Text'. Use blocks, NOT a metaobject: a metaobject's entries appear on every page that uses it, so content cannot be unique per page. Each page therefore needs its own blocks, added through the theme customizer. Shopify allows at most 50 blocks per section, so split very large glossaries across several sections or pages. The sidebar sticky behaviour and active-link highlighting are implied by the screenshots but not described in the ticket.

items:
Block: Heading (HTML
for line breaks) + Heading size (H5 shown)
Block: Content (rich text with bold, links, lists)
Main Article: content max-width toggle, Max-width (800px), Corner radius (0), Padding (40px)
Product card: Show vendor, Hide price, Show secondary image on hover, Show product rating (checkbox added so it can be disabled when no reviews exist), Product image size (Natural)
Mobile: Top space and Bottom space (px)

The product rating display needs a reviews app and should stay off without one. No metafields or metaobjects are required in the final version. The earlier metaobject solution was deleted because it could not hold per-page content. The client's store theme is not connected to GitHub, so JSON template data and content cannot be restored after an overwrite. Recommend connecting the theme to Git and backing up before structural changes.

name: Typeform Quiz Button (PDP, Metafield-Driven)
status: Built — launched (live theme: Focal)

what.text: A configurable button placed above the variant selector on the product page. Clicking it opens a Typeform survey/quiz (here a 'card calculator' that tells the shopper how many cards they need). The screenshot shows a rounded pill button with a speech-bubble question-mark icon and the label 'Wie viele Karten brauche ich?' (How many cards do I need?). The button is hidden by default and only appears on products with a Typeform form ID set in a product metafield.

why.text: Helps shoppers who are unsure about quantity or fit to get a tailored recommendation right where they choose a variant. This reduces choice uncertainty and the risk of buying the wrong amount, and can raise AOV by recommending larger bundles. The interactive quiz also adds engagement and a sense of personalised guidance. Note: this is inferred; the ticket does not state a rationale.

how.text: Build it as a theme block (named 'CRO | TypeForm Button') in the product page template, positioned above the Variant picker. The block loads the Typeform embed script (//embed.typeform.com/next/embed.js) and renders a data-tf-live widget, using the form ID from a product metafield (standard.typeform_form_id) rather than a hardcoded ID. Show the block only when the metafield has a value. To set it up, enter the Typeform form ID (just the ID, e.g. 01K4…, not the full embed snippet) in the product's metafield. The block must be added to the product template in the specific theme in use. It was built for the 'Focal [Live]' theme, and the button did not appear in a different theme where the block was missing.

name: Reviews.io Star Ratings (Announcement Bar + PDP Buybox + Product Cards)
status: Built — live on Green Guardia, awaiting customer feedback

what.text: Reviews.io rating data is shown as social proof in three places. (1) Announcement bar: a Reviews.io widget with a star icon, average score and review count (e.g. '4.5/5 1649+ Bewertungen'), set up for this client to show aggregated product reviews rather than shop reviews. The link to the Reviews.io company page can be switched off so the bar is display-only. (2) PDP buybox: a 'Ratings Snippet' / 'Rating Bar' block with filled stars and review count between the product title and price, plus a full 'Product Reviews Widget' app block further down the page. (3) Product cards on Home, Collection and other product listings: a custom snippet that shows each product's Reviews.io rating between the product name and the price. Clicking the stars opens the full review list (average, review count, sort, search, verified-buyer reviews, 'write a review' button).

why.text: Star ratings and review counts are among the strongest trust signals. They reduce perceived purchase risk at the moment of decision. A site-wide rating in the announcement bar builds brand credibility from the first pageview. Stars on product cards help shoppers compare and choose products while browsing. Stars in the buybox next to the price reinforce the decision at the point of purchase. Verified-buyer reviews in the pop-up add authenticity.

how.text: 1) Install Reviews.io and enable its app embed in Theme Settings > App embeds. Without this, nothing renders, even if the blocks are added in the editor. 2) Announcement bar: add the 'Reviews.io Widget' block inside the Announcement bar section. Set the keyword and widget link to the client's own Reviews.io account (check it is not a leftover URL from another store). Set text and star colors. Remove the link if the bar should not be clickable. 3) PDP: in the product template add the 'Ratings Snippet' (or 'Rating Bar') block directly under the title/price area of the buybox, and add the 'Product Reviews Widget' app block under Apps lower on the page. Each product template is separate, so repeat this for every template. 4) Product cards (Home, Collection, other listings): the theme has no native option for this, so a custom Liquid snippet renders the Reviews.io rating per product between name and price. Include the snippet in the card/product-grid templates. 5) Test on the live preview, not inside the theme customizer, which does not sync ratings correctly. If a rating still shows 0 stars, the store's sync with Reviews.io may need a test review created and approved in the Reviews.io dashboard.

name: Cart Free Gift & Free Shipping Progress Bar
status: Built — delivered and approved (client uses only the shipping bar; free gift hidden by default)

what.text: A progress bar at the top of the cart drawer that shows how close the customer is to reward thresholds. In the screenshots there are two milestones: a free gift at €80 and free shipping at €120. Each milestone has an icon pill (gift, truck) that gets a checkmark once reached. A dynamic message sits under the bar, e.g. 'Only €20.10 left until free shipping', 'You've unlocked free shipping!' or 'Congratulations! Add your free gift!'. When the gift threshold is met, the gift product appears in the cart as a line item at 100% off ('Kostenlos' with the original price struck through and a 'You save' note). The free gift part is optional. It is hidden until enabled in theme settings, so the bar can run as a pure shipping-progress bar.

why.text: The goal-gradient effect: people speed up as they get closer to a goal, so a visible gap ('only €20.10 left') pushes shoppers to add one more item and raises AOV. A free gift or free shipping works as a concrete, loss-averse reward, because customers don't want to miss out once they are close. Showing several milestones on one bar makes the reward ladder tangible. The strikethrough price and 'You save' text make the gift's value explicit. The icon and checkmark change on completion gives instant positive feedback.

how.text: Implement it in the cart drawer (the original build was made for the Focal theme). It compares the cart subtotal to the configured thresholds, fills the bar proportionally and swaps the message and icon states (default vs. active). The free-gift logic uses a minimum amount and a selected gift product, which can be added automatically or manually via a prompt. The gift line item is discounted 100%. Colors, border style and icons are editable under Theme settings > Cart > Progress Bar and Cart Free Gift. Message text is edited via Edit language > Cart > 'Free shipping remaining html'. In the final version the icons are uploaded as images (default and active) rather than pasted SVG code. Free gift settings stay hidden until enabled.

name: Custom Unit Price Label (Metafield Override)
status: Built — launched (merged into Live theme)

what.text: The unit price label shown next to the product price, such as "€2,00/item", can be replaced per product with custom text such as "Stück" ("piece"). The price and calculation still come from Shopify's native unit price calculator. Only the label text changes. The override appears on the PDP price row and on the cart drawer line item (e.g. "€19,90/Stück"). If the metafield is empty, the default Shopify label is shown.

why.text: Shopify's unit price measures are fixed (ml, l, m, m², kg, g, "Per item" and so on) and have no "piece" option. German shoppers therefore see the English word "item" in an otherwise German store. A mixed-language label looks unpolished and can reduce trust. A native-language unit label keeps the price easy to understand and the store consistent. The effect is small and mostly hygiene, but it matters for localized stores.

how.text: 1) Create a product metafield (definition) named "Unit Price Label" as single-line text. 2) In the theme's unit price snippet, which is used on the PDP price and the cart drawer, output the metafield value if it is present and otherwise fall back to the default Shopify unit measure label. 3) Keep the Shopify unit price calculator enabled (total measure / base measure with unit "Per item") so that the price math is still native. 4) Fill in "Stück" for the relevant products in the product metafields section. The original build was done in the development theme and then merged into the Live theme.

Native Shopify unit price (total measure, base measure) remains the source of the price value

name: Mobile Burger Menu with Image Icons, Accordion Sub-Navigation and Pinned Account Area

what.text: A restructured mobile burger (drawer) menu for a Shopify store on the Impact theme. Top-level items have round images in front of them and an arrow at the end. Tapping an item expands its sub-items downward as an accordion. Badges can sit in the bottom corner. Account and Login are placed in a fixed spot at the bottom. The groups are visually separated more clearly than in the original mobile menu, which was cluttered. The final sketch is not attached to the ticket, so this description comes from the comments.

why.text: On mobile the menu is often the main way to browse. A flat, crowded list forces extra scanning and taps, so visitors drop off before reaching a collection or product. Round images give quick visual cues, which cuts cognitive load and makes categories easier to recognise. Arrows signal that an item expands. Grouping and clear separation make a long hierarchy easier to scan. Putting account/login in a predictable place keeps secondary actions out of the way of the main navigation. Badges can draw attention to key items such as bundles or new products.

how.text: 1) Build the menu hierarchy in Shopify Navigation, with top-level items and nested children, as in the screenshot. 2) In the Impact theme's mobile drawer, add a round image or icon in front of each top-level link, using a menu-item image mapping or a custom Liquid snippet. 3) Add a chevron at the end of expandable items and make the children collapse and expand downward. 4) Add clear dividers or spacing between groups. 5) Add optional badge labels in the bottom corner. 6) Pin Account / Login at the bottom of the drawer. Impact's native mega-menu and drawer options only partly cover this, so custom Liquid/CSS is probably needed.

Round image or icon per top-level item

Account/Login placement at the bottom of the drawer

name: Hero Banner with Social Proof Pill, Headline, CTA and Product Mockup
status: Built — launched (Sectionfy.io store, Oct 2025)

what.text: A dark, full-width hero banner for the top of the homepage. Order of content: a small social-proof line (final copy: "€5,000,000 additional revenue from A/B-tested Sectionfy sections"), a large headline ("Shopify sections that sell"), a short sub-headline ("Our sections are based on real A/B test results and integrate into any Shopify theme in seconds"), and one bright green CTA button ("Discover all possibilities"). On the right (desktop) or below the text (mobile) sits a tilted phone mockup with floating UI cards that show the product's sections in use, for example a free-gift progress bar and a customer-count social-proof chip. A separate mobile image is used, with soft fades at the top and bottom edges so it blends into the page.

why.text: The social-proof line puts a hard, quantified result in front of the visitor before they read anything else, which builds credibility. The headline and sub-headline state the benefit (sections that sell, based on real A/B tests) and remove friction (fast integration). The product mockup shows the offer instead of describing it. A single high-contrast CTA gives a clear next step. The mobile fade avoids a hard visual break, so the page feels continuous and the content is easier to scan.

how.text: Design the hero as two images: a desktop banner (2800x1000 px) and a mobile banner (1200x1600 px). Upload them to the theme's image banner section, using the 'Image' and 'Mobile image' slots. Create the mockup (phone plus floating cards) in a design tool or 3D tool, and export a version with text and a version without. Preferred approach: keep the text (social-proof line, headline, sub-headline, CTA) as live Shopify text rather than baked into the image, so screen readers can read it and the copy is easy to edit. Export the images at full quality, because early uploads looked blurry. On mobile, add a gradient fade at the top and bottom of the image instead of a hard edge. Placing the heading on top of the image with no gap would need custom code, so the fade was chosen instead.

items: Text baked into the image vs. live Shopify text (live text recommended for accessibility)
Mobile edge fade (top and bottom) built into the mobile image

dependencies.text: Needs a theme banner section with separate desktop and mobile image pickers, which the Sectionfy theme already has. No app is needed. Text overlaid on the image, or a heading placed directly on the image with no gap, would need custom Liquid/CSS. The mockup artwork must be produced separately (design or 3D tool).

items: Conversion rate from homepage visit to purchase (or sign-up)
LCP / image load time (large hero images)

what.text: A strip of monochrome (white) customer brand logos, each 32px tall, shown on the homepage and product pages. why.text: Recognisable brand logos work as borrowed credibility. Visitors see that other shops already use the product and feel less risk. Well-known logos add the most trust. how.text: 1) Decide the logo mix (all big brands, all small brands, or a mix such as 3 well-known plus 5 smaller). 2) Collect SVG logo files from clients, because PNGs look pixelated and low-resolution files cause blur on mobile. 3) Make white/monochrome versions at 32px height. 4) Upload them in the Shopify theme editor into the scrolling-image section and add that section to the homepage and PDP template. 5) Check sharpness on desktop and mobile. Where no SVG existed, the logos were redrawn as SVG as a stopgap, and original client SVGs should still be collected.

name: PDP Gallery Review Collage Image (customer quotes + client logos)
status: Designed — client-approved (final with logos); awaiting live launch confirmation

what.text: A designed square image for the product gallery that works as a social-proof slide. A headline ("Our customers are convinced") sits above a row of grayed-out client/brand logos. Below that is a stack of 2–3 customer review cards. The front card is sharp and the cards behind it are tilted and blurred. Each card shows an avatar, name (with shop or company in brackets), a bold review title, 5 green stars and a short quote. An earlier version showed an aggregate rating (4.9/5, 100+) and a heart icon. Both were removed in the final version.

why.text: Real customer voices and recognisable brand logos reduce perceived risk right where the shopper is already looking at product images. Placing the proof in the gallery means it is seen without scrolling. The sharp front card plus blurred cards behind it suggest volume and make one quote easy to read. Named reviewers with photos and a company name feel more authentic than anonymous stars. The aggregate rating was removed because no real reviews had been collected yet, which avoids a credibility-damaging claim.

how.text: 1) Design the collage in Figma or a similar tool as a square image: headline, logo row, one sharp review card in front and 2 blurred, rotated cards behind it. 2) Fill the cards with real, approved customer quotes (name, company, title, 5 stars, avatar). 3) Add a row of client or partner logos in muted gray. 4) Only show an aggregate rating (e.g. 4.9/5 and review count) if it is real and verifiable. 5) Export the image and add it as a regular media slot in the PDP gallery, usually at position 2–4. The brief was to include 1 product image with 2–3 reviews. No theme code is needed.

Number of review cards (2–3, with 1 featured in front)
Review content per card: avatar, name + company, title, star rating, quote
Show/hide aggregate rating and review count (hide until real data exists)
Decorative accent such as the heart icon (removed in the final version)

dependencies.text: Real, approved customer reviews and avatars, plus permission to use client logos. A design tool to produce the image. A PDP gallery that accepts extra image slots, so no app is required. If the rating is shown, it needs a verified source.

why.text: Short, scannable benefit bullets near the title and CTA state the core value proposition at the moment of decision, which reduces uncertainty without extra reading.
