name: How It Works – 3-Step Accordion Section
status: Built — copy delivered, launch not confirmed

what.text: A 'How it works' section that explains the offer in three numbered steps. It has a small eyebrow line ('Personalized sections, no coding'), a headline with the brand name in a logo/script style ('And this is how Sectionfy works'), and three side-by-side columns. Each column has a divider line with a green dot and a 'STEP 1/2/3' label, plus a rounded card with a short step title and a '+' icon that expands the card to show a longer description. In the example the steps are: 1) Buy a section, 2) Add it to Shopify, 3) Customize.

why.text: Breaking the purchase and onboarding process into three simple steps lowers perceived effort and uncertainty, especially for non-technical buyers. Phrases like 'no coding skills needed', 'saves developer costs' and 'start right away' address the main objections up front (complexity, cost, time). The accordions keep the section compact and scannable, and shoppers can open only the step they care about (progressive disclosure). The numbered sequence also gives a clear mental path from purchase to result.

how.text: Build a section with an eyebrow text, a heading (with an optional brand logo or script-font span) and 3 blocks. Each block has a step label, a title and a rich-text description. Lay the blocks out as a 3-column grid on desktop that stacks on mobile. Render each block as a collapsible card (a <details>/<summary> element or a small JS accordion) with a plus icon that turns into a minus when open. Draw the step label with a horizontal rule on both sides and an accent-colored dot. Use a dark background with light text and a green accent, as in the screenshot. Copy per step: STEP 1 – Buy a section: choose your preferred section (hero banner, product slider, testimonials), and it's yours in a few clicks. STEP 2 – Add it to Shopify: follow the clear step-by-step guide to add it yourself, with no coding skills, saving time and developer costs. STEP 3 – Customize: adjust colors, text, images and layout directly in the theme settings to fit your brand.

items: Step description (rich text) shown on expand
Default open/closed state of the accordions
Background and text color, accent (dot) color

dependencies.text: No apps or metafields are needed. It requires a theme that supports sections with blocks (Online Store 2.0) and a small amount of JS/CSS for the accordion. The brand wordmark needs to be supplied as an SVG or image, or set in a script font. The expanded-state design is not visible in the screenshot.

what.text: A horizontally scrolling carousel of product cards titled "Das wird dir auch gefallen" ("You'll also like this"). Each card shows a product image, a title, a short description, a 5-star rating with review count, the compare-at price struck through, the current price, and a green discount badge (e.g. -20%). The next card is partly visible at the right edge to signal that the row scrolls.

why.text: Showing a few relevant add-ons or alternatives at the decision point increases the chance of a second item and raises AOV. The eyebrow line ("8 out of 10 customers also use...") uses social proof and bandwagon effect to make the suggestion feel like a normal choice. Star ratings and review counts add credibility. The struck-through price and discount badge create a sense of deal value. The peeking card invites scrolling and discovery.

how.text: Build a carousel section in the theme using the native Shopify recommendations source. Curate each product's recommended products manually in the Shopify "Search & Discovery" app, with 3 relevant, product-specific picks per article as the initial brief. In comments, the developer advised linking at least 4 products per article so the cards fill the row with even spacing to the edge, and this was approved. Card content comes from standard product data: image, title, description, rating (review app or metafield), price, compare-at price and a computed discount badge. Add prev/next arrow buttons and let the last card peek in.

Rows and per-cell values (yes/no) should be editable in the theme editor. The brand column should be checked in every row, and the competitors should be filled in honestly. what.text: A 'How it works' section that explains the process in three numbered steps. It has a small uppercase eyebrow line, a large headline (here 'And this is how Sectionfy works', with the brand name as a green logo), and three side-by-side cards. Each card sits under a 'STEP 1/2/3' label with a green dot and thin horizontal lines on both sides. Each card has a bold title and a plus/minus toggle. Collapsed cards show only the title. why.text: Breaking the purchase and onboarding journey into three simple steps lowers perceived effort and complexity. Keep the body texts about the same length so expanded cards have equal heights. Per the feedback, make the eyebrow larger, regular-weight and higher-contrast on desktop, and make the step labels a bit larger. Mobile was approved as-is.
